    Changelog (Developer / Technical)¶

    Full technical detail for each release. Companion to CHANGELOG.md — same section structure, same entry numbering, same bold lead per entry, but the body keeps class names, file paths, audit IDs, error fingerprints, and failed-approaches notes that get trimmed from the user-facing log.

    Lift from commit-message bodies on each release; this file is a curated rollup, not new authoring.

    Legend: 🟢 confirmed working in-app  ·  🔴 added but not yet verified in-app

    [Unreleased]¶

    Unreleased entries live in CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED_DEV.md — this file is the released archive.

    [0.8.2] - 2026-09-04¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 auto_camera_visibility_trigger decides when the automation runs. EnumProperty (SWITCH_STILL "On Still Mode" / SWITCH "On Every Switch" / MANUAL "On Request", default SWITCH_STILL) in preferences/props/props_automations.py, drawn as the first row under the master toggle in draw_workflow.py (split label-and-field row, S11.2) and registered in both prefs_search.py registries. The whole decision is one pure function, core/cascade_camera_vis.applies_on_switch(trigger, is_still) -> bool, so the switch gate in cascade_apply.py (~L543, before _schedule_camera_visibility) and _on_camera_pref_changed cannot drift apart. is_still is a zero-arg callable consulted only for SWITCH_STILL -- it resolves the six-tier Still cascade and runs on the switch hot path -- and it reaches still_mode through the existing still_mode.resolve_still provider, never an upward import (ARCH-01). The read is legal inside depsgraph_update_post: Constitution rule 2 bans writes. An unknown enum value degrades to True, so a preference file from a newer build cannot silently switch the automation off. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 823 -> 825 (this enum + expand_hotkeys_cameras).
    2. 🟢 A no touches nothing, and no automatic path ever unhides. A draft answered a non-Still landing with a REVEAL, because hide_viewport / hide_render are GLOBAL object flags rather than per-take, so a Still take's hides otherwise persist onto every take after it. The user ruled it out and the reason is decisive: nothing is stamped, so reset_camera_visibility cannot tell its own work from a camera the user hid by hand -- an automatic reveal would switch that one back on behind them. Hides now stay until the user clears them, by hand or with Reset Camera Visibility, and a hand-made unhide equally survives until the next switch or request re-isolates (nothing polices the flags in between). reset_camera_visibility keeps its two DELIBERATE callers, the Reset button and the master toggle going off, and its docstring now says why no automatic path may call it. Telemetry carries why -- 'apply' / 'not_still' / 'manual' / 'off' -- get_camera_vis_telemetry() is a 4-tuple, and the profiler's Camera Visibility row names the setting that sent it away instead of a bare SKIPPED. _scene_cameras(scene) stays extracted and shared by the isolate and the reset paths, so neither pays the O(objects) walk the reset used to do alone.
    3. 🟢 tks.apply_camera_visibility + Shift+Alt+H + the row-menu entry. New operator beside TKS_OT_ResetCameraVisibility in operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py; all work in execute so a scripted caller gets what a click gets (Constitution rule 7), {'CANCELLED'} + a report when both sub-flags are off, and poll_message_set naming the reason when the master is off. Registered through the same five-file chain as its twin (ops_tree_design -> ops_settings -> context_popovers -> panels/context/_class_registry classes list). Bound on the Window keymap in the ADDON keyconfig only (ops_global_shortcuts.py) -- a user-kc bootstrap makes Blender drop the user's own bindings from that keymap on the next enable. Shift+Alt+H: H is Blender's hide family and this is a hide-and-show; the 5.2 factory keymap leaves the chord free in every 3D View mode (the Sequencer's sequencer.unmute outranks Window there, deliberately left winning); never Ctrl+Alt, which German AltGr sends. The row-menu entry sits under the mirrored toggle in tree_context_menu.py and greys with it, and Blender prints the live chord beside it -- which is what makes the key discoverable. New "Cameras" group in HOTKEY_SECTIONS, its expand_hotkeys_cameras flag, and its membership in ACCORDION_GROUPS so the fold gestures reach it.

    Naming note: the parked verb is intent, never action. In this add-on action means a bpy.types.Action, and the auditor's CRASH-08 reads a parameter of that name as a live RNA element -- parking one in a module-level dict is exactly the heap-corruption class that rule catches. The first draft used action and the scan flagged the one line whose whole purpose is to store names only; the word changed rather than being silenced with a sentinel.

    Tests: dev/tests/test_camera_vis_trigger.py (8, pure -- the three triggers, that MANUAL and SWITCH never resolve the Still cascade, and the unknown-value fallback) and dev/tests/test_camera_vis_apply_op.py (20, headless -- the enum's identifiers and default, the counts, reveal clearing all three flags, the operator's poll/execute/cancel paths, the single addon-kc keymap item matched on identity fields only, the pref callback under each trigger, what the switch gate parks, and the telemetry intent). Auditor after the rename: quality 9.4, identical to main on every rule, retained elements back to 0. 4. 🟢 Apply When is reachable from the tree row menu, and the camera block ends where it stops being about cameras. New TKS_MT_CameraVisibilityMode in panels/context/menus.py, registered through panels/context/_class_registry.py like its siblings, drawn by _list_settings as mode.menu(...) directly under tks.apply_camera_visibility, followed by the layout.separator() that closes the block before Previews and Tree Design. A SUBMENU rather than the house popover: this opens from inside a menu, and a menu cannot open a popover panel — the same constraint that makes Previews and Tree Design invoke_popup operators. Its three rows are layout.prop_enum, so Blender draws the radio dot on the value in force and writes the preference itself; the row menu therefore cannot drift from what Preferences shows, and the choice needs no operator (nothing new for MAINT-13 to reach). The submenu greys via mode.enabled on its own row because a Menu carries no poll; the operator above is deliberately NOT wrapped with it, since Blender prints the shortcut only for an entry drawn straight onto the menu. Icon TIME (already used by the render-jobs popover, so no icon-literal drift). Tests: 5 more in test_camera_vis_apply_op.py — registration, that the draw names all three identifiers through prop_enum, submenu-after-operator order, the separator between the submenu and Previews, and that the greying row wraps only the submenu. Suite: 179 passed across camera / row-menu / i18n / shortcut / registration.

    Naming pass on the user's ruling, same day. The setting is Apply When, not Apply On and not Apply Mode: Mode is a taken word here (Rest Mode, Still Mode, Diff State are things you switch ON, so Apply Mode reads as a mode called Apply), and When is what the three entries actually answer. One label serves the Preferences row and the submenu, so the control has one name in both places. The row menu's button says Isolate - the toggle above it already says WHICH visibility, so the row can name what the click GIVES rather than which machinery ran, and it is the word the profiler already reports and Blender's own word for show-this-hide-the-rest. The operator keeps bl_label = "Apply Camera Visibility" for the two surfaces with no heading over them, the Hotkeys page and Blender's operator search, and a test pins both halves. Isolate is exact only while both sub-flags are on (the default); with Hide Other Cameras off the click merely unhides the assigned camera, so the tooltip now names that dependency instead of the label carrying it.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 features/sequencer/mode.py (new) resolves a tri-state from the two switches that already existed - WindowManager.tks_timeline_sync (session) and TKS_AddonPreferences.sequencer_scene_autoswitch (saved). No new property: the mode is derived, and set_mode() always writes the PAIR, so "both on" stops being representable. TKS_OT_TimelineModeToggle is the single seam - popover rows, the Mode pie and a scripted bpy.ops.tks.timeline_mode_toggle(value=...) all land in the same execute(). An empty value reaching execute() reports and returns {'CANCELLED'} rather than {'FINISHED'} (AI-01). value='FRAME' while resolve_still() is true is refused with a real message, replacing the old behaviour where the whole button greyed out.
    2. 🟢 features/sequencer/popover.py (new) holds TKS_MT_TimelineModes (a Menu) and TKS_PT_TimelineAdvanced (a Panel, 'PROPERTIES'/'HEADER' + {'INSTANCED'}, so one panel serves the VIEW_3D N-Panel and the SEQUENCE_EDITOR sidebar). Two kinds on purpose: a menu shuts on the first click, which is right for picking a mode and wrong for a stack of toggles. The nav control had to go back to layout.operator because UILayout.popover() never sees a modifier key - which also restored depress, so the button highlights like the other six modes again. invoke() reads event.shift and calls wm.call_panel(keep_open=event.shift): the modes close on the pick, the settings stay open. Shape copied from TKS_OT_StillPopover.invoke. Only the Frame Sync ROW carries frame_sync_available(); gating the popover or the button would lock Scene Follow behind a Still take it has nothing to do with. sequencer_scene_autoswitch is deliberately NOT drawn - it IS the FOLLOW mode. sequencer_follow_enabled is deliberately NOT gated - a strip applies its own take while scrubbing in every mode.
    3. 🟢 features/sequencer/panel.py lost the inline mirror (old :57-79) and draws the same operator button. panels/navigation/panel.py replaced the tks_timeline_sync checkbox and dropped the now-unused _active_still block; panels/mode_toggles.py dropped its _active_still helper, split TIMELINE_SYNC into three entries and APPENDED TIMELINE_FOLLOW / TIMELINE_OFF to MODE_KEYS and MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS (stored slot values - TIMELINE_SYNC keeps its id and now means Frame Sync). Tests in dev/tests/test_timeline_mode.py.
    4. 🟢 Confirmed by probe rather than by eye: the overlay draws with the GPU, so a headless run cannot prove pixels - it proves the step before, that both keys reach collect_modes() when their mode is on and leave when it is off (dev/temp/probe_mode_badges.py, PASS). panels/process_overlay.py had five ModeCandidate rows for the header's seven modes. Added scene_follow and diff_state, with overlay_mode_scene_follow / overlay_mode_diff_state in OverlayPropsMixin (EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 823 -> 825) and their icon toggles in preferences/draw_interface.py, in nav-header order. The timeline pill now reads the mode from features/sequencer/mode.current_mode() instead of wm.tks_timeline_sync directly, so pill, button and pie share one resolver; its label follows (Timeline Sync -> Frame Sync); the icon stays NLA. The chooser is TKS_MT_TimelineModes, a Menu and not a panel, opened with wm.call_menu - TKS_MT_StillGlobal line for line: acting states, separator, Off, and the menu's own bl_label as the title. Only the settings half stays an INSTANCED popover (wm.call_panel(keep_open=True)), because only it has to survive a click. Frame Sync and Off both keep NLA, the icon the old checkbox always carried - Frame Sync IS that feature; only Scene Follow needed a new glyph (SEQUENCE).
    5. 🟢 sequencer_autoswitch_on and sequencer_autoswitch_back_on were ENUM_FLAG properties, and Blender can only paint a flag enum as a row of toggle buttons - five of them were wider than the preferences column, so "Playhead" and "Arrows" clipped to "Play..." and "Arro...". They are seven BoolProperty rungs now (EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 825 -> 830), drawn by one ui/styles.draw_bool_grid in BOTH preferences/draw_workflow.py and features/sequencer/popover.py. The rung table lives in utils/constants.py (SEQ_SWITCH_RUNGS / SEQ_BACK_RUNGS) because three layers read it and none may import the others sideways: the feature tests a trigger against it, the preferences draw from it, and _migrate_config_dict maps the old flags through it. Saved flag sets migrate rung by rung, a present new key always winning, and the two old keys drain via _LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS - so nobody loses a trigger they had switched off. The flag identifiers are unchanged, so every keymap item, operator property and log line still says HOVER / CLICK / PLAY / SCRUB / ARROWS; engine.switch_triggers() / back_triggers() hand the consumers the same set they read before. Both hosts also rule the three groups apart with separator(type='LINE') - the way out, the way back, and what a strip does are different questions, and an unbroken stack of checkboxes read as one long list of unrelated ticks.

    6. 🟢 Every mode that offers a way out draws it with QUIT (user ruling 2026-09-03): the Still dropdown's "Off (per-take)" (features/still_mode/ menus.py), the Timeline menu's Off row (features/sequencer/mode. MODE_OFF_ICON), both pie entries (panels/mode_toggles.py) and both slot items (MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS). They had worn PREVIEW_RANGE in some places and NLA in others, so the same act looked different depending on where it was offered. Deliberately NOT changed: each button's RESTING glyph - Still's PREVIEW_RANGE and Timeline's NLA - which reports the state "nothing on" rather than the act of leaving. QUIT verified present in Blender 5.2's icon enum before use.

    7. 🟢 The chooser. features/diff_state/properties.py registers two new session bools - WindowManager.tks_diff_state_drift and .tks_diff_state_keyed, both default=True, both update=_on_toggle - and turns the original tks_diff_state into a DERIVED summary (get= any, set= writes both). Same shape as features/sequencer/mode.py: "off" is not a third flag, it is both marks off, so "on but drawing nothing" is not representable. Nothing is stored, so no migration and no .blend change, and every existing reader keeps its meaning - the header depress (panels/navigation/panel.py), the viewport pill (panels/process_overlay.py), the DIFF_STATE pie entry, and a scripted wm.tks_diff_state = True. The master carries no update=: its setter writes through RNA, so each mark's own callback fires the redraw. unregister() drops the summary FIRST - a getter reading properties already released would raise during teardown. features/diff_state/menus.py (new) holds TKS_MT_DiffStateModes, a Menu with the MODES/MODE_LABEL/MODE_ICON/MODE_OFF_ICON table features/sequencer/mode.py uses, and bl_label as the title. It shipped for one commit as an INSTANCED popover PANEL holding two independent toggles, and both halves of that were overruled the same day (user, with a screenshot of TKS_MT_TimelineModes). Behaviour: the four choices are EXCLUSIVE - one four-way mode, not two ticks. Look: a panel CENTRES its row text with the icon stranded at the left edge, because layout.prop(toggle=True) and layout.operator() both centre, and no alignment trick keeps a full-width highlight while moving the label left. Only a Menu draws left-aligned menu rows. The two rulings agree - an exclusive choice belongs in a widget that shuts on the pick, and that widget is the one that draws the rows right. features/diff_state/logic.py carries the resolver, "derived, not stored" again: MODE_DRIFT/KEYED/ALL/OFF, resolve_mode(show_drift, show_keyed) and its inverse mode_pair(mode). The four choices ARE the four states of the pair, so no combination falls outside the chooser and leaves it showing nothing as live; an unknown mode reads as OFF rather than inventing a fifth behaviour. TKS_OT_ToggleDiffState gained 'NONE' (unset sentinel, now the default, SKIP_SAVE), 'DRIFT' and 'KEYED' enum items, and an invoke() that opens the menu ONLY while the state is still 'NONE'. 'DRIFT'/'KEYED' SET rather than toggle: each writes the whole pair through logic.mode_pair(), so the other stands down and picking the live choice twice is idempotent - Off is its own row. 'ON' is what All calls; every identifier is frozen, so no stored keymap or script moves. execute() reads 'NONE' as TOGGLE, so a bare bpy.ops.tks.toggle_diff_state() keeps its old meaning (AI-01: no work moved into invoke(), and bpy.ops defaults to EXEC_DEFAULT, so a script never reaches it). The wm.call_menu call carries an AI-02-OK sentinel: the menu's rows call this same operator with an explicit state, which is the very seam a script uses. _STATE_ITEMS stays module-level (CRASH-07). logic.visible_states(states, show_keyed, show_drift) is applied in draw.py _draw() per object AFTER marked_objects(). Filtering after the scan is deliberate: the drift scan is cached against the depsgraph and the frame, and a switch flip changes what is DRAWN, not what an object IS - filtering inside the scan would throw away a cache whose answer did not change. Dropping a state also hands the survivor its full mark set, because split_marks() only lets drift claim a keyed mark while drift is present.

    8. 🟢 features/diff_state/panel.py (the Diff State subpanel inside Blender's own Overlays popover) KEPT its tks_diff_state checkbox and gained, indented beneath it via ui.styles.indent with .active gated on the summary, one layout.menu("TKS_MT_DiffStateModes") row naming the live choice. Replacing the master with the choices - the original plan - would have put three controls at one left edge reading as three equals; the master is not one of the marks. It briefly held two checkboxes instead, which once the choices became exclusive was a second and differently-behaving way to say the same thing: one control, so one widget, in both of its homes.

    9. 🟢 panels/mode_toggles.py MODE_KEYS and preferences/addon_prefs_constants.py MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS gained DIFF_DRIFT/DIFF_KEYED/DIFF_ALL/DIFF_OFF, APPENDED (values 12-15) - stored slots must never change what they point at, so DIFF_STATE keeps its id and its meaning (flip the whole mode). Four slots rather than a chained popover: a pie slice must not open one. Labels match mode_toggles verbatim; test_mode_pie.py holds the two tables together.

    10. 🔴 MAINT-14. TKS_OT_RenderJobsPopover (features/batch_render/ jobs_popover.py) never named Shift+F12. Blender writes its Shortcut: line for MENU entries only, and only for the operator the key is bound to; this one is reached from the render-scope pie's slot dispatcher and from panel buttons, so Blender printed nothing. It grew a description() classmethod composing OP_RENDERJOBSPOPOVER with the new OP_RENDERJOBSPOPOVER_KEYS through compose_tooltip, the chord read LIVE off the keyconfig via live_shortcut() so a rebind moves it and the reader's hide-shortcuts preference still takes the line away. Same route as the tree's delete button (operators/inspector/ops_slots.py). Its bl_description was then DROPPED: Blender always calls description() when a class defines one, so the line became unreachable text - test_no_new_shadowed_constant caught it at 46 against a baseline of 45, and the count is back to 45.

    11. 🔴 INFO-18, both strings. "Missing filename" -> "Missing File Name" (jobs_popover.py) and PANEL_TIMELINE_ADVANCED "Timeline Options" -> "Timeline Settings" (texts/tooltips_sequencer.py). Both German keys moved in the same commit; the i18n drift guard fails otherwise.
    12. 🔴 INFO-09, both gaps. TKS_MT_DiffStateModes and TKS_MT_TimelineModes carried no bl_description, and Blender promotes a Menu's class docstring to its hover tooltip exactly as it does an Operator's - so two user-facing strings lived in code files. Each now names a constant (MENU_DIFF_STATE_MODES, MENU_TIMELINE_MODES). Worth remembering: this looked like a rule false positive until the rule's own docstring was read, which states the Menu case deliberately.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 _redraw_everything() in preferences/props/props_language.py read bpy.data.window_managers unguarded. Restoring saved preferences at startup fires the update= callback on every ticked TKS_JargonTermItem.use_english row, and at that point bpy.data is Blender's _RestrictData stand-in with no ID collections on it: AttributeError: '_RestrictData' object has no attribute 'window_managers', one printed traceback per ticked term on every Blender start. Harmless in effect - apply_vocabulary() calls i18n.register_translations() first inside its own try, so the vocabulary was installed correctly, and nothing is painted that early anyway - but it put a traceback in front of every user. Fixed with the repo's existing early-out idiom (getattr(bpy.data, "window_managers", None)), the same guard features/sync/handlers_viewport.py already uses against pref-load. Routing through signal_redraw() was rejected: it walks window_managers[0] and filters by _REDRAW_AREA_TYPES, so it cannot repaint the Preferences window this callback runs in. Regression test test_the_redraw_survives_blenders_restricted_startup_data in dev/tests/test_prefs_language_page.py. Full record in doc/troubleshooting/language_redraw_restricted_startup_data.md.

    2. 🟢 The sandbox fixture in dev/tests/test_changelog_split.py copied the repo's real CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED{,_DEV}.md into its tmp dir. A release cut empties that pair by design, and release_cut.cut() refuses an empty pair - so the three tests that need a SUCCESSFUL cut (test_a_cut_moves_every_entry_and_empties_the_working_pair, test_a_cut_refuses_a_version_that_already_shipped, test_a_cut_restamps_the_lock_so_the_new_block_is_frozen_too) went red the moment 0.8.1 was cut, on release timing rather than on anything they cover, and would have gone green again on their own once the next entry was written. The fixture now SEEDS its own three-entry mirror pair (SEEDS) and copies only the two archives, which the freeze tests genuinely need for the shipped 0.8.0 and 0.7.11 blocks. Verified with all four sandbox tests against a fresh seed each, plus 971/3152 impact-selected.

    3. 🟢 42 accordions were missing from ACCORDION_GROUPS, so solo mode and Shift+Click did nothing on them. TKS_OT_ToggleAccordion.invoke resolves a clicked section's siblings with group = next((g for g in ACCORDION_GROUPS if self.target in g), (self.target,)), and _accordion_new_states iterates group in BOTH modifier branches - the shift fan-out and the solo and new_state exclusive. The fallback is a group of ONE, so an unlisted section has no siblings: solo closes nothing, Shift folds nothing, and both degrade into an ordinary click with no error and no log. The contract spans two files that share no import (preferences/props/props_*.py declares the toggle, preferences/addon_prefs_constants.py lists it), which is why it drifted.

    ACCORDION_GROUPS 111 -> 145 names, 24 -> 32 groups, no name in two groups. Three whole pages had no row at all and got one: Interface > Tooltips (2), Interface > Language - split into the three top-level sections and a nested pair for the word-list groups drawn inside Terms, matching the keyframe-pie precedent - and Interface > Diff State (6: a marks table and a look block per state plus the two shared sections, all drawn into the one box). Four newcomers joined existing groups: expand_auto_inspector (Workflow > Automations), expand_storage_snapshots (Data > Storage), expand_presets_defaults (Data > Presets). The Configuration Inspector gained four new groups, one per tab, for the sub-category rows draw_data_inspector.draw_tab_group builds as f"{tab_prop}_{sub_name.lower()}" - grouped per TAB on purpose, so Shift+Click folds one tab's categories rather than the whole inspector.

    Eight props are deliberately NOT grouped and now say so with # CORR-25-OK: <reason>: expand_inspector_main (master toggle - folding one tab must not fold the tree, which addon_prefs_constants.py already stated in prose), and seven that draw nothing at all - expand_inspector_features{,_automations}, expand_inspector_naming{,_templates,_tokens} (naming lives under the Workflow tab today), expand_inspector_ui_general (the UI tab has no General sub-category) and expand_inspector_legend (a dismissable tip box, not an accordion). All seven are leftovers of an older inspector layout, referenced only by utils/manual_map.py anchors and preferences/persistence_io.py; they are left declared rather than removed, because deleting registered preference properties is a separate decision. The three naming sentinels are written one per line: the shared radius is 3 lines and a single block comment above all three would not reach the last.

    Found by the auditor's new CORR-25 Accordion Group Coverage check (blender-addon-auditor, commit b800690), which is what makes this non-recurring - a future section left out of the table is now a scored finding rather than a silent dead toggle. Rescan of this branch: unlisted 42 -> 0, accordions_listed 111 -> 145, exempt 8, solitary 0, stale_entries 0; Takes' Code Quality 8.4 -> 9.4 with nothing left saturated. Data-only change (one constant table plus comments): no imports moved, no registration touched. 4. 🔴 One key standard for all nine fold arrows. Each expand/collapse arrow had its own invoke and each author added the modifier they needed that day, so the vocabulary drifted: tks.toggle_scene_expand and tks.vsw_tree_toggle answered Shift, Ctrl and Ctrl+Shift / Shift+Alt, while tks.toggle_accordion, tks.custom_token_toggle_category, tks.pm_toggle_group_expand, tks.preload_toggle_section, tks.profiler_toggle_group, tks.tag_group_toggle_expand and tks.tagtree_toggle_expand answered Shift alone and silently swallowed the rest. A chord learned on one arrow did nothing on the next - no error, so it read as a broken key rather than an absent one. Found by the auditor's CORR-26 check (blender-addon-auditor 152ee9c), 7 of 9 out of step.

    The vocabulary now lives in ONE place, utils/fold_gestures.py: fold_scope(event) returns a FoldScope (SELF / CHILDREN / LEVEL / ALL) and FoldScope.resolve(has_children, has_levels) narrows it to what a surface can actually offer. The two-key chords are tested BEFORE the single ones - a bare event.shift check first would swallow Ctrl+Shift before it was ever seen. Both spellings of ALL are kept because the All-Takes tree has accepted them interchangeably since the 2026-08 ruling; the tree that set the standard was refactored onto the shared helper too, so there is no second definition left to drift.

    resolve() is what makes a flat surface honest. Custom-token categories, process-monitor groups, preload sections, profiler groups and tag groups have one level and no nesting, so ALL folds down to LEVEL and CHILDREN down to SELF: every chord is answered with the widest thing that surface has instead of being ignored. Only two surfaces carry real structure - Preferences (a new ACCORDION_NESTED map, 9 parents / 40 children, alongside ACCORDION_ALL flattened once from ACCORDION_GROUPS so a held chord does not re-walk 32 groups per keystroke) and the Tag Library tree, where Ctrl now carries a category's state into its groups and Ctrl+Shift carries it into every group of every category (new hidden with_groups property).

    _accordion_new_states takes a scope instead of a shift bool, plus nested= and universe=. Ctrl deliberately ignores solo mode: the reader asked for a branch, not for exclusivity. Both tag operators moved off a bare bl_description onto compose_tooltip + a _KEYS block, like every other fold arrow, so the shortcut lines drop with the same preference.

    Tooltips updated for all seven; texts/locales/de_DE.py re-keyed in lockstep (5 reworded sources, 2 new entries) - the drift guard fails on any entry whose source no longer exists, so this is not optional. ACCORDION_NESTED was validated against ACCORDION_GROUPS: every child is a known accordion, no child appears twice, and the only parent outside the groups is expand_inspector_main, which is the CORR-25-OK master by design.

    Two existing guards had to be satisfied, and both were right. test_no_tooltip_promises_a_gesture_it_lacks went red because _delegate_pool was file-local: moving the reads into a shared module made nine tooltips look like liars. Its one hardcoded shared module (operators/cascade/_helpers.py) became _SHARED_DELEGATE_MODULES with utils/fold_gestures.py beside it, so a third shared helper needs no edit. Then test_no_new_silent_gesture went red on five FLAT surfaces: they now read event.ctrl through fold_scope while their tooltips named no Ctrl gesture. That is a real gap - a reader who learned Ctrl on the tree tries it here and is told nothing - so each gained {ctrl_click}: an ordinary click - nothing is nested here. The first draft of both extra lines said "the same" without saying the same as WHAT, which under a Shift line reads as "same as Shift"; reworded so each line stands alone (the same as {shift_click} - one level is all there is).

    dev/tests/test_accordion_mode.py rewritten, 7 tests -> 19, covering each scope, the two spellings, the chord ORDER, that Alt alone is not a fold gesture, and that a flat surface answers everything. Rescan: CORR-26 out_of_step 7 -> 0, all nine toggles reading alt, ctrl, shift; CORR-25 still 0; Code Quality 8.7 -> 9.4. Full suite 3165 passed, 1 skipped. Full record in doc/troubleshooting/fold_gesture_standard.md.

    1. 🟢 Scene Auto-Switch triggers: one squeezed row -> a two-column grid. sequencer_autoswitch_on is a five-rung ENUM_FLAG and both call sites drew it into a row(align=True). In a preferences column that is far too narrow for five rungs, so Blender clipped the last two to Play... and Arro... - a control the reader cannot read. New _draw_flag_grid in preferences/draw_workflow.py wraps them with grid_flow(row_major=True, columns=2, even_columns=True, even_rows=False, align=True), the shape of Blender's own Overlay > Objects block the user pointed at. even_rows=False keeps a short last row from padding out.

    Not search_prop. It wraps its prop in a row(align=True) of its own, and a row inside a grid cell puts every rung straight back on one line. The helper applies the same dimming (active from the search flags) to the grid itself, plus the enabled gate from the master toggle above it.

    sequencer_autoswitch_back_on gets the same call for consistency; with two rungs the grid renders as it did before.

    The rungs stay ONE flag property, so nothing about saved preferences changes - the alternative (five BoolProperties, which is what real checkboxes would need) would have reset every existing choice. Layout-only diff: no audit, no tests (python -m py_compile only, per the house rule - no rule scores pixel positions).

    1. 🟢 Interface > Overlay was split across two accordion groups, so Shift+Click folded four of its ten sections. Reported from the app: Placement, Appearance, Progress Bars and Mode Badges opened; Keyed Slot Marks, Keyed Slot Look, Drifted Marks, Drifted Look, When Both Apply and Diff State Switch stayed shut.

    My error in entry 3, not a new defect. The Diff State block carries its own comment header and sits under a draw_category_gap, so it READS like its own page - and I grouped it as one. It is not: draw_interface.py draws all ten into the same box inside elif self.active_subtab_ui == 'OVERLAY', four directly and four more through _draw_diff_state_block(self, box, ...). The two groups are now one group of ten.

    Why CORR-25 reported zero. The rule asks "is every accordion listed in SOME group?" - all ten were, so the answer was honestly zero. It never asks "is it listed with the sections it is actually drawn beside?" That is a different question and the rule does not model it. A probe that clusters draw_collapsible_section calls by the layout they draw INTO and diffs each cluster against ACCORDION_GROUPS finds exactly this one mismatch and 13 clean clusters across the addon, so the check is tractable - see the auditor's doc/roadmap/ideas/ follow-up.

    1. 🔴 Icon Sheet gets a default chord: Ctrl+Shift+Alt+I. It shipped as keymap_items.new('tks.view_icon_sheet', 'NONE', 'PRESS') - registered in the addon keyconfig, Window/EMPTY so it works anywhere, but with no key, so the feature was unreachable unless the reader bound it by hand.

    Every other chord on the I key is taken. Read out of Blender's shipped keymap_data/blender_default.py, not from memory: plain I inserts a keyframe (15 bindings), Alt+I deletes one (7), Shift+I is blank-frame / add-IK (6), Ctrl+I is font style + mask fill (2), Alt+Shift+I clears keyframes (1), and Ctrl+Alt+I is pose.ik_clear in the POSE keymap - the one mode this addon's readers spend the day in, so that near-miss was rejected rather than shipped as a mode-specific dead spot. Only Ctrl+Shift+I and Ctrl+Shift+Alt+I are free. The user was offered both and chose the four-key one.

    German-layout note: AltGr arrives as Ctrl+Alt on Windows, so this is the same event as AltGr+Shift+I. AltGr+I types no character on that layout, so it cannot fire while writing.

    Still only a DEFAULT - Data -> Debug already draws a rebind row (draw_debug.py), and the operator's description() reads the key live via live_shortcut, so a rebind shows up in the tooltip with no code change.

    1. 🟢 Three Process Monitor rows sat under no group header. Reported from the app: Diff State Geometry Watch, Diff State Load Reset and Still Frame Lock rendered loose at the bottom of the tree while seven groups sat above them. TWO different causes behind one symptom.

    Cause 1 - no group asked for. The two Diff State handlers called register_process(name, HANDLER, UI_SYNC, "features.diff_state.cache"). The third positional is category (CORE / UI_SYNC / RENDER / REST), NOT feature_group - a separate keyword they never passed. They now pass feature_group="diff_state".

    Cause 2 - a group that was never registered. Still Frame Lock DID pass feature_group="still_mode", and register_process dropped it on the floor: if feature_group and feature_group in _feature_groups fell through in silence when the name was unknown. No group named still_mode existed. It now warns (level='WARNING', topic="SYSTEM", subtopic="monitor") naming the process and the missing id, so the next one says so instead of hiding.

    Why still_mode was missing: the list was written down twice. The eight register_feature_group(...) calls were typed out verbatim in BOTH takes_for_blender/__init__.py and takes_for_blender/features/__init__.py, so adding a feature meant remembering two files and nothing failed when you did not. Now one DEFAULT_FEATURE_GROUPS tuple in utils/process_monitor.py plus an idempotent register_default_feature_groups(), called from both entry points - idempotent on purpose, so neither caller has to know which runs first.

    Two groups added: still_mode -> "Still Mode" / ONIONSKIN_OFF and diff_state -> "Diff State" / SHADING_BBOX. Labels and icons copied from the mode toggles in panels/mode_toggles.py, so the same feature reads the same way in the monitor and on the badge row. Both labels were already in de_DE.py from the toggles, so no re-key was needed (checked, 0 missing).

    The de-duplication silently untranslated two labels, and the i18n guard caught it the same run. i18n_extract reads a group label from the CALL (_POSITIONAL_TEXT_CALLS = {"register_feature_group": (1,)}), so folding the eight calls into a tuple took "Core" and "UI Sync" out of the catalog and test_no_orphan_translations went red on their now-sourceless German entries. The other six survived only because the mode toggles spell them out too. Fixed at the harvester, not by putting the duplication back: new _TEXT_TABLE_CONSTANTS = {"DEFAULT_FEATURE_GROUPS": (1,)} plus _add_table_rows, the same shape it already uses for an enum items= table - slot 0 is a stable id and slot 2 an icon name, so neither is harvested. Verified: all ten labels in the catalog, zero ids or icons leaked. test_catalog_collects_display_text_tables in dev/tests/test_i18n_guard.py pins both halves.

    dev/tests/test_pm_feature_groups.py - 5 tests, pytest.mark.pure (AST only, no bpy): every register_process names a group that exists, every one names a group AT ALL, the three reported rows are pinned by name, the group list is spelled out in exactly one file, and ids/labels are unique. The second test is the one that would have caught the Diff State half on the day it was written. 9. 🔴 CORR-01, the only finding on that board deducting score. jobs_popover._unregister_keymap() removes its keymap item without the # CORR-01-OK: addon-kc teardown on full unregister sentinel that every other teardown site in the addon already carries (sequencer/keymap.py, smart_syntax/icon_picker.py, variant_switch/ops_crud.py, ops_global_shortcuts.py, ops_smart_undo.py, tags/ops_groups.py, panels/context/__init__.py, pie_menus/keyframe_keymap.py). The pattern was always correct - _register_keymap() binds in the ADDON keyconfig only, as its own docstring says - so this is a missing comment, not a missing guard. 10. 🔴 MAINT-09. core/cascade_apply.py imported query from .providers inside two separate functions (lines 541 and 886). providers.py is a LEAF - no module-level imports of its own - so there was never a cycle to defer around; hoisted to module level. The second site KEEPS its except ImportError: with the import gone that guard now covers the REGISTERED provider, which is feature code and may fail to import its own dependencies. 11. 🔴 The Shift+F12 binding was invisible to the wiki manifest. features/batch_render/jobs_popover.py bound it as km.keymap_items.new(TKS_OT_RenderJobsPopover.bl_idname, *_HOTKEY, shift=True). Both arguments read as None to an AST, so dev/build/manifest_extractor.py dropped the binding rather than write a half-known entry - correct on its own terms, but the consequence reached the reader: no row in ui_manifest.json, so the wiki's {{ keys(...) }} macro could not resolve it AND verify_wiki.py rejected a hand-written ++shift+f12++ as drift. The shortcut was undocumentable, which is how it came to be missing from the Hotkeys page at all. Spelled out now, the way every other binding in the addon already is; _HOTKEY is DELETED rather than kept beside it, because _find_kmi() matches by operator id alone and that tuple had exactly one reader. Three tests in dev/tests/test_manifest_extractor.py (the file that exists for extraction rules that have bitten us): a spelled-out call is harvested, an indirect one is skipped with the reason recorded, and the real binding reaches the manifest as F12 + shift. No runtime behaviour changes - the same chord is bound in the same keymap. 12. 🔴 NAME-05: tks.preview_settings lived outside its feature. The preview code's homes are features/vl_preview/, features/batch_render/ops_utils and preferences/ops_addon_ui, but TKS_OT_PreviewSettings sat in operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py - while utils/manual_map.py had already been pointing readers at features/vl_preview/ for it, so map and code disagreed. It belongs there on the merits too: every property it draws (tks_show_preview, tks_preview_size, tks_preview_bg_color, tks_preview_bg_transparent) is registered by that package, and it imported nothing from the module it left. It was also named in THREE classes lists - ops_settings.py, panels/context/_class_registry.py and panels/context_popovers.py - of which only _class_registry's is reachable from register(); the other two are legacy lists nothing iterates (panels/__init__.py has no registration code at all, despite the comment above one of them). Registering from two live lists is REG-01's third check, so the shape was one reachability change away from a real finding. All three entries are gone; features/vl_preview/operators.py defines AND registers it alone. Nothing referenced the class by symbol - the row menu draws it by idname - so the move is invisible at runtime.     [0.8.1] - 2026-09-03¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Internal: two-lane depsgraph stress harness (dev/stress/) + CRASH-09 baseline gate. Seeded, replayable work sessions against the six depsgraph_update_post handlers. Headless lane A (synthetic depsgraph, 24-cell matrix) and lane B (real operators, real evaluation — --background has a real VIEW_3D; global undo does NOT exist there, so the undo family is GUI-only by construction); GUI lane with two windows, one step per timer tick, a crash-safe fsynced JSONL journal whose last BEGIN names the killer step, --repeat for intermittence, ddmin shrink, --disable-handlers (Process Monitor) for per-handler bisect, and a wrapper that detects a dead/stalled Blender in seconds and never leaves a window open. TKS_STRESS_SKIP env gates (inert unless set) in core/vl_switch.py, core/vl_switch_fast.py, core/cascade.py enable phase-level bisecting. dev/tests/test_crash09_handler_mutation.py gates the auditor's new CRASH-09 rule (Handler Mutation Ban) at the current 9-site baseline in apply_vl_switch_unified — a tenth in-tick animation write, or one in a new file, fails CI. 63+ harness tests; full suite green. Commits 62d00b21..a0b8dce8.

    2. 🟢 get_variants(tier, …) — the read half of switch_variant. Card facade-missing-verbs. The survey learned the live choice by calling switch_variant and reading changed: False — a read implemented as a write. Same addressing as the write verb (_VARIANT_TIERS → get_cascade_target), parses target.tks_vsw_cascade via parse_multi_cascade, answers every product with its live variant name or None (unset = the next tier up wins); assignments for products that no longer exist surface as a warning, not a row. Read-only: no session, no undo. AI_GUIDE.md variants section updated. Tests in dev/tests/test_ai_missing_verbs.py (read-what-was-written, unset→None, read-only pin, unknown-tier refusal). Verified 2026-08-31 by an automated probe (dev/temp/verify_ai_ready.py) driving the facade in a live Blender 5.2 session: a probe product switched at the SCENE tier reads back as its live variant, the unconfirmed delete_preset refuses with NEEDS_CONFIRM and the confirmed one removes the file, and describe() lists a freshly linked camera. Headless needs vl_lifecycle._deferred_load_apply() run by hand first or every mutating verb refuses BUSY. Entries 2–4 flipped together on that run, plus 34 targeted facade tests green.

    3. 🟢 delete_preset(kind, key, tier=None, confirm=False) — the undo for a mistyped create_preset. create_preset rightly refuses to overwrite, which made a wrong name permanent (the survey's probe preset needed filesystem surgery). Wraps serialization.delete_preset with: kind/key validation (candidates in the hint, same shapes as apply_preset), an ambiguity refusal when the key exists in several tiers and tier was not given (deleting the copy the user did not mean is a silent loss), and the delete_take-style NEEDS_CONFIRM dry run carrying a {kind, key, name, tier} preview. No undo label — deleting a FILE is permanent, and claiming a step would lie about recoverability (the cancel_render precedent). Added to _MUTATING_VERBS. Tests: dry-run leaves the file listed, confirm removes it, missing-key and unknown-kind refusals.

    4. 🟢 describe() now carries cameras (+ count). Assigning a camera is a first-class facade move, but the orientation call named none — the survey read bpy.data.objects raw, the exact detour the facade exists to prevent. New _camera_names() (sorted camera-object names) is the single source for BOTH describe() and _SETTABLE["camera"]'s validator, so describe can never advertise a name set_override refuses — pinned by test_describe_cameras_match_what_set_override_accepts.

    5. 🟢 UI vocabulary standard — §13 of doc/standards/naming_conventions.md + doc/standards/ui_vocabulary.json. Card ui-vocabulary-standard. Origin ruling: the follow-selection work shipped a preference reading Follow Selection, a button beside it reading Find Action/Slot, and that button's tooltip saying "follow the watchlist selection" — three phrasings, one feature. §1–§12 govern IDENTIFIERS; nothing governed the words a reader sees, so §13 is an EXTENSION of the same standard, not a rival document. Scope is labels only — bl_label, bl_description, *Property(name=/description=), enum item labels, section titles, texts/ constants. Explicitly OUT of scope forever: property identifiers, bl_idname, enum item ids, RNA paths, all frozen as wiki keys by §7.1.

    6. 🟢 Inspector Actions/Slots lists follow the watchlist selection. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-29.) The jump logic moved out of TKS_OT_FindActionSlot.execute into module-level jump_to_action_slot(context, action_name, slot_name, target_id_type='') (operators/inspector/ops_find_action.py), because the follow runs from a property update= callback, which cannot invoke an INTERNAL operator; execute() now delegates to it and keeps only the reporting, so button and follow cannot drift. Hook: panels/inspector/cache._on_objects_index_changed — the existing update= on WindowManager.tks_inspector_objects_index, which already pushed selection list->viewport; the follow rides INSIDE its _syncing_objects_list re-entrancy guard so list writes cannot bounce back. NOT a depsgraph handler, so no CRASH-09 deferral needed (the one indirect route, sync_viewport setting the index from depsgraph_update_post, writes only UI props). New _row_id_block resolves object rows AND the synthetic __tks_scene__: / __tks_world__: watchlist rows, so Scene and World reach their actions through the same route as any object. Guard: returns early on TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating — a take/VL switch drives selection itself and would fight the user for the lists. State: session wm.tks_follow_selection (BoolProperty, agent-settable per Constitution 7) seeded from new pref inspector_follow_selection by cache.seed_follow_from_prefs, called from a 0.2s one-shot at register (prefs unresolved during register()). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 569 -> 570. Prefs UI: Workflow > Automations > Actions + prefs_search map; texts/ + de_DE keyed in lockstep. Tests: test_follow_selection.py (11). Suite 2745 passed. Glossary decided 2026-08-29 on the principle Blender's word wins (§7's principle applied to prose), which settled six of eight. Four user rulings: View Layer spelled out everywhere, no VL short form at any UI width; Watchlist beats Actions List; New/Add both kept with Blender's own split (New Material vs Add Modifier) and Create/Make banned; standard + auditor rule FIRST, the ~85-string rename as a separate later pass. Remaining terms: Autokey (Blender is itself inconsistent, so the addon's dominant form wins), Folder over Directory with Path reserved for the FIELD, Settings over Options with Preferences reserved for the prefs window, Configuration over Config, Data-block. Delete/Remove/Clear are three REAL acts and all three stay — what is banned is two of them naming one act on one object. Select/Pick is a definition for authors only; the auditor does not judge which is right, because that needs a human (the dev note's "do not promise more"). Machine-readable half is ui_vocabulary.json, read by the auditor as INFO-18 UI Vocabulary through ui_glossary_path (auditor repo, own tests + regenerated goldens). It lives in THIS repo, version-controlled and reviewable, rather than in the auditor's gitignored addons_registry.json — the ARCH-01 arch_layers regression is what that costs. Advisory (no score deduction) until the glossary settles, then promoted, the same ramp INFO-05 used. First live scan: 197 findings over 4130 reader-facing strings — 165 term (View Layer 93, Folder 23, Data-block 14, Settings 12, Watchlist 11, Configuration 10, Autokey 2), 27 banned verb (Create 26, Drop 1), 5 verb collision (action, slot, item, token, selected), 0 shape (declared labels were already clean), 2 exempt. Make Relative / Make Absolute are in the glossary allow list: Blender owns those strings, so the same principle that bans Make rescues them. NO RENAME IN THIS COMMIT. §13.5 records the hard constraint for the rename pass: every renamed English label is a translation key and texts/locales/de_DE.py must be re-keyed in the SAME commit or dev/tests/test_i18n_guard.py fails — no grace period, no follow-up commit.

    7. 🟢 Eight new built-in render-path tokens + world widened to render paths. Prompted by a side-by-side with another add-on's variable sheet; everything on it that we lacked and that earns its place is now ours. resolution_x_scaled / resolution_y_scaled (the pixel size actually written after resolution_percentage), region_width / region_height and their _scaled partners (the Blender render border measured in pixels, falling back to the full frame while use_border is off — one branch in _resolve_render_tokens keyed on "width" in token / endswith("_scaled"), not four copies), frame_step (scene.frame_step, in the animation cluster beside frame_start/frame_end), and render_type → "still" / "animation". render_type is ours, not Blender's: it reads the add-on's own Still & Animation Mode cascade, so a take pinned to the still frame names its output differently from an animated one — the reason this token is worth more than a raw property mirror. It is asked through the provider seam (core.providers.query("still_mode.resolve_still", scene, view_layer), registered in features/still_mode/__init__.register), NOT by importing still_mode sideways: the first draft did import it and test_no_new_architecture_violations correctly failed with ARCH02 features/smart_syntax/resolvers.py→still_mode. An unregistered provider defaults to False → "animation", which is the right answer for a torn-down feature. world gains CONTEXT_RENDER_PATH alongside CONTEXT_SLOT_NAME and a real smart-engine resolver in _resolve_context_tokens (scene.world.name or NoWorld); before this it only resolved through the naming engine, so [world] in a render path echoed back unresolved. NoWorld joins ABSENCE_SENTINELS so the grid dims the token instead of previewing the sentinel. All eight land in TOKEN_CATEGORY_MODEL (render + animation categories), which the superset guard test_model_covers_every_unified_token requires. Named region_*, not render_region_*: the Build Syntax grid is a fixed-width grid_flow and a token past roughly 21 characters truncates to an ellipsis ([render_region_width_s...), which is what the first draft shipped. resolution_percentage (21) is the measured ceiling, so region_height_scaled (20) is the longest name here. The render_ half was pure redundancy inside a category already titled Render & Format. Deliberately NOT added: blend_full_path (an absolute path inside a file name is not a naming component). Tests: dev/tests/test_scene_output_tokens.py (29). (Verified 2026-08-30 by a live probe against merged main, not by the suite alone: known scene state — 1920x1080 at 50 %, a half-width/half-height render border, frame step 3, a named world — then every token resolved through SmartSyntaxEngine.resolve_token and one whole pattern through resolve_path -> //renders/animation/960x540_step3. All 13 token values, both render_type states, the NoWorld sentinel and the no-border fallback matched.) Branch feat/more-builtin-tokens, merged 84dfb21a.

    8. 🟢 Keep technical terms in English — the machinery, the page, and the first term. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-30.) A German 3D artist reads Voreinstellung and has to translate it back in their head. The German word list can now point at a term by name — «preset» — instead of spelling it out, and texts/i18n.build_dict() fills the name in ONCE while the finished list is handed to Blender. Blender still receives plain finished sentences, so no panel, button or message in the tree changes and drawing costs exactly what it cost before. Flipping the switch rebuilds the list and re-registers it, which is one cheap call. Guillemets, not braces: every other bracket is already a naming token ({token}, [token], <token>, (token), %token%, #token#, $token$) and %s / {name} are live format placeholders inside these very strings. «…» collides with none of them and appeared nowhere in the tree (verified). An unknown name is left visible rather than blanked, so a typo reaches the guard test instead of a reader. texts/locales/vocabulary_de_DE.py ships 23 terms, and the defaults are EVIDENCE not taste: on where Blender's own German catalogue refuses to translate the term (measured in 5.2 — Preset, Slots, Take, Tag, Token, Shader, Material, Batch, Data-block all come back unchanged) or where its German misleads (Slot → Position, Compositor → Setzer); off where the German is ordinary German an artist says out loud (Szene, Kamera, Welt, Ordner). Those are offered, never forced. The page had to be invented. Preferences ▸ UI ▸ Language did not exist and neither did any language setting — the add-on never owned one, it follows Blender's view.language. New LANGUAGE sub-tab under Interface (props_navigation), drawn in draw_interface.py, backed by preferences/props/props_language.py and preferences/ops_language.py. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 571 → 578. The list is user data. A shipped term is stored by KEY (so re-wording either spelling never orphans the user's answer); a term the user invents stores both words, since nothing else knows them, and is applied as a plain text swap — the page says so, because it cannot follow grammar the way a marked term does. Both collections ride their own JSON blocks (_jargon_terms, _custom_jargon) because a bpy_prop_collection cannot go through the scalar save path; ensure_terms() seeds EVERY shipped language, not just the active one, or a user who installs in English and switches to German later would find an empty list with nothing to re-seed it. First term family marked: presets, 61 occurrences. PLURAL ONLY on purpose — German's plural article is die for every gender and plural adjective endings do not vary by gender, so swapping a plural noun can never strand an article or an ending. The singular changes gender (die Voreinstellung → das Preset) and 41 of its 80 occurrences sit behind an article or an adjective that would have to agree; those need a curated pass, measured and not guessed. The page was blank in English, and that shipped. The first cut drew ONE dismissible tip - “the language it is set to now has no word list, so there is nothing to choose here” - and closing it left a page with nothing on it, which reads as a broken add-on. Field report, not a test. The page now always draws its real content: Blender's own view.language and use_translate_interface sit at the top, because this page is where a reader looks for them and without them an English session has nothing it can act on; the switch and the term list are drawn greyed out rather than missing; and the “no word list” note is a plain label row, never a tip, so it cannot be dismissed into nothing. test_prefs_language_page.py records a stand-in layout and asserts the page draws controls, text, the language setting, the switch and both buttons in en_US AND de_DE - the smoke test only proved the draw did not RAISE, which an empty page also does not. +5 tests, prop count 578 → 579.

      Both spellings rendered as the SAME German word. Field report with a screenshot: every row read “Voreinstellung · Voreinstellung”, “Position · Position”. The label showing the ENGLISH form was itself being auto-translated, because Preset, Action, View Layer are sources in our own word list - so the one thing the row exists to tell apart was destroyed. Both labels now draw with translate=False: a word being OFFERED as a choice is DATA, not interface text. Same report: the list is one column in two named groups now (grouped_keys()), and the split is the same line the defaults already follow, so the page SHOWS why a box is ticked. Three i18n traps on the way, all measured: the collector does not harvest English sources from texts/locales/ (it is translation data), does not see a string buried in a tuple of tuples, and does not see a text= behind a dict lookup - so the group ids live in the vocabulary and the WORDS are literal label(text=…) branches at the draw site. Suite 2678 passed, 1 skipped.

      A ticked box that did nothing, and no way to tell what ticked MEANS. Field report: View Layer was listed, ticking and unticking it both changed nothing, because only presets had been wired into the German strings - a dead switch reads as a broken feature. locales.wired_terms(code) now answers which terms the word list actually points at (computed once and cached, never per draw), and the page offers only those; test_no_dead_switch_is_offered pins it. Four more plural families were wired in the same pass - viewlayers 107, scenes 96, actions 38, channels 14 - plurals only and never inside a compound, or Ansichtsebenen-Gruppe would have become View Layers-Gruppe. Separately, a bare tick box beside two words never said WHICH word it picks: each group now carries an English | Translated heading with the box under the word it turns on, and every row dims the spelling you are not getting, so the bright word is always the one you read. Both groups are proper accordions (expand_language_group_jargon / _german), prop count 579 → 581. Suite 2680 passed, 1 skipped.

      Ticking a term reverted the word and it stayed reverted. Field report, and the sharpest bug of the feature. In an RNA update callback self is whatever struct owns the property that fired - the AddonPreferences for the master switch, but a single LIST ROW for a term tick or a custom word. _vocabulary_update passed that row straight on, so effective_terms() read keep_terms_english off an object with no such property, fell back to False, and handed Blender a fully German list. The master switch worked, every per-term tick did the opposite of what it said. It resolves the real preferences through get_prefs() now, pinned by test_a_term_row_update_still_reads_the_real_preferences. That test also had to learn to put the WHOLE world back: leaving the switch on re-registered a German-with-jargon word list that outlived it, and three AI call-log tests then read translated log lines and failed - caught by baselining the suite with the change stashed rather than calling them flaky. Suite 2681 passed, 1 skipped.

      Every answer belongs to ONE language (user ruling 2026-08-29). A term key is shared between languages but the ANSWER must not be: a German reader wanting Preset in English says nothing about what a French reader wants for the same term, and a word someone invents (Ordner → Folder) is meaningless outside the language it was written for - swapping it into another translation would corrupt it. Both row types carry a language now; ensure_terms seeds one row per (language, term) and only for a language that is actually translated (code in LOCALES, or a vocabulary with no word list beside it would produce rows that change nothing - the dead-switch problem one level up); effective_terms / effective_custom read only the active language; the page lists only its rows; Add Term stamps the language it was written in and Reset Terms resets that language alone. A row saved before this existed has no code and migrates to de_DE, which is the only thing it could have meant. The tests for it are PURE - a stand-in preferences object, never the live one. The first cut switched view.language and the master switch on the real preferences and put them back, and still took out three AI call-log tests further down the run; stashing the change and watching the suite go green proved it was mine both times. +8 tests. Suite 2689 passed, 1 skipped.

      Five of the 23 shipped terms were WRONG, and reading the sentences is what caught it. The vocabulary was first built by matching an English term to the German word that usually stands for it. That is not the same as reading the place it matched: slot→Position never once meant an animation slot (frame position, keyframed position, an index in a collection - the add-on's German already writes Slot); render→Rendern is the nominalised VERB, so zum Rendern would have become zum Render; marker→Markierung was a STAR on a token and a red camera marking; override→Überschreiben sat under the English source Render Overwrite, which is overwriting a FILE; modifier→Modifikator was Key Modifier, a keyboard key. All five removed, with the reasoning kept in the file, because the rule matters more than the list: a term earns its place by what the sentence says, never by a word appearing often enough. Two of them had already been marked in de_DE and are unmarked again. Wired in the same pass: timeline (12) and viewport (1) - both keep their German GENDER (Zeitleiste f → Timeline f), so no article or adjective in front of them can be stranded, which is the whole reason the plurals were easy. Nine terms work now. The page tests also learned to open an accordion before asserting about what is inside it - a collapsed section draws nothing, and testing that is testing the fold. Suite 2689 passed, 1 skipped.

      Four things the suite caught and are fixed: wrapped_info_box takes context; a row must not COMPOSE its label (two proper nouns are drawn as two labels, so the composed-string guard has nothing to catch); the collections needed the JSON round-trip above; and test_reserved_config_keys_is_empty asserted the reserved set was EMPTY when it meant no token key is reserved — rewritten to its actual intent. 13 new tests. Suite 2673 passed, 1 skipped. End-to-end probe in a German 5.2 session: switch off Render-Voreinstellungen, on Render-Presets, unticking the one term puts it back. 9. 🟢 Diff State Mode — a POST_VIEW viewport overlay marking objects by the state they are in. The sister of Rest State Mode. Two states: KEYED (the datablock holds an action slot carrying F-Curves, resolved through core/anim_utils.get_slot_fcurves — being BOUND to a shared action is NOT being animated) and DRIFT (live values match neither the Rest Action nor the object's own keyed value). Drift is READ from Rest State via core.providers.query("rest_state.get_rest_drifts"), never a sibling-feature import (ARCH-02 rejected the first attempt). Correctness rule: a KEYED channel's drift is only readable at frame 0 or inside Rest State Mode, so off that frame the mode refuses the reading and says so in the Overlays panel rather than painting a wrong colour. State lives on WindowManager.tks_diff_state (session-only; a test asserts it is absent from Scene). Two homes, each hideable: a button in the navigation mode row (three edits — panels/navigation/panel.py, panels/mode_toggles.py MODE_KEYS, and the stored pie enum in preferences/addon_prefs_constants.py) and a VIEW3D_PT_overlay subpanel. The operator is a plain execute() with NO invoke() (Constitution rule 7), held by two tests. The scan is cached between draws and dirtied by any depsgraph update or a frame change — drift depends on the frame — because a full rest scan per draw would cost more than the drawing. Marks follow what the VIEWPORT shows: visible_get(viewport=space) folds in Local View, hide flags and collection visibility, and must run per space rather than in the scene-wide scan. features/diff_state/: logic.py (pure, no bpy), states.py, cache.py, shapes.py, draw.py, operators.py, panel.py, properties.py. Commits 1deecd53..b49f13d7.

    Field reports fixed on the branch, before release: the mode ignored Local View and marked hidden objects; nothing drew when the master had no marks and only one kind had its own; the camera pyramid appeared only while the Box mark was also on; marks pulsed in camera view and surfaceless curves vanished. Each was found in-app, and none could have been caught by the unit tests, which were green throughout - they were control flow inside the draw callback and a scan that listed more than the viewport shows. 10. 🟢 Each state owns a complete settings set; 229 new preferences. Colour, random hue, line width, three opacities, four master marks, empty style and size, plus a fourteen-row object-kind table (own-flag + 4 marks + style + size) — per state, generated per state and per kind rather than written out, since a copy-paste block that long is where a wrong name hides. Property names come from helper functions (state_master_prop, kind_mark_prop, …): a typo inside a getattr is silent, a typo in a helper fails a test. The table is properties rather than one stored string BECAUSE click-and-drag across toggles is a property-editor behaviour that never works on operator buttons — the string version was built, measured, and replaced. Per-kind capability is PROBED, not assumed: only MESH/SURFACE/META/CURVE/FONT yield geometry; six kinds report bounds of exactly ZERO and box from their DISPLAY size instead; ARMATURE reports a sliver. Asking for a mark a kind cannot draw never drops the object — it falls back to the best mark that kind can draw. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 586 → 815 after the merge with main (220 generated in the loop, plus the drift-priority enum, two homes and six section flags). Commits ed0ebdd8, 570a37ae, 05b06177. 11. 🟢 Four marks, including an Empty in a chosen style. Box (one shared unit-cube batch through a per-object matrix — cost independent of poly count), Outline (inverted hull: the cached triangles pushed along their normals with FRONT culling), Fill (translucent surface), and Empty (one of Blender's empty display shapes at the origin, sized from the object's own extent). Outline and Fill share ONE geometry store held in LOCAL space and reused through the object matrix, so an object that merely MOVES never rebuilds — the handler keys on is_updated_geometry, never on transform, and writes nothing but that store. Past a 400k-triangle budget the heavier objects fall back to the box, cheapest first so the ceiling costs the fewest objects, ties broken on name so the choice cannot flicker; reported once, not per frame. Commits fb60ea13, 2c088e98. 12. 🟢 Shapeless kinds are outlined with the shape Blender itself draws. A camera's real view_frame pyramid, a spot light's cone from spot_size, an area light's emitter rectangle from size/size_y (a real ELLIPSE when the shape is oval — drawing it as a circle threw the Y size away), an empty's chosen display type, a lattice's own point cage, an armature's own bones, a box light probe as a box. Built from the SAME data the gizmo uses, in local space, so the world matrix scales them exactly as Blender scales its own (three tests: uniform scale, non-uniform scale, display-size edit). Grease pencil and volume keep box only — the table stays honest about what exists. Commits 2859ff74, 2d3e61d0, 7173b5f1. 13. 🟢 A per-object random hue, as a switch on top of the state colours. Hue from object.session_uid stepped by the golden-ratio conjugate, so consecutive ids land far apart on the wheel - tests assert >0.05 separation across 40 consecutive uids and all six hue buckets covered across 120. Keyed on session_uid, never a name hash (would recolour on rename) and never as_pointer() (banned - freed addresses are reused, so the cache would hand one object's colour to a stranger). The STATE still decides which marks draw; only the hue comes from the object. Commit 4d4b11c6. 14. 🟢 Drift priority: how much of a doubly-marked object drift takes over. An object can be keyed AND drifted; two colours on one object say neither clearly. Drift always wins where both want the same mark. ALL (default) gives it the whole object; MATCHING gives it only the marks it draws itself and leaves the rest to keyed. Pure split_marks(), eight tests. Two subtleties pinned there: a state with nothing left to draw drops out rather than drawing an empty set (otherwise a drift drawing no marks would take the keyed marks down with it), and an unknown saved priority reads as ALL rather than inventing a third behaviour. Commit b49f13d7. 15. 🟢 Unsaved-moves review in the drift warning panel. get_rest_drifts entries partition on their existing keyed flag in panels/navigation/warnings/cascade_rest_drift.py: unkeyed drift keeps the classic red box, keyed drift renders as an 'Unsaved Moves' box (a borrowed value Blender discards on the next animation evaluation) with per-item Keep (tks.keep_unsaved_move, keys the SHOWN value via a value FloatProperty so a draw→click race cannot key a stale live value) and per-item Let Go (existing tks.snap_prop_to_rest), plus bulk tks.keep_all_unsaved_moves / tks.let_go_all_unsaved_moves delegating to the operator-independent cores keep_all_unsaved / let_go_all_unsaved in features/rest_state/logic.py, both built on the new rest-independent iter_unsaved_moves(context) (keyed channels whose live value differs from fc.evaluate(frame_current), driven channels excluded, valid at any frame). All ops are plain execute() with name/path args (Constitution 7); bulk cores are the tested surface because a headless bpy.ops dispatch re-evaluates pending tags and discards the borrowed values before execute runs (interactively they survive — verified against the 2026-08-31 field log). 11 de_DE entries, 3 long tooltips parked in _pending.py. Tests: dev/tests/test_unsaved_moves_review.py (5), dev/tests/test_keep_scalar_channel.py (2 — field report: Keep answered 'Could not keyframe the moved value' on SCALAR channels, whose fcurve array_index is 0 while the property takes no index; keyframe_channel in logic.py now keys by the property's real shape, used by the op and the bulk core).

    1. 🔴 Row actions and add actions get a home in TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu. panels/context/tree_context_menu.py held one entry ("Show Overrides…"), so right-clicking a row taught nothing about the eight row actions bound to keys. It now draws rename, duplicate, duplicate linked, retarget, group, ungroup, invert selection, the three add actions, and delete — ten of the fourteen bound operators. Two invariants are pinned by tests because both are easy to undo in a tidy-up: the menu draws the dispatcher ids (tks.global_*), never the sub-operators they route to (drawing tks.delete_tree_item would delete the row perfectly and silently stop teaching X, since Blender looks the key up by the operator it is BOUND to); and both duplicate entries set linked explicitly. Delete sits last behind its own divider. Entries pass no text= where the operator's bl_label already says it, so only one new English string exists (Duplicate Linked, re-keyed in texts/locales/de_DE.py as Verknüpft duplizieren in the same commit). Icons are all names already used elsewhere in the tree (icon enum names drift between versions).

      The chord is Shift+RMB (user ruling 2026-08-31; it was Ctrl+RMB, which nobody finds). Two other routes were tried and are written up in dev/tests/test_tree_context_menu_trigger.py so neither is re-attempted. CORRECTED after a second field report: a keymap item on plain RIGHTMOUSE was tried and DOES NOT FIRE over a tree row — Blender's UI button handler sits ahead of the Window keymap in the region's handler list and consumes the press for its own property menu. The dead binding was removed rather than left to fire only over blank space, which would make the behaviour depend on where in the panel you click. Ctrl+RMB worked only because nothing else claimed that chord, and Shift+RMB is the same bargain. Appending our rows to Blender's property menu was then tried, shipped, confirmed working in-app — the entries appeared and each printed its key — and WITHDRAWN on the user's ruling: Blender builds the native half in C before any Python runs, so our block could only ever sit below reset-to-default and copy-data-path, and a menu that is half ours reads worse than one that is none of ours. Researched before conceding: the property menu is not keymap-driven (Blender's own "User Interface" keymap has no RIGHTMOUSE item), UI_MT_button_context_menu.draw is already an empty stub so the override-the-draw-pointer trick changes nothing, and UI_MT_list_item_context_menu is appended into the same popup below the same block. Three of the native entries are Developer Extras and vanish when the reader turns that preference off; the rest cannot be removed from Python at all. A reader right-clicks a row and Blender answers with its own PROPERTY menu for tks_all_viewlayers_index — reset to default, copy data path — which teaches nothing (reported with a screenshot 2026-08-31). Those native items are drawn in C BEFORE UI_MT_button_context_menu is appended, so Python can add to that menu but never remove from it; showing only ours means taking the chord. Both chords are bound: Ctrl+RMB stays, because removing a chord people already learned is a regression. Taking plain RMB forces a narrower poll — in_sidebar alone is every tab of the 3D View sidebar, and Blender's reset-to-default must survive on properties that have nothing to do with this addon. TKS_OT_OpenTreeContextMenu.poll now also requires region.active_panel_category == 'Takes', read with getattr so an unknown category is treated as ALLOWED, never denied: a Blender that does not expose the property should cost a menu that is slightly too eager, not one that has silently stopped opening. (The property is absent from Blender's bundled scripts but present in the 5.2 binary and used by other addons.) The menu keeps ONE entry from the menu it replaces — Online Manual, via the existing tks.open_documentation, re-keyed as Online-Handbuch in the same commit. dev/tests/test_tree_context_menu_trigger.py (9) pins the scope, the unknown-category fallback, and that the category string still matches the panels' own bl_category. 17. 🟢 Blender prints the bound key beside each of those entries — measured, not assumed. Phase 1 was a spike (dev/tmp/spike_shortcut_lookup.py, dev/tmp/spike_shortcut_gui.py, dev/tmp/spike_popup_context.py; full write-up in doc/roadmap/_dev/clickable-hotkeys.md). Python has no binding for WM_key_event_operator_string, so the probe used wm.keyconfigs.find_item_from_operator — the binding for the same wm_keymap_item_find search with the same strict property matching. Result in a GUI 5.2: 10 of 11 HIT, every one reporting keymap Window with the correct chord. Four catches, all measured: (a) --background answers NOTHING — the context search misses ed.undo, wm.search_menu, object.delete and screen.animation_play too, so a control group is mandatory or a background zero reads as a real answer; (b) the addon keymap must first be MERGED into the user keyconfig — enabling the addon inside the same timer frame as the probe gave a clean 0-of-11 false negative; (c) tks.global_duplicate asked with NO properties resolves to Alt+D, the LAST binding registered, so an entry reading "Duplicate" would advertise the linked key — with linked=False it is Shift+D and with linked=True it is Alt+D, exactly; (d) tks.smart_undo was the one miss, correctly: _set_user_kmi_active(False) deactivates its user-kc mirror when the smart-undo toggle is off and the search skips inactive items. Also measured: the menu popup INHERITS the invoking region — inside the open menu area=VIEW_3D, region=UI, in_sidebar(context)=True, identical to the sidebar baseline — so the dispatchers' _in_sidebar poll passes and no gate change was needed (the expectation had been TEMPORARY and greyed entries). And: bpy.ops.wm.call_menu under --background is an EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, not a catchable exception. 18. 🔴 Ratchet guard dev/tests/test_shortcut_reachability.py. Walks every keymap_items.new( call and every .operator()-family call site with ast, resolving both string literals and SOME_OT_Class.bl_idname on both sides, and fails when an operator the addon binds a key to has no call site. MAX_UNREACHABLE = 0 (13 on main @ b78e5e8f, 15 once the auditor's new MAINT-13 found two the hand count missed), paired with the usual tightener so the baseline cannot go stale, plus a check that no exemption is stale and every exemption states a reason over 40 characters. new_modal is not a shortcut; a bpy.ops call is not a button. Five declared exemptions, each an argument rather than a parking space: tks.smart_undo / tks.smart_redo (a hijack of Ctrl+Z that DEFERS to Blender's undo — listing it would tell the reader Takes owns undo, and its key is invisible whenever the master toggle is off, so the entry would teach nothing half the time; they are also not row actions, and Blender puts undo in the Edit menu), tks.open_tree_context_menu (it opens this menu; an entry inside it would be circular), tks.vsw_live_key_guard (a PASS_THROUGH autokey guard, invisible by design), tks.invoke_keyframe_pie (the pie is its own surface, and its key is read from preferences so no chord could be printed). Pure Python, no Blender. 7 tests here plus 17 in dev/tests/test_tree_context_menu.py. Full suite 2778 passed, 1 skipped, run against the worktree via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS with the junction left on main.

    2. 🔴 A button for the row-actions menu, in the tree's own side column. Shift+RMB is still a shortcut, and a shortcut nobody knows about is the exact problem this card exists to end — a menu reachable only by a chord has the same discoverability as the keys it was built to teach. panels/context/draw_tree.py now draws col.menu("TKS_MT_tree_context_menu", text="", icon='DOWNARROW_HLT') directly under the +/- pair, which is where Blender puts a list's specials menu. It must be layout.menu, not an operator that opens the menu: only a Menu subclass gets the bound key printed beside each entry, and an operator wrapper would work perfectly while teaching nothing. A menu button is also a UI_BTYPE_PULLDOWN, and ui_popup_context_menu_for_button returns early for those — so right-clicking this button is silent rather than offering copy-data-path, which is a small free win after the whole property-menu detour. The menu acts on _active_item(), the highlighted row, so the button and the chord operate on exactly the same thing.

    3. 🟢 The tree's settings move into the row dropdown and the gear button is retired. The column briefly carried a chevron AND a gear (tks.icon_visibility_settings, SETTINGS) - two dropdowns that look like they do different things, with nothing on either to say which is which. TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu._list_settings now draws the settings at the foot of the one menu, the slot TKS_MT_WatchlistRowMenu and the two inspector list menus already use. _draw_body's no-row early return calls _list_settings before returning, or an unclicked tree would have no door to Tree Design at all. test_the_two_dropdowns_do_not_share_an_icon is replaced by test_the_column_has_only_one_dropdown, test_the_settings_moved_into_the_row_menu and test_the_settings_survive_an_empty_selection.
    4. 🔴 The row menu's heading spells the row type out, and the manual link leaves. VL:, SG: and VLG: are banned by the UI vocabulary standard (doc/standards/naming_conventions.md section 13), and this header is exactly why the ban exists: it was the one place they appeared, with nothing anywhere to tell a reader what they stood for. _header is now a table of {item_type: (word, icon)} composed through pgettext_iface, so all five headings translate with no new English strings — View Layer, Take, Scene, Scene Group and View Layer Group were already in de_DE.py. The Online Manual entry is removed with it: it was there only while this menu was replacing Blender's property menu on plain right-click, and the menu is what you do TO a row, not a place to leave. Its de_DE key goes in the same commit, because the drift guard fails on a translation whose English source no longer exists. Two tests pin the wording, one per direction: the headings read as expected, and none of them contains an abbreviation.
    5. 🔴 Collection Visibility copy/paste moves to the row menu and gains Shift+C / Shift+V.
