It sat in the tree-design popover, which configures how the tree LOOKS; copying a view layer's collection visibility is something you do TO a row. tks.copy_vl_settings / tks.paste_vl_settings are drawn in TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu and bound in the Window keymap. Not Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V, and that is measured rather than taste: neither is in Blender's "User Interface" keymap (only Ctrl+Shift+C is), which means the button handler owns them in C — the same reason a plain RIGHTMOUSE item never fires over a tree row. A Ctrl+C item would have lost the press identically. Both polls gained the in_sidebar gate, without which a Window-keymap key fires anywhere in Blender the moment a view layer row happens to be highlighted. Neither entry needs enabled bookkeeping in the menu: copy already wants a view layer row, paste wants one AND a valid clipboard. Both bl_labels were renamed from "Copy/Paste View Layer Settings" to "Copy/Paste Collection Visibility" — every surface that ever showed them said Collection Visibility while the operators said something else, which is the drift INFO-18 exists to catch. Three de_DE keys move in the same commit; the now-unused ('*', 'Collection Visibility') entry is deleted, which is how the orphan-translation guard caught the rename in the first place.
    6. 🔴 Retarget leaves the tree-design popover, and finally greys out. Its entry is tks.global_retarget in the row menu, so _draw_retarget in operators/misc/ops_tree_design.py had no caller left and is gone with it. The greying is the real fix: TKS_OT_RetargetTreeItem.poll answered the weaker question — "is this a row type that CAN be retargeted" — so it stayed lit on a scene whose file holds only one scene group, and clicking reported a refusal. That is right for a KEY, which cannot grey, and wrong for a menu entry sitting there looking available. The poll now resolves the row type (single or multi-select) and asks the TYPED operator, which already knows whether it has anywhere to move to; the four-way table is shared with execute so the greying and the action cannot disagree, the same discipline the move arrows follow. The poll swallows exceptions — a poll that raises takes the whole panel down.
    7. 🔴 Group and Ungroup grey out separately. TKS_OT_GroupOrUngroup is one operator with an action property and ONE poll classmethod serving both values — and a poll never sees the property. So both dispatchers asked the same question and got the same answer: Ungroup offered on a row already sitting in Ungrouped, Group offered on a group header that _group refuses outright and reports on. New can_group / can_ungroup in operators/context/groups/ops_manage.py split the question, reading the SAME conditions _group and _ungroup route on rather than restating them, and TKS_OT_GlobalGroup.poll / TKS_OT_GlobalUngroup.poll each call their own. A cross-scene view-layer selection is deliberately left ENABLED: it is refused with a sentence saying why, and a grey button would say nothing at all. 10 tests in dev/tests/test_group_ungroup_greying.py, including the bug in one line — a group header can be ungrouped and cannot be grouped, so any implementation answering both from one poll is wrong whatever it returns.
    8. 🔴 Show Overrides leaves the row menu. User ruling: the cascade overflow popover is already reached from the row's own icons, and a second door crowded a menu whose job is the operators that have a KEY. Its de_DE key goes in the same commit — the orphan-translation guard caught it, as it caught the Collection Visibility rename before it. Audit of every remaining entry (the user asked for all of them to be checked, not just the one reported): Rename greys off non-rows; Duplicate and Duplicate Linked grey on group headers; Retarget asks the typed operator (entry 16); Group and Ungroup as above; Invert Selection lights only in multi-select, which is correct and is why it read grey in the field screenshot; Copy Collection Visibility wants a view layer row and Paste wants one plus a filled clipboard; the three Add entries are always available by design, since they open menus rather than act on the row; Delete delegates to the batch operator's poll in multi-select. Two were wrong, both fixed here; the rest were already honest.
    9. 🔴 Select All joins the row menu, and both selection tools say what they need. TKS_OT_SelectAllMultiselect (tks.select_all_multiselect) is the twin of the invert operator, running select_all — which already existed and had the same provider problem — through the same honest _run_multiselect helper, so it cannot inherit the shape Fixed 31 removed. The "multi-select only" clarification goes in the TOOLTIP, on the user's ruling: a label reading "Select All (multi-select)" would invent a second name for a mode that already has one. Both tooltips were rewritten to say what the action does AND that it is only available while multi-select is on; the invert rewording orphaned its old German key, which the drift guard caught. No hotkey was invented for Select All — Ctrl+A is a plausible one but was not asked for, and an unrequested binding is a clash waiting to happen.
    10. 🔴 Multi-select changes what five entries REACH, so while it is on they say so. Switch the mode on and Delete stops meaning "this row" and starts meaning "every ticked row" — with no change to the label. Delete is a bad place to discover that. TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu._label marks global_delete, global_group, global_ungroup, global_retarget and paste_vl_settings with (Multi-Select) while tks_multiselect_list == "CONTEXT". Composed from two words that were ALREADY translated — the operator's own label and Multi-Select — so the marker costs no new English string and reads correctly in German the day it appears. Rename, Duplicate and Copy Collection Visibility are deliberately NOT marked: they act on the active row whatever the mode, and a marker there would be a lie in the other direction. Three tests: marked when on, bare when off, and never marked on the single-row three.
    11. 🔴 The three Add entries leave the row menu; Shift+A and Ctrl+N find better homes. Adding is not something you do TO a row. Shift+A moves to the tree column's +, which becomes col.operator("tks.global_add_menu") instead of col.menu("TKS_MT_FullAddMenu") — the difference is the point: a menu button carries the menu's STATIC bl_description, while an operator has a description() classmethod reading the live keyconfig, so that button names its key and keeps naming it after a rebind. It also routes by active list (takes / tags / variants) rather than hardcoding one menu. Ctrl+N moves INSIDE the menu that opens, as the first entry, where Blender prints the key beside it. Ctrl+Shift+N is exempted in the ratchet with its reason: it is the always-ask variant of Ctrl+N and opens the very menu an entry for it would have to live in. Researched while deciding: Blender does not communicate Shift+A anywhere either — NODE_MT_add sits in a header, and header menus print no shortcut — but bl_ui/space_view3d.py twice carries the comment "Primarily for shortcut discoverability" above operators placed in a menu purely so their key shows, which is this card's whole premise in Blender's own words.
    12. 🔴 The multi-select marker blanked five labels when the mode was off. _label returned "" as its "unmarked" answer and the caller passed it straight to text=. Blender does not read text="" as "no override" — it takes it literally and draws an entry with an icon, a key, and no name between them. Reported from a running session one commit after the marker landed. _label returns None now, and _draw_operator(layout, idname, icon) passes text only when there is something to say. Two guards, because the first version of the test could not have caught it: the fake layout distinguishes "no text given" from text="" with a sentinel default, and a second test sweeps EVERY entry in BOTH modes for an empty label. The wrapper then hid five entries from the reachability ratchet, which walks .operator( calls and cannot see an idname passed to a helper — exactly the false-positive class the auditor's MAINT-13 notes list as its known blind spot, arriving in our own code the first time a menu needed a conditional label. It is named _draw_operator rather than _op so the guard can match it by name without catching anything else, and the guard reads its idname from argument two.
    13. 🔴 active_panel_category answers UNSUPPORTED, not None, off the draw path. Measured while chasing a greyed + (dev/experiments/probe_add_button.py): read from a Region OUTSIDE a draw, Blender 5.2 returns that literal string; read inside a panel draw it returns the live tab name. TKS_OT_OpenTreeContextMenu._in_takes_tab compared it to "Takes" and treated anything else as "wrong tab", so wherever that poll runs off the draw path it would silently refuse to open the menu — the shape of bug that never reproduces for whoever reports it. UNSUPPORTED and "" now count as unknown, which the existing rule already treats as ALLOWED. The same probe measured what it was actually sent for and cleared it: in a panel draw the sidebar is area=VIEW_3D, region=UI, in_sidebar=True and tks.global_add_menu.poll() is True, so the + is not greyed by its own poll and its column carries no disable flag. Both probes kept at dev/experiments/.
    14. 🔴 Ten dispatcher tooltips rewritten, and the + goes back to being a menu. The field tooltip read: "Add Menu / Route Shift+A to the active list's context add menu / Shift+A: the key this is bound to right now / Shortcut: Shift A". Three faults in one box. The description described the PLUMBING — "route X to the active list's Y" is how it works, not what the reader gets — and hardcoded the key in prose, which is the staleness live_shortcut exists to prevent. The hand-written key line read like debug text. And Blender already prints Shortcut: Shift A itself on an operator button, so we said it twice, ours worse. All ten now say what the button does, with the multi-select reach spelled out where it differs; the {key} line is gone, and with it the ten description() classmethods that existed only to fill it — they are plain bl_description constants now, and live_shortcut is no longer imported there. Ten German keys re-keyed; a regex ate an unrelated Route batch-render… entry on the way through and the diff caught it. Separately, the tree's + reverts from col.operator("tks.global_add_menu") to col.menu("TKS_MT_FullAddMenu"): as an operator it came out GREY in the field. A routing dispatcher's poll answers a KEYPRESS question — am I in the sidebar, so Shift+A does not clobber the viewport's — and a button that simply opens a menu has no business inheriting it. A + that greys is a worse trade than a + whose tooltip does not name its key. tks.global_add_menu is exempted in the ratchet with that reason, and a test pins the + as a menu so the swap is not retried.
    15. 🟢 The + keeps its menu-button look, and the trade behind that is written down. Three shapes were built and shown before the ruling. (1) The BOUND dispatcher greys: a panel button is polled against the area's WINDOW region, and in_sidebar is a guard written for a KEYPRESS — so Shift+A does not clobber the viewport's — which a button never needed to ask. (2) An UNBOUND twin fixed the greying and bought a live, hideable key line, because Blender prints its own unhideable Shortcut: line for any button it CAN find a binding for; but it changed how the button looks, since Blender draws menu buttons and operator buttons differently. (3) col.menu keeps the look and gives up the computed tooltip — a menu's bl_description is a fixed string, so its chord goes stale on a rebind and no preference can hide it. The look won (user ruling 2026-09-01), and everything that existed only for the twin came out with it: the operator, its key template, its German key, and the key hole added to compose_tooltip. What was KEPT is _open_add_menu, a routing table replacing an if/elif chain — and the crash that forced it: the twin reached the dispatcher through bpy.ops, inheriting its poll, and Blender raised context is incorrect on every click. Guarded by an AST test, because the substring version of it matched the comment above the fix and failed on the commit that made it true. MENU_FULLADDMENU also stopped burying the chord: (Shift+A). mid-sentence became Shift+A: open the add menu on its own line after a blank one, the house shape, re-keyed in German. Still prose, still stale-able — that is the accepted half of the trade, and the ratchet exemption for tks.global_add_menu now records all three attempts so a fourth is not started from scratch.
    16. 🔴 Ctrl+A for Select All, through a dispatcher rather than the feature operator. The first attempt put the sidebar gate straight onto TKS_OT_SelectAllMultiselect, which made features/ import from operators/ — an upward import, and test_no_new_architecture_violations failed the build on it. Correctly: the layer rule is utils < [core, properties] < [features, ui, prefs] < [operators, panels], and the established shape was already sitting next to it — tks.global_invert_select is exactly this, a thin operator in the operators layer carrying the gate and routing to the feature. TKS_OT_GlobalSelectAll (tks.global_select_all) is its twin, reusing OP_SELECTALLMULTISELECT so the key costs no new English string and no German. The gate is not optional: a Window-keymap item without it fires anywhere in Blender the moment multi-select happens to be on, and Ctrl+A is select-all-text in the text editor. Ctrl+A is safe where Ctrl+C was not — Blender claims it only in editor keymaps (Object Mode's apply menu, the text editor, the sequencer), never in "User Interface", so nothing owns it over the sidebar. Two tests: the gate is on the dispatcher, and features/ contains no from ...operators import.
    17. 🔴 Select All and Invert Selection are HIDDEN outside multi-select, not greyed. Greying is the right answer for an action that exists but cannot run on THIS row — Retarget with nowhere to move to, Ungroup on an already-ungrouped row. These two are a different case: without the mode there is no selection at all, so the operations have nothing to be about, and a grey pair would be two permanently dead rows in a menu the reader opens constantly (user ruling 2026-09-01). One _multiselect_on() reader now serves both the visibility test and the (Multi-Select) marker on the five entries whose reach changes, so the two can never disagree about what mode the tree is in. tks.global_invert_select therefore left the unconditional ROW_ACTIONS list in the tests and is covered by a pair of visibility tests instead.
    18. 🔴 Delete leaves the row menu. The tree column's - already deletes, one button below the +, and a second door to a destructive action in a menu the reader opens constantly is a door too many (user ruling 2026-09-01). tks.global_delete therefore loses its only .operator() call site and is exempted in the ratchet with the reason — the - performs the action, it simply draws the CONCRETE delete operators rather than the dispatcher, because a panel button drawn from a dispatcher greys out (its poll is written for a keypress, and a panel button is polled against the area's WINDOW region — the same fact that cost the + two attempts).
    19. 🔴 The - names its key, which is why losing the menu entry costs nothing. Blender prints no Shortcut: line there: the button draws tks.delete_context_item / tks.delete_selected_context_items / tks.delete_group, and the chord is bound to tks.global_delete, so Blender can find no binding for what it sees. The three operators now compose the line themselves — compose_tooltip(..., key=live_shortcut('tks.global_delete')) — which reads it live off the dispatcher, so a rebind moves it, and puts it past the blank line where the reader's "Show Shortcuts in Tooltips" switch can take it away. compose_tooltip regains the key hole removed two entries ago, now with a caller. Three key templates and their German. Why the auditor did not catch this: MAINT-13 asks whether every BOUND operator is reachable, and tks.global_delete was reachable — it had a menu entry. It has no opinion about a button that PERFORMS a keyed action without announcing the key, which is a different rule and one no check currently makes.
    20. 🔴 The single-row actions are hidden in multi-select, the mirror of the two selection tools. Audited by reading the OPERATORS, not the labels: TKS_OT_RenameItem and TKS_OT_DuplicateTreeItem both resolve _resolve_active_item and have no multi-select branch anywhere, so in that mode they sat there implying they act on the ticks and quietly acted on one row. Same rule as Select All and Invert Selection, the other way round: an entry appears only in the mode where it means something. Copy Collection Visibility reads one row too and deliberately stays in BOTH modes — it is the only way to fill the clipboard, and Paste writes to every ticked row, so hiding it would make copy-to-many impossible without leaving the mode first. That exception has its own test so a later tidy-up cannot "fix" it. Full audit for the record: Rename / Duplicate / Duplicate Linked = active row only; Retarget / Group / Ungroup / Paste = both modes, already marked; Select All / Invert = multi only; Copy = one row, both modes.

    21. 🔴 Shift+Click opens the row menu as well, and the menu's own tooltip names it. A second way in on the user's ruling; nothing else claims that chord on a tree row, since the multi-select ticks are their own checkboxes and the tree has no range-select. It may still lose to Blender's UI button handler the way a plain RIGHTMOUSE item did — a click on a UIList row is a button press the handler consumes to set the active index — which is two lines to try and two to remove, cheaper than another probe. MENU_TREECONTEXTMENU was "Right-click menu for a takes-tree row" and named no chord at all; it now carries the house Key: effect block. Only Shift+Click is named: test_tooltip_house_style knows the Click chords and nothing else, so "Shift+Right Click" reads to it as prose following the shortcut block and fails the style twice over — first for not starting its line with a known chord, then for trailing the block. The right-click chord still works; texts/keys.py simply has no name for a right-click gesture yet, which is a gap worth closing on its own.

    22. 🔴 Ctrl+M toggles multi-select. New dispatcher TKS_OT_GlobalMultiselect (tks.global_multiselect) in operators/ops_global_shortcuts.py, bound in panels/context/__init__.py on the Window/EMPTY keymap like its siblings, routing to bpy.ops.tks.multiselect(list_type=...) under a temp_override. Its poll is _in_sidebar plus _list_context(context) in ('CONTEXT', 'TAGS', 'VARIANTS') — only lists that ANNOUNCE themselves via tks_active_list_context can be toggled by one chord, so the key stays quiet over the inspector and split-view lists rather than toggling whichever list was focused last. No new English string: TKS_OT_MultiSelect's own OP_MULTISELECT ("Toggle multi-select mode") is reused, so nothing to re-key in de_DE.py. Why Ctrl+M and not Ctrl+Shift+A (both were free — the only keymap competing over the sidebar is Blender's "User Interface", which holds just Ctrl+Shift+C): in this addon Ctrl+Shift+X already means "a variant of Ctrl+X" (Ctrl+Shift+N is the always-ask variant of Ctrl+N), so Ctrl+Shift+A would have promised a different kind of Select All rather than a mode. Blender's own M chords are all editor keymaps in the WINDOW region.

    23. 🔴 The row menu draws the toggle in BOTH modes, depress=cls._multiselect_on(), unlike Select All / Invert Selection which appear only while the mode is on. It is the way in and the way out, so hiding it in either mode would strand the reader in the other. Drawing the DISPATCHER, not tks.multiselect, is what makes Blender print Ctrl M beside it — the same rule that governs every other entry in this menu. The separator it brought let the selection-tools block drop its own.

    24. 🔴 The Hotkeys page lists every bound chord. preferences/ui_draw_hotkeys.py carried a hand-written allow-list of ten operator ids and a parallel label dict; eight later bindings never reached it — tks.smart_undo, tks.smart_redo, tks.open_tree_context_menu (twice), tks.copy_vl_settings, tks.paste_vl_settings, tks.global_select_all, tks.global_multiselect, tks.vsw_live_key_guard, tks.view_icon_sheet — so the reader could neither see nor rebind them. Replaced by one module-level HOTKEY_SECTIONS table. The table sets the row ORDER too: it used to be keymap registration order, which is an accident of which module registered first.

    25. 🔴 Seven accordions instead of one. New expand_hotkeys_add/select/visibility/menu/undo/other BoolProperties beside the existing expand_hotkeys_actions (renamed "List Actions" → "Row Actions", the property name kept so utils/manual_map.py and the wiki anchor stay valid); all seven added to the Shift+Click fold group in addon_prefs_constants.py, to prefs_search.py's HOTKEYS section list, and to SECTION_EXTRA so a search for "Select All" opens the section holding it. Other defaults CLOSED: rebinding either row in it has a cost the label cannot carry — the keying guard has to sit on the same key that inserts a keyframe, and the icon sheet ships bound to nothing on purpose. Eleven German keys added.
    26. 🔴 The ratchet grew a second half. test_every_bound_shortcut_is_rebindable reads HOTKEY_SECTIONS with ast — not a substring search, which is how the first version of this file went blind — and fails when a bound id has no row. test_the_page_lists_nothing_stale guards the other direction. _PIE_LISTED exempts tks.invoke_keyframe_pie: the Pie Shortcuts accordion draws it with its own reader, because wm.call_menu_pie is one id for four pies and the operator id alone cannot name which.
    27. 🔴 The Hotkeys page rows were never translatable, and the guard said so. HOTKEY_SECTIONS held its row names as bare literals in a tuple, and _variant_label returned three more from a function body. dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py reads the texts/ package wholesale and reads nothing but name= / text= literals anywhere else, so those labels never entered the English catalogue - which made Redo, Live Apply Key Guard, Duplicate (Linked), Row Menu (Right Click) and Row Menu (Click) read as ORPHANS in de_DE.py: German written for an English source the harvester cannot see. test_no_orphan_translations caught all five plus List Actions, a section title renamed to Row Actions whose German entry was simply dead and is deleted. All 22 row names now live in texts/tooltips_preferences.py as LABEL_HOTKEY_* and are named from both the table and prefs_search.SECTION_EXTRA, so the words a reader types into the search cannot drift from the rows they match. The second half of the bug: _draw_custom_kmi does row.label(text=name) with a VARIABLE, and Blender only translates a literal it can see at draw time, so every row would have stayed English even once harvested. One pgettext_iface(name) fixes all of them. Every one of the 22 already had German, so nothing new landed in the untracked ledger. Confirmed with the full suite: the run that found this was 1 failed / 2985 passed; the impacted re-run is 843/843.
    28. 🔴 The key-only exemptions moved into the source as # MAINT-13-OK: <reason> sentinels. They lived only in dev/tests/test_shortcut_reachability.py's EXEMPT table, which the auditor cannot read, so a scan reported eight bound keys as undiscoverable that had every one been argued through - two guards asking one question and disagreeing in public. Sentinels now sit at the eight bindings (tks.smart_undo, tks.smart_redo, tks.open_tree_context_menu, tks.vsw_live_key_guard, tks.global_add_menu, tks.global_delete, tks.global_new_menu, tks.invoke_keyframe_pie); the auditor now measures MAINT-13 0 unreachable of 20 bound and MAINT-14 0 silent of 7 keyed buttons. The placement bit once: the scanner reads the binding line and THREE lines above it, no more, and the first pass put the token at the top of a seven-line comment - six of the eight stayed invisible. The token line has to TOUCH the binding, prose above it. A new test, test_every_exempt_binding_carries_its_sentinel, pins that: every EXEMPT entry must carry the token within three lines of one of its bindings, so the table and the source cannot drift apart again. The scan fixture now returns its trees so the test does not walk the addon a second time.
    29. 🟢 List focus is claimed by the reader's CLICK, not by a panel's draw. New core/list_focus.py: a table of the twelve clickable lists, each with the WindowManager index property that identifies it, plus claim / current_key / current_family / claimer. Focus used to be wm.tks_active_list_context = "CONTEXT" written inside draw_tree_view, and two other panels did the same. The property's own description says "which list the user last interacted with" and it never meant that - it meant which panel drew LAST, decided by panel order and which tabs are open. With the tags panel below the tree, Ctrl+N added a view layer however long the reader had been working in tags. Every one of these lists is a template_list over a WM index, and Blender fires that property's update= when a row is clicked, which is the only honest click signal in the Python API - there is no "which UIList is under the mouse". claimer(key, then) wraps the five existing callbacks so they keep running, claim first. _list_context in ops_global_shortcuts.py now reads current_family(), and a new _list_key returns the exact list.
    30. 🟢 Two values, because there are two questions. tks_active_list_context stays AMBIENT (written at draw, answers "what is on screen") and the new tks_active_list_key is CLICKED (answers "what did the reader use"). Removing the draw writes was tried and reverted the same hour: draw_tag_library_panel sets the context precisely because the tag operators' polls read it through _resolve_active_tag_item, and a panel that draws their buttons without it leaves every one of them greyed - a bug reported once already and written into the code in place. current_family() prefers the click and falls back to ambient, so a shortcut pressed before any click still lands somewhere sane. The five SPLIT_* keys share the CONTEXT family on purpose - a shortcut asking "am I in the context tree?" must say yes for all five - while keeping distinct keys, which is exactly the split-view blind spot list-focus-dispatch named. Read-only lists (debug log, process monitor, profiler, capture coverage, property patterns) are deliberately absent: a claim there would let a shortcut fire where it can do nothing.
    31. 🔴 tks_inspector_slots_index had no update= at all, so clicking a slot row was invisible to the addon; it claims now. Known gap, left deliberately: clicking the row that is ALREADY active fires no update, so the clicked value does not move - the ambient fallback covers the common shape of that, and an operator may call claim directly when it must be certain. dev/tests/test_list_focus.py (16 pure tests) pins the table, the value-guard against callback loops, the fallback order, and three source checks: the panels still write ambient, nothing outside core/list_focus writes the clicked key, and every list in the table is actually wired to a claimer - a list in the table with no wiring reads as focusable and silently never claims, the quietest possible failure. Cost one Blender run: four of the five wiring sites used claimer with no import, which is one NameError at register and read as 236 failed / 95 errors across unrelated files. An undefined-name sweep over the touched files now precedes the run - the auditor's CORR-11 is the same check.
    32. 🔴 One row menu and one button, for three lists instead of one. TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu keeps its id and its home - renaming a menu the reader has already learned buys nothing - but _active_item now goes through core.list_focus.active_item, so the menu shows the row that was clicked in whatever list it was clicked in. Same for the OPENER: operators/context/ops_tree_context_menu.py had its own copy of the takes-tree lookup, and its poll requires an active row, so the menu would have refused to open over the tag library however many entries it had for it. New ui/styles.row_menu_button(col) draws the dropdown - layout.menu, never an operator, because only a Menu subclass gets the bound key printed beside its entries, and a menu button is a PULLDOWN so Blender opens no property context menu on it. The takes tree's own hand-rolled col.menu(...) now calls the helper, so there is one place that decides the icon. ROW_MENU_ID is a literal there rather than an import: ui sits below panels in the layer order.
    33. 🟢 Which entries appear is decided per FAMILY, from a table that cannot lie. _FAMILY_ENTRIES gives TAGS (rename / group / ungroup / retarget) and VARIANTS (rename / duplicate) their sets; the takes tree deliberately keeps its hand-written set, because three of its entries are special in ways a table cannot express - the duplicate PAIR sets linked on each half, and copy/paste collection visibility appear in both multi-select modes for opposite reasons. dev/tests/test_list_row_menu.py (13 pure tests) parses _FAMILY_ENTRIES and the dispatchers in ops_global_shortcuts.py and fails when a table entry names an operator with no branch for that family - such an entry draws un-greyed and does nothing, which is worse than no entry. Delete is in no table, same ruling as the tree: every one of these lists already has a - beside it. _multiselect_on reads _family(), the same helper draw uses, because two readers of "which list is this?" drift. Cost: the menu now depends on session state, so the seventeen tree-menu tests passed alone and failed in the suite - an earlier test left a focus claim behind and the menu drew the tag set. An autouse fixture pins the focus to CONTEXT and restores it. 1061/1061 impacted tests pass.
    34. 🔴 Show Active / Comma is REMOVED, and the row menu can no longer fail in silence. The feature is gone in full - operator, 3D View keymap item, menu entry, Hotkeys row, refocus/list_id_for, the tks_list_refocus_token property and five German entries. It could not work and could not even say so: Blender exposes no way to scroll a template_list (uiList.list_scroll is C-only, and the one door - a changed active index - fires this addon's view-layer switch), and Blender declines to print a key beside a menu entry for an item bound in the 3D View keymap, which is where the binding had to live because COMMA is Blender's own there. A key that neither works nor names itself is the dead key this card exists to remove, not add. In its place, evidence: Blender SWALLOWS an exception raised inside Menu.draw and shows an empty box, which is why two rounds of "the menu is empty" were guesswork. draw is now a wrapper that logs its class, LIST_KEY and FAMILY, delegates to _draw_body, and on any exception writes the traceback with force=True (it lands with every switch off) and draws "Menu error - see the Takes log" on screen. The opener logs its poll result and which menu it calls. Topic UI / subtopic Hotkeys.
    35. 🟢 The split view's private focus tracker folds into core.list_focus, and two dead branches come alive. tks_split_last_active_list was a second tracker for one question, written from _on_scenes_index_changed, _on_viewlayers_index_changed and _on_take_index_changed - three of the split view's FIVE lists. _on_sg_index_changed and _on_vlg_index_changed never wrote it, so the SCENE_GROUPS and VL_GROUPS branches of _resolve_active_item could not be reached: click a scene group, press Delete or Retarget, and the resolver answered with whichever list HAD written - usually the scene. core.list_focus claims from all five (the claimer wrappers landed in entry 46), so the resolver now reads current_key(wm) through a _SPLIT_LIST_OF table and every branch is reachable. The table exists because this module has spelled them SCENES / VIEWLAYERS / TAKES / SCENE_GROUPS / VL_GROUPS since long before there was a tracker, and renaming five branches to match SPLIT_* buys nothing. The property is deregistered, its three writes are gone, and _on_take_index_changed is now an empty then kept for shape. Two tests pin it: the tracker cannot come back, and the resolver's table must equal the SPLIT_* keys in core/list_focus - a missing row there is exactly how the old one failed. Cost one run: removing the property removed its name= string, orphaning the German entry; the i18n guard caught it.
    36. 🔴 One row menu per list, and the button names its own. Reported with a screenshot: the menu opened over the VARIANTS tree showing the takes tree's header ("View Layer: blue"), Copy Collection Visibility and the rest. Root cause: the menu worked out which list it was for at draw time from current_key, and current_key was stale - clicking a row that is ALREADY highlighted fires no update callback, so the last claim was a click in the tree from minutes earlier. TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu now declares LIST_KEY / FAMILY and is the BASE for TKS_MT_TagRowMenu and TKS_MT_VariantRowMenu, which declare their own; _active_item(key) and _multiselect_on read the menu's own list rather than asking which was clicked. styles.row_menu_button(col, menu_id) takes the menu id, and each panel passes its own - a button drawn by a panel KNOWS which list it sits beside, so it cannot open another's. Shift+RMB still has to choose (Blender exposes no "which UIList is under the mouse") and chooses by the last claim, which is the best available answer for a keyboard route.
    37. 🟢 The keyboard route stops guessing which list it is for. Reported within the hour: Shift+RMB in the TREE opened an empty menu. TKS_OT_OpenTreeContextMenu.invoke had just been taught to pick a menu from current_family, and the last claim was still VARIANTS from a minute earlier - so the variant menu opened over an empty variant list and drew "No row selected", in the one list that certainly had a row. Blender exposes no "which UIList is under the mouse", so a keyboard route CANNOT know, and this one stops pretending: MENU is the takes tree's, which is what this chord has always been. Its _active_item asks active_item(wm, "CONTEXT") by name too, so a selection in another list cannot let the tree's menu open with nothing to act on. Every other list reaches its own menu through the button in its column, which knows because a panel drew it. Two tests pin it, including one that fails if _MENU_OF ever comes back.
    38. 🟢 The row menus stop subclassing each other. Giving the tag library and the variant tree their own menus was done by subclassing TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu, which is a REGISTERED bpy.types.Menu. The takes tree's menu then opened empty. The traces added for exactly this said where: open row menu poll: tree row = Global and open row menu: calling TKS_MT_tree_context_menu are both in the log, and the row menu draw: line that is the first statement of draw never appears - so Blender resolved the id, called nothing, and showed a blank box. Blender registers a Python subclass of an already-registered class as a new RNA type derived from the first, and the three ids stopped resolving to the right draw. The shared code is now a plain-Python mixin, _RowMenu, with NO RNA of its own, and each of the three menus is a DIRECT bpy.types.Menu that mixes it in. The mixin carries CONTEXT defaults so its helpers can be read straight off it by a harness; every real menu declares its own, and a test fails if one stops. This is also the fault that made six rounds of reader reports meaningless: the extension junction pointed at main, and later at another session's worktree, so nothing built here had ever been in the Blender doing the reporting. The junction is now on this worktree - check it BEFORE asking anyone to test.
    39. 🟢 One dropdown per list. The variant column had TWO chevrons side by side - the new row menu and the old TKS_MT_VSW_ProductsSettings - saying different things with the same icon. _RowMenu gains a _list_settings(layout) hook that does nothing by default; TKS_MT_VariantRowMenu overrides it to draw the Show Columns props at the foot of its own menu, and the second col.menu(...) is gone from features/variant_switch/panel.py. The class stays registered - the Variants sub-list still uses its sibling.
    40. 🟢 Shift+RMB picks the list that actually has a row. Both simple rules were reported wrong within the hour: the last claim alone opened an EMPTY variant menu while the reader was in the tree, and always-the-tree gave the variant list a view-layer header and Copy Collection Visibility. _menu_for now takes the claimed key's menu only when active_item finds a row in that list, and falls back to the tree otherwise - a stale claim is nearly always a claim on a list that has since emptied. _active_item walks the same order, so the poll can neither allow a menu that opens empty nor refuse one that would have been fine.
    41. 🟢 The gap belongs to the button. styles.row_menu_button draws its own col.separator() before the menu, so the row menu is never flush against the - that deletes - a destructive button and a menu one mis-click apart. It was three call sites and three chances to forget, and the tag library had already forgotten. The variant column's own separator is dropped so it does not read as a double gap, and a test fails if a caller adds one back.
    42. 🟢 One order, every list: multi-select first, rename last (user ruling 2026-09-01). The takes tree already opened with the mode switch; the table path did the opposite, drawing rename at the top and the selection tools at the foot. _selection_tools is now the first call in BOTH paths and drops its leading separator (the header drew one), and a new _rename helper is the only place that draws rename, at the end of both. _FAMILY_ENTRIES no longer lists rename at all - _table_actions filters it out as well, so a list that lists it cannot draw it twice - and four tests hold the rule in both paths, including one that fails if rename is written anywhere but _rename. Two draw paths were two chances to hold the rule in one and lose it in the other. Cost one red run: _rename first drew through a constant, layout.operator(cls._RENAME[0], ...), and the shortcut ratchet walks .operator() arguments for a string it can RESOLVE - an id handed in through a constant is invisible to it, exactly the blindness the auditor's MAINT-13 carries. The draw uses the literal; only the table filter reads the constant, and a test now asserts the literal is there.
    43. 🟢 Blender DOES say which list the mouse is over, and the chord uses it. Two rounds were built around the opposite assumption. A diagnostic in a running Blender settled it: an operator fired over a template_list gets context.property = (owner, 'tks_vsw_tree_index', -1) - the widget under the cursor, and for a list row that is the list's ACTIVE INDEX, which is the identity core/list_focus is keyed by. New hovered_key(context) maps it through KEY_OF_INDEX_PROP. context.ui_list is set too and names the UIList class, but the index property is the better key: two panels can draw the same UIList class and cannot share an index property. _menu_for and the poll now read hovered -> clicked -> tree, in that order, and the chord CLAIMS the hovered list so the menu, its dispatchers and the next shortcut all agree. The diagnostic that found this is removed, as promised when it went in. It also cost four rounds of false reports: the launcher runs a PRIVATE profile, so its log is under .sandboxes/profiles/<repo>--<worktree>/scripts/presets/..., not the real one - the log being read was a different session's entirely.
    44. 🟢 Rule mode gets its own titled menu. draw_tag_library_mode draws ONE list for both Globals modes, over one collection and one index property, so nothing about the list distinguishes them and hovered_key correctly answers TAGS for both. Only the NAME differs, and a menu titled "Tag" over a list headed "Rules" is the kind of small wrongness that makes a reader doubt the rest. TKS_MT_RuleRowMenu is the same LIST_KEY and FAMILY as the tag menu - same rows, same entries - with bl_label = "Rule". The panel passes it when mode == 'RULES' (a panel knows which mode it drew), and the chord reads wm.tks_globals_mode through a small _MODE_MENU table, because the Globals mode is the only thing that CAN tell the two apart. No new German: both words were already in the catalogue.
    45. 🟢 The five split-view lists get menus, and they are the tree's. Same family, so every tks.global_* dispatcher already serves them and _resolve_active_item has resolved split rows since long before this menu existed - only the KEY differs, and it is what lets the header name the row. core.list_focus.active_item gained a resolver per split list (_ROW_RESOLVER), because their rows are Blender's own data rather than a wm collection: bpy.data.scenes, a scene's view_layers, a version set's versions, and the two group collections on the World. Each returns a tiny two-field Row, NOT the datablock - the menu reads item_type and name and nothing else, and handing it a real Scene would invite something later to hold RNA across ticks. The resolver catches its own lookup errors: a menu that cannot name its row draws "No row selected", one that RAISES draws an empty box, and that cost a day.
    46. 🟢 The inspector's three lists get menus of their OWN operators. No shared dispatcher has an INSPECTOR branch, so the entry rule widened: a table entry may be a shared dispatcher (which must have a branch for that family, still checked) or a list's own operator (which answers for itself). The watchlist offers Find Action/Slot and Convert to Override; Actions and Slots have exactly one button each and it is the - in their column, so they get the multi-select block and nothing else. HAS_RENAME = False on the inspector base, because tks.global_rename has no branch for them and would be the un-greyed dead entry this menu keeps not having. _FAMILY_ENTRIES is keyed by LIST KEY now, not family: the three inspector lists share a family and want different things.
    47. 🟢 The render queue has no row menu, and that is a decision. Its column holds one button - a settings popover for the whole list - and its rows are queued renders. Nothing to rename, group, retarget or duplicate about one, so a menu there would carry the multi-select block and nothing else. Written into tree_context_menu.py beside the class list so nobody adds it back by symmetry.
    48. 🟢 The inspector's three columns get one dropdown each again. Adding a row menu beside an existing settings menu put two identical chevrons side by side doing different jobs - the same fault reported for the variant column, repeated three times. The _list_settings hook now draws each list's settings INSIDE its row menu: Actions and Slots call TKS_MT_ActionsSettings.draw / TKS_MT_SlotsSettings.draw with our own layout, so the Show Columns props and the clean-up operators keep ONE definition; the watchlist's settings are a popover rather than a menu and cannot be drawn inline, so the entry that opens it sits at the foot instead. A test walks every column that has a row menu and fails on a second DOWNARROW_HLT.
    49. 🟢 The chord refuses over a list this addon does not own. hovered_key answers "" for the debug log, the process monitor and the profiler - they are output, not data, and are deliberately absent from LISTS - and the fallback chain then opened the TAKES TREE's menu over a list of log lines. New hovering_a_foreign_list(context) separates "on a list we do not own" from "not on a list at all" using context.ui_list, which Blender sets only over a list; the poll refuses the first and keeps the fallback for the second, which is what makes the chord work from a panel's empty space (user ruling 2026-09-01).
    50. 🟢 View Layer marker style (Socket / Box), Box shipped as the default. tks_vl_icon_style (WindowManager) mirrored by default_vl_icon_style (ListHeightsPropsMixin), the usual live/saved pair, so it rides the existing _TREE_MAP loop in BOTH preferences/ops_addon_ui.py and preferences/persistence_io.py rather than growing new plumbing. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 815 -> 816. SOCKET keeps template_node_socket + KEYFRAME; BOX draws PIVOT_BOUNDBOX / SHADING_BBOX. Blender cannot tint a plain icon=, so tks_active_vl_color is greyed out under BOX in BOTH settings surfaces (preferences/draw_interface.py, the Tree Design popover) rather than left looking live. Two draw sites: panels/context/draw_layers.draw_vl and features/variant_switch/ui_row_renderers. Enum items are inlined at both property definitions, not shared from a constant - dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py only harvests enum labels from a literal items=[...] INSIDE a *Property() call, so a shared constant makes every label an untranslatable orphan; test_both_sides_offer_the_same_two_choices pins the two lists against drift instead. Tests: dev/tests/test_vl_icon_style.py (13), including an icon-literal guard against Blender's icon-enum drift.
    51. 🟢 View layer rows carry a kind icon beside the name. GREASEPENCIL_LAYER_GROUP when the layer holds takes, OUTLINER_DATA_GP_LAYER when it does not. Reads the same has_versions answer the expand chevron already uses, so glyph and chevron cannot disagree. Dims with its row (_ms_name_dim / _tag_dim / not active), because a bright glyph on a filtered-out row reads as "this one is selected".
    52. 🟢 The Rules and Tags sections drew nothing, and nothing said so. panels/globals_panel.py calls tag_library_ui.draw_tag_library_mode(...) through the PACKAGE, and the large-file split had trimmed panels/tag_library_ui/__init__.py down to from .draw import TKS_MT_TagAddMenu - so both modes raised AttributeError on every draw. Blender SWALLOWS what a panel's draw raises and shows an empty panel, so no test, no log line and no error reported it; it was found by a reader navigating to a panel that was not there. Present on main BEFORE this branch merged (git show 99c0d419:... has the trimmed line) and carried through the merge, which took main's side of that hunk. The export is restored with a note saying why it is public. New dev/tests/test_panel_package_exports.py walks every <package>.<attr>(...) call in panels/ and fails when the package does not export the name - the check that could have caught this the day it broke.

    Changed¶

    1. 🔴 Internal: six duplicated code paths collapsed to one implementation each; verified dead code removed. Behaviour-neutral except where noted. operators/inspector/ops_slots.py — select_all/invert_selection were mirror twins over their first two thirds (= True vs = not <lvalue>); folded into _walk_visible(context, list_type, decide) with a module-level _FILTER_TO_CAT (the two copies were byte-identical) and the cloned dead categories_with_matches deleted. The CONTEXT tails stay separate — invert's seen_* dedup bookkeeping is required semantics, not duplication. ai/api.py — five verbs (switch_take, delete_take, rename_take, create_take, explain) opened with the same scene+VL resolution; _resolve_scene_vl returns (scene_obj, vl_obj, None) or (None, None, envelope) with BYTE-IDENTICAL codes/messages/hints (facade contract AI-04). _resolve_tier_target's near-miss (dict-wrapped envelope, different wording) is pinned as deliberately separate. core/cascade.py — _write_world_record/_write_camera_record were verbatim twins apart from the recursion flag, resolve_world_adopt_target/resolve_camera_adopt_target apart from a pref name and two prop names; now _write_tier_record(..., flag_attr=) + _resolve_adopt_target(kind, ...) over a 3-string table, all four public names kept as wrappers (external callers in ops_apply_scene_camera.py/ops_apply_scene_world.py). is_world_reconciling/is_camera_reconciling stay DISTINCT — a shared flag would let one write silence the other's callback. Everything stays module-local (R-HOT-PATH-COHESION). panels/context/draw_layers.py — draw_take and draw_vl each spelled their 7-column icon cluster twice; AST-compared with the pin conjunct/overflow/import-placement stripped (draw_vl identical; draw_take differed only in where take_has_variant is imported), then merged behind wm.tks_show_X and (_draw_all or wm.tks_pin_X) with _draw_all = not collapsed per row — same two attribute reads per column, no new call, no string building on the draw path. -138 lines. take↔vl NOT merged (~0.40 similar: different data sources, idnames, alert logic). features/batch_render/process_manager.py — 107 identical lines across BGRenderManager.poll/FastBGRenderManager.poll (incl. a 30-line byte-exact run) hoisted to _drain_stdout/_apply_engine_line/_apply_status_line on the base, with _on_task_start/_on_task_done/_on_task_error hooks carrying the real deltas (Fast learns active_task from the worker's start line, pops the queue, clears on done/error) and _LOG_LABEL keeping "BG"/"Fast BG" distinct in the render log. The process-exit tails stay separate — genuinely different lifecycles. Dead code swept: preferences/persistence_io.py (unused webbrowser/Operator/StringProperty/4 OP_* constants, duplicate function-local import json, write-only _project_prefs_warning global — get_project_prefs_warning() checks the path on disk each call; ops_addon_ui.py:391 had a second copy with no reader either), core/vl_lifecycle.py (commented-out V1 sequential pipeline; seven from .event_bus import emit, X lines collapsed to one), duplicate import lines in mirror_logic.py/sync_viewport.py/ops_action.py/ops_camera_levels.py, panels/inspector/handlers.py's import of three names it never used, ops_crud.py's zero-caller _get_existing_override stub, tag_library.py's dangling "Rebuild full tag cache" comment (no cache in that module; the rename already propagates every reference), and 84 try: <call> except ImportError: pass guards whose try body contains no import — a call raises NameError, never ImportError, so the guard could never catch anything (persistence_io.py:381 already made the same call unguarded two lines above a guarded one). Unwrapping used an AST filter restricted to a verified-safe callee set; every one of those callees either imports nothing or handles its own ImportError internally (event_bus.emit, providers.query), and any try containing an import was left alone. KEPT by prior decision: _apply_preview_cascades, the preview_bg plumbing (lost-feature suspect, own ticket), rename_scene_in_ledgers + its caller. New characterisation tests land BEFORE each fold: test_multiselect_walk.py (7), test_ai_scene_vl_preamble.py (4), test_cascade_world_camera_twins.py (7), test_bg_poll_dispatch.py (10). Auditor AST-only scan, main -> branch: CORR-20 Impossible Except Guard 85->1, CORR-19 Phantom Deferred Import 47->44, CORR-21 Never-Filled Collection 2->1, CORR-22 Loop-Variable Capture 1->0, CORR-23 Write-Only Local 2->0, CORR-24 Unknown ID-Type Literal 1->0, MAINT-11 Clone Code 2269->2225, MAINT-09 Import Hygiene 829->805, MAINT-10 Commented-Out Code 2->1, MAINT-03 135->133; quality score 2.05 -> 3.00. Branch fix/spaghetti-cleanup, commits 8545ed22..068679bb.
    2. 🟢 The preset change tip says that Accept or Revert resolves the change, not saving the file. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-27.) texts/infoboxes.py's INFOBOX_PRESET_CHANGES_SCOPE read "Changes are kept per scene until saved or reverted.", drawn by panels/navigation/warnings/presets_changes.py:63. "saved" reads as Ctrl+S, which resolves nothing: there is no pending-change store at all — features/render_presets/preset_state.get_preset_diffs:479 recomputes the diff on every redraw from the preset JSON (load_preset_cached → serialization/crud.load_preset:242) against live RNA (preset_engine._capture_for_type), and features/render_presets/ registers no save_pre/save_post/load_post handler (the only save_pre registrants are core/cache_version.py, core/store_guardian.py, core/vl_lifecycle.py:511 and utils/keymap_audit.py, none of which touch preset state). So wm.save_mainfile is a strict no-op for preset dirtiness and the warning returns byte-identical after a reload. The only writers are tks.update_render_preset (ops_manage_crud.py:117) and tks.save_all_dirty_presets (ops_manage_sync.py:104), both overwriting the JSON in the preset's own tier (decode_preset_key → find_preset_tier → 'USER'), so Accept carries cross-scene / cross-file blast radius; tks.revert_to_preset re-applies the preset onto the scene. New wording names both buttons. texts/locales/de_DE.py re-keyed in lockstep (a texts edit that leaves the old key behind trips test_i18n_guard); the entry keeps its alphabetical slot and reuses the button translations Übernehmen / Zurücksetzen. Commit 0388c101.
    3. 🟢 The changelog is split into a working pair and an append-only archive, and the release cut is a script. The 0.8.0 cut was a ~400-line manual text move and it went wrong: the ## [0.7.11] - 2026-07-12 heading ended up ABOVE the last twenty dev Fixed entries instead of below them, so six weeks of August work sat under a July release with no ### Fixed header, numbered 90-109 a second time — Fixed 90 named two different fixes in one release. Neither file looked wrong while reading it. The split. Entries are written in CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED.md / CHANGELOG_UNRELEASED_DEV.md. CHANGELOG.md / CHANGELOG_DEV.md keep their names (GitHub and the shipped ZIP expect a complete CHANGELOG.md) and become append-only, with a pointer where their Unreleased block was. The cut. New dev/scripts/release_cut.py is the only thing that appends to an archive: it refuses unless the working pair is a valid mirror (same sections, same counts, contiguous 1..N), inserts one dated block into each archive, empties the working pair, and re-stamps the freeze lock. --dry-run prints without writing. The freeze. check_changelog_mirror.py digests every released block into dev/changelog_archive.lock; a shipped block that no longer matches fails the commit with "shipped notes were edited after release". The mirror and numbering checks moved onto the working pair, where drift starts and a fix is still cheap. check_changelog_terse.py defaults to the working file and falls back to the archive for an older checkout. 11 tests in dev/tests/test_changelog_split.py cover all three, including the 0.8.0 failure itself as test_editing_a_shipped_release_fails.

    4. 🟢 The unreleased user entries are a TIGHT list again. A blank line between two items makes Markdown render a LOOSE list - each entry wrapped in its own paragraph, with a gap around it. Every block before 0.8.0 is tight; 0.8.0 itself shipped with 39 blank lines between entries and the unreleased block had drifted to spaced throughout, so one document rendered two ways. 14 blank lines removed, and check_changelog_terse.spacing_offences() now refuses a commit that puts one back. The archive was normalised in the same pass — 44 blank lines out of CHANGELOG.md (39 in 0.8.0, which shipped spaced while every older block was tight, plus 5 strays among the pre-marker **Bold** entries), with all 1175 entry lines asserted byte-identical before and after and dev/changelog_archive.lock re-stamped. That is a deliberate one-off: the freeze refused it first, which is the guard working. The rule is pointed at the user file only: the dev mirror's entries are multi-line paragraphs that Markdown would run together without the blank line. +3 tests.

    5. 🔴 sequencer_follow_enabled default flipped False → True (user ruling 2026-08-27). Follow the Playhead is what applies the strip's take under the playhead (handlers.poll_follow + on_frame_change); shipping it off read in the field as "the merged feature does not work" — the in-app report that triggered this was scrubbing with no view-layer switch, traced to the pref being off, not to a defect. The caution that shipped it off is covered elsewhere: sequencer_cache_off (ships ON, consulted only while the follow is on) guards the stale-frame footgun, and the write paths honour the mutation locks. One-line default + comment rewrite in preferences/props/props_automations.py; no prop added, so no prefs-version bump. Existing profiles keep their saved value — the autosave JSON overrides the default, so only fresh installs see the change. New pin test_sequencer_follow.py::test_the_follow_ships_on (red before the flip, green after, verified against the worktree code via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS); no test pinned the old default.

    6. 🟢 The View Layer properties tab shows one Takes presets panel instead of two. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-28.) TKS_PT_ViewLayerPresetsStandalone in features/render_presets/panels_ui.py drew the same styles.preset_row(..., 'viewlayer', 'viewlayer_preset', apply_only=True) that panels_helpers.draw_viewlayer_preset_header:39 already prepends onto Blender's native View Layer panel, so the tab carried two identical preset rows. Removed: the class, its entry in the classes tuple, its import in panels.py, and the now-unused 'TKS View Layer Presets' key from texts/locales/_pending.py KEEP_ENGLISH (a texts edit that leaves a dead key behind trips test_i18n_guard). No surviving reference to the idname or the class anywhere in the tree. Branch fix/drop-dup-viewlayer-preset-panel (commit 9f1685b9) sat 111 commits behind main; the replay-onto-main path is denied by the harness permission layer, so main was merged INTO the branch (9c4849c9) and main was then fast-forwarded onto it. Full headless suite run against the merged code via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS (the extension junction was left pointing at main - the user's Blender was live): 2587 passed, 1 skipped.
    7. 🟢 Find Action/Slot modifiers: scene/world moves Alt -> Shift, Alt takes the follow toggle. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-29.) TKS_OT_FindActionSlot.invoke branched on event.alt for Scene/World/World Nodes (the only route to them, since they are not objects and the plain branch reads context.active_object). They are watchlist rows now (panels/inspector/sync.py, synthetic prefixes, gated on _id_has_any_action), so the follow reaches them by row — but the direct one-click jump is kept as convenience and moved to event.shift rather than retired, which also means no route is lost (iter_anim_targets(world) still yields the world node tree). event.alt now flips wm.tks_follow_selection and reports the new state. Docstring, module header, wiki (interface/hotkeys.md + interface/inspector_panel.md) and de_DE updated in lockstep. Ships WITH Added 5 — a standalone gesture move would cost muscle memory for no gain.
    8. 🔴 UI vocabulary pass: INFO-18 197 findings -> 0. Every edit driven by the rule's own findings (file+line+literal), so only the exact reader-facing strings it named were rewritten - no property identifier, no bl_idname, no RNA path moved (naming standard section 7). Terms: View Layer (was ViewLayer/VL/View-Layer, 93), Folder (Directory), Configuration (Config), Settings (Options), Data-block (datablock), Watchlist (Actions List), Autokey. Verbs: 27 Create X -> New X; Drop & Re-apply -> Revert & Re-apply (Revert already names that act in the same feature's drift warning). Collisions settled by MEANING, not by picking one word - Clear empties an assignment, Remove takes a thing out of its list, Delete destroys it: Remove Action said permanently in its own docstring so it is now Delete Action (matching the confirm pref already named that); Delete Selected/Clear Selected keep their verbs but name their object (... Items / ... Properties); Delete Item -> Delete Tag or Group; token keeps both words for its two acts. tks.remove_slot RETIRED - it duplicated tks.delete_slot (same confirm gate, same multiselect, same targets) and was drawn nowhere and bound to no key; class, registration and manual-map row removed. Five tooltips stopped leaking a property name at the reader (vl.use -> 'render icon'). Protected, not renamed: {viewlayer} naming-template tokens and the 'directory' option identifier - added to the glossary allow list, since renaming those breaks what the user must type. Glossary also gained verb_collision_allow (auditor commit 0568fad) for the three legitimate pairs. de_DE re-keyed in the same commit for all ~150 changed strings (orphan+untranslated guards green). Suite 2762 passed; INFO-18 re-scan 0 findings / 7 exempt over 4134 strings. Field rounds after the first build closed four interaction defects the unit tests could not reach: the viewport route never followed at all (sync_viewport sets the row inside the _syncing_objects_list guard, which silenced the index callback - the sync now runs _follow_selection itself); Scene/World rows could not be clicked (Pass 2 re-pointed the watchlist whenever the row name differed from the active object, and a synthetic name never matches - it now reacts to _last_synced_active changing); a World animated on its NODE TREE looked unanimated (_animated_target prefers the row's own action, else walks iter_anim_targets_only, the same list the button walks); and a plain click died on a Scene/World row after that row deliberately cleared the viewport (_selected_special_row_id supplies the source, active object otherwise). Also: depressed button state, dynamic multi-line description, canonical name 'Follow Selection' pinned to the pref's own label by test, pref moved to its own open Inspector section (expand_auto_inspector, EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 571), jump selects the matching watchlist row, and a REST/UI log line per follow. 28 tests; suite 2762 passed.

    9. 🔴 Report messages brought onto the glossary, and their plural glue split. INFO-18 read only declared labels, so a clean 0-finding scan said nothing about the status line an operator writes into the info area — a string a reader reads exactly like a label. The rule gained a report_msg harvest site (auditor branch feat/info-18-report-terms, e520a81; terms only, since a status line is a sentence: "Created 3 takes" is not a Create button), and Takes immediately reported 29 findings over 4892 strings where every other site kind reported none. All 29 fixed here across 15 files: VL(s) 13, directory 7, ViewLayer 5, config 1. Fourteen of those sites carried (s) plural glue, which [[project_multi_language_support]] bans — a translator cannot inflect a phrase around it. Each is now an explicit pair chosen at the call site, pgettext_rpt('… {count} View Layer') if count == 1 else pgettext_rpt('… {count} View Layers'), both literals visible to dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py (a helper would have hidden them: the collector and INFO-10 key on the pgettext_* call-site NAME). Two judgement calls: Rendering {len} VL(s) ({skipped} non-VL ignored) became … ({skipped} ignored) — non-View-Layer re-introduces a banned variant (View-Layer), and a second count in the same sentence would need four templates for one status line; and Removed ViewLayer: {vl_name} merged onto the Removed View Layer: {vl_name} key that already existed, closing the duplicate the German second-witness pass first exposed. de_DE re-keyed in the same commit (section 13.5, no grace period): 27 keys, 13 of them split into a German singular/plural pair, which also removed the mirror-image Ansichtsebene(n) glue. Every German VERB is left exactly as the translator settled it — entfernt where it said entfernt, gelöscht where it said gelöscht — so the act-split ruling merged on main is untouched; only the noun and the plural move. Four German values still reading {count} VL(s) are fixed as a side effect. Guards: orphans() 0, untracked() 0; INFO-18 re-scan 29 → 0 over 4906 strings; suite 2652 passed, 1 skipped, with the four known worktree collection errors. NOT touched, and worth a later card: sibling messages abbreviate VLG and SG (View Layer Group, Scene Group), which the glossary does not know, and (s)/(n) glue survives in strings the rule never looked at, e.g. Cleared action on {count} child(ren).

    10. 🔴 Group abbreviations spelled out, and two strays the new template site exposed. The glossary gained View Layer Group (banning VLG, VL Group, VL-Group, ViewLayer Group) and Scene Group (banning SG), plus the same rows in doc/standards/naming_conventions.md §13.2. Same ruling as the parent term: the short forms only ever appear in a status line or a popover header, never anywhere a reader could learn them. INFO-18 then reported 20 findings, all fixed here. Eight of the twenty were invisible until the rule learned to read a text= that is an EXPRESSION rather than a literal (auditor 6ab9139): four cascade popover headers draw pgettext_iface("Action -- VL Group '%s'") % name, which _str_kwarg could not see. The same pass caught VL Switch Profiler and Timeline Options (→ Timeline Settings, Options is banned) — neither is a group name, both had been drifting in plain sight behind the same blind spot. layout.label(text=f"ViewLayer: {vl.name}") in ops_cascade_layers.py was BOTH the wrong word and the only popover header in its family that was never translated. It is now pgettext_iface("View Layer: %s") % vl.name with a de_DE key, matching its four siblings — a term fix and a translation gap closed in one edit, which is why it is not a separate entry. German moved with it: VLG/SG in translated values became Ansichtsebenen-Gruppe/Szenengruppe — the words the translator already used in Name der Ansichtsebenen-Gruppe and Name der Szenengruppe, so the German half stays one word per thing too. 20 keys touched, 1 added. orphans() 0, untracked() 0; INFO-18 20 → 0 over 5277 strings; suite 2652 passed, 1 skipped.

    11. 🔴 Plural glue swept out of every translated template. Entry 9 split the 14 sites the vocabulary rule happened to report; a tree-wide AST sweep for (s) / (es) / (ren) inside a pgettext_* template found 68 more sites / 62 distinct templates, at labels, confirm dialogs and status lines the rule never looks at. [[project_multi_language_support]] bans the glue outright — a translator cannot inflect a phrase around slot(s), and German has to agree an adjective and a case ending with the same number. All 68 are now explicit pairs picked at the call site, written as two literal pgettext_* calls so the collector and INFO-10 keep seeing them (a npgettext(count, sing, plur) helper would read better and hide every template from the drift guard — the same trap noted under entry 9). Splicing was done on BYTES, since ast reports col_offset in UTF-8 bytes and several templates carry an em dash. Five templates count two different nouns, so each got FOUR templates rather than a reworded English sentence: Saved {len} preset(s), synced {synced} scene(s), the Value Lock capture line, Remove %d slot(s) and %d action(s)?, Removed {len} slot(s) and {len_2} action(s), and Removed {removed_count} object(s) ({removed_slots} slot(s) deleted). Both nouns inflect in German, so 2x2 is the honest shape. preferences/ops_misc.py was already a deliberate on/off pair (two whole sentences, not an interpolated word) and became 2x2 the same way: on/off x one/many. Six German values would have split wrongly and are hand-written: %d Datei existiert bereits. (verb agreement), nicht erfasster Wert / nicht erfasste Werte (adjective ending), %d leeren Slot entfernen? (accusative), and Ruhezustand-Kanal (the translator had written only the plural). Two English strings needed the same care: WARNING: %d file already exists. and Gave {split} object its own slot.     12. 🟢 Build Syntax popup widened: TKS_PT_TokenBuilderPopup.bl_ui_units_x 30 -> 36. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-30.) The token grid is a grid_flow(columns=4, even_columns=True) inside that fixed width, so the four columns split whatever the panel is given and cannot grow past it — a token wider than a quarter of the panel clips to an ellipsis with no other symptom. Shortening the region names bought headroom but left [resolution_percentage] (23 characters with brackets) sitting on the edge, which is the residual shift the user saw. 36 units gives each column ~9 units instead of 7.5. Chosen over the render_jobs_popup_width treatment (a preference plus _apply_panel_width’s unregister/re-register dance in features/batch_render/jobs_popover.py) — that is a real feature with a prefs row, German text and an EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT bump, and is worth its own card if the fixed width ever chafes. The two halves of the bargain are now written down together: the class comment says to raise the width or shorten the name, and test_no_grid_token_name_is_too_long_to_render fails the moment a name outgrows resolution_percentage.

    13. 🟢 resolution_x / resolution_y now report the RAW scene setting; the percentage-scaled value moves to the new _scaled pair. Semantic correction, not a rename. Both tokens have always resolved through the legacy cluster names res_x / res_y, whose bodies are int(r.resolution_x * (r.resolution_percentage / 100)) — so [resolution_x] silently returned the SCALED size while its own registry description said "Resolution X", Blender's property of that name holds the raw value, and Blender's native {resolution_x} (the token ours is declared to BE, via BLENDER_NATIVE_NAMES) resolves raw too. Three sources of truth disagreed with the code. Now resolution_x / resolution_y dispatch on themselves and return str(r.resolution_x); _LEGACY_TOKEN_ALIASES maps resolution_x_scaled → res_x / resolution_y_scaled → res_y instead, so the cluster bodies are untouched and — importantly — a saved path containing the legacy [res_x] keeps resolving to the scaled value it always did (test_legacy_res_x_alias_keeps_the_scaled_meaning pins exactly that, and it was the one test GREEN before the implementation). User-visible risk, stated plainly: a saved render path using [resolution_x] at a resolution percentage other than 100 will now produce a different folder/file name. At 100 % (the default, and what the alias test's other cases cover) nothing moves. test_blender_native_tokens.py's exact-equality assertion on _LEGACY_TOKEN_ALIASES and test_token_builder.py::test_categorized_tokens_search_filters were updated for the new names. (Verified 2026-08-30 by the same live probe: at 1920x1080 and 50 %, resolution_x answered 1920 and resolution_x_scaled answered 960, while the legacy res_x still answered 960 — the back-compat promise holds in the shipped code, not only in a unit test.) Branch feat/more-builtin-tokens, merged 84dfb21a.

    17. 🟢 Tooltip house style — explanation first, shortcuts last, one Key: effect line each. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-30.) Card doc/roadmap/active/tooltip-house-style.md, dev note doc/roadmap/_dev/tooltip-house-style.md. User ruling 2026-08-29, from the Find Action/Slot tooltip: "The tooltip is a one liner. Each function should get its own line. All hotkeys should be at the end of a tooltip." Blender renders \n in a tooltip as a real line break but never wraps a long line — it clips at the popup width — so a one-liner that buries Alt+Click mid-sentence is unreadable by construction. The standard. doc/standards/tooltips.md (normative, sibling of naming_conventions.md): purpose first, shortcut block last, key first then ": " then the effect, one shortcut per line; §2 line length, §3 no trailing period on a line, §4 dynamic tooltips, §5 the # TOOLTIP-OK opt-out for prose that names a gesture rather than offering it, §6 the i18n lockstep, §7 what the guard checks. Static pass. 19 of the 38 modifier-carrying constants in texts/tooltips_*.py were reshaped: tooltips_batch_render.py (5, incl. OP_VLRENDERTOGGLE and the stale (Alt+Click) hint on OP_PREVIEWRENDER, whose operator is code-called only and draws no button), tooltips_context.py (1), tooltips_misc.py (6, incl. OP_VLCOMPOSITORPOPOVER, which used → instead of ": " and leaked "(handled by popover_invoke)" into the user's tooltip), tooltips_preferences.py (4), tooltips_render_presets.py (2), tooltips_slots.py (1). tooltips_inspector.py::OP_FINDACTIONSLOT is NOT among them — entry 7 shipped the reference shape there first, with different keys (Shift+Click for scene/world, Alt+Click for the follow toggle); the merge takes that version whole and this branch only inherits it as the worked example. PROP_MISCPROPSMIXIN_SOUND_FOR_CTRL_CLICK keeps entry 8's wording verbatim and takes the documented # TOOLTIP-OK opt-out instead — the preference names the gesture it is about, not its own shortcut. One sentinel in use, cap five. Dynamic pass. A @classmethod description(cls, context, properties) overrides bl_description entirely, so those operators never show the texts/ constant at all — they were the tooltips users actually read and nothing was checking them. 15 sites reshaped: features/batch_render/ops_utils.py TKS_OT_VLRenderToggle (6 returns — the •-separated one-liner fallback ×3, plus the timestamp / not-rendered / except branches, whose bare Click:/Shift:/Ctrl:/Alt: keys became full chords), features/variant_switch/ops_column_popovers.py (2), ops_crud.py (1), operators/cascade/ops_viewlayer_camera.py (3), operators/cascade/_helpers.py::popover_description (1, the shared helper several cascade popovers delegate to), operators/inspector/ops_datablock_action.py (1), ops_object_action.py (2), operators/misc/ops_cascade_overflow.py (1). These are f-strings over runtime state, so the i18n harvester never sees them — a known translation gap, recorded in §4, not widened here. i18n lockstep. Every reshaped English string IS the translation key, so each edit orphans its texts/locales/de_DE.py entry and would fail test_i18n_guard::test_no_orphan_translations. Verified 0 orphans, 0 untracked, 0 dead-pending, 0 both. Two mechanical traps hit on the way: ast reports col_offset in bytes, so slicing de_DE.py by character offset corrupts every entry on a line containing an umlaut (the first attempt merged 21 entries into their neighbours); and the file is CRLF while git show hands back LF, so a byte-level rewrite must restore CRLF or the whole file shows as changed. The guard. dev/tests/test_tooltip_house_style.py, pytestmark = pytest.mark.pure (pure-Python AST, no bpy, so it collects in the GH Actions pure job). Eight tests over two scanners: module-level string constants in texts/tooltips_*.py (38 name a modifier), and every description() classmethod plus module-level *_description() helper in the addon (18 name a modifier), the latter reconstructing an f-string's wording from its JoinedStr constant chunks with FormattedValue holes as {}. Rules: a modifier-bearing tooltip contains \n; every modifier line matches ^<chord>:; no explanation line follows the shortcut block; OP_FINDACTIONSLOT stays the worked example; at most five # TOOLTIP-OK sentinels. Confirmed RED before the fix (3 of 5 failing, 21 constants listed) and GREEN after. Not done. Card phase 3 — reshaping the remaining long single-line tooltips that carry no shortcut — is a wording pass over ~2,500 lines of constants and stays open on the card; the shape rules do not bite there, and the guard is silent on them by design.     24. 🟢 A Tooltips page in Preferences: two switches and a value style, with a worked example built by the real composer. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-31.) Blender gives an add-on no bold, no colour and no markup inside a tooltip, so line order and omission are the only levers there are; this turns both into the reader's choice instead of one decision made for everybody. show_tooltip_explanation (default True) drops the purpose line and tooltip_state_style (VALUE_FIRST default, PLAIN) chooses whether the state reads above the purpose; both are read lazily through bpy.context.preferences.addons rather than by importing preferences/, since texts/ sits below it and the import would be upward (ARCH-01). The explanation survives whenever nothing else would remain — an empty popup reads as a broken button, not a tidy one. texts/compose.example_tooltip(style, with_keys, with_purpose) builds the preview through the same composer the real tooltips use, so it cannot promise a shape the add-on does not produce. The cascade popovers needed a fix to benefit: operators/cascade/_helpers.popover_description pre-joined purpose and state into one string, so the two beats arrived as one and the order could never be swapped — the style did nothing on exactly the buttons it was built for. A QUOTED style is deliberately absent: compose_tooltip receives the state as one finished string and cannot tell the datablock name from the source that won it, so quoting wrapped the whole line; it returns when the 28 state builders become templates with a {value} hole (doc/roadmap/ideas/half-german-tooltips.md). EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 583 → 586 with each bump's reason recorded in place. Caught by the suite: the eight new strings had no i18n decision, and one of them still described the cut quoted style — English corrected first, German written against the corrected wording. Full headless suite 2754 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Commits 60dc83a8, 03edb9ec.
