A layout.menu() cannot see modifier keys, so the Shift+Click route this replaced would have meant redrawing the control as a plain operator, which loses the menu's dropdown arrow — rejected on sight. The F12 pie entry and render_scope_ops' RENDER_JOBS action still reach the popover directly. 70. 🟢 Shift+F12 opens the Render Jobs popover. Bound in jobs_popover.py on the 'Window' keymap, beside the F12 render-scope pie, so the pair reads as one idea. ADDON keyconfig ONLY — a user-kc bootstrap marks the entry user_defined, and Blender then drops the user's own bindings in that keymap on every enable (the trap the render-scope pie documents at render_scope.py:_register_keymap). _find_kmi matches on kmi.idname, never on the key combo, so a rebound entry is still removed cleanly on uninstall, and it reads no kmi.properties in unregister. A test asserts the entry lands in the addon keyconfig on ('F12', shift) with no other modifier. No tooltip change: Blender prints the shortcut beside the menu entry itself. 71. 🟢 The render menu greys out Render Jobs when it is drawn inside the job list. _draw_render_menu(layout, context, show_jobs=True) now sets row.enabled = show_jobs on that entry, and TKS_MT_RenderMenuInJobs — a SECOND Menu, deliberately not a subclass of TKS_MT_RenderMenu — passes False; the popover's header draws that subclass. A second menu rather than runtime state: a menu draws whenever Blender opens it, long after the host panel's draw returned, so nothing readable at that moment says where the click came from. Greyed rather than hidden so the menu keeps one shape wherever it opens. Registering a subclass of an already registered menu can shadow the parent, which stops the sidebar button opening anything at all — reported from a real session and the reason both are plain Menu subclasses. This was also the only route that could stack a second popover, so no open-state guard is needed — an earlier attempt timed the panel's last draw and was dropped as over-built. Blender exposes no "is this popup open" flag, so a hotkey press while the popup is on screen is still not detectable; it simply is not reachable, because the popup holds the input. 72. 🟢 The header's time read-out is named, and gains elapsed. It was a bare duration between the title and the buttons, which said nothing about what it measured. job_snapshot.time_parts(total_eta, stats, elapsed_str) returns (kind, value) pairs — ('ETA', v) idle, ('ELAPSED', v) and ('LEFT', v) during a batch, each half dropped when it has no value — and TKS_PT_RenderJobs._time_text names them with pgettext_iface("Elapsed {t}") and friends. PAIRS rather than a finished sentence on purpose: the extractor reads literals, so a phrase assembled in the snapshot layer stays English while the i18n guard reports green, which had already happened twice on this branch. elapsed comes from get_batch_progress(wm) through the queue's own format_eta. de_DE entries added. 73. 🟢 The queue ETA appears without opening the Batch Render tab, and survives a running batch. Per-job estimates live in render_queue_engine._display_estimates, which _refresh_display_estimates(wm) rebuilds by walking wm.tks_render_queue — a collection only the Batch Render tab fills. Open the job list in a fresh session and that collection is empty, so every estimate read 0 and snap['total_eta'] came out blank; render_scope_ops._call_batch already carried a comment about the same trap. New job_snapshot.prime_render_queue(context) calls sync_render_queue(wm) from the popover's _open and from tks.render_jobs_rescan — operator context only, since it writes a WindowManager collection and a draw must never do that (sync_render_queue also early-returns during a batch). time_parts now puts ('ETA', ...) FIRST in both states instead of only when idle, so the whole-queue number never vanishes mid-run. 74. 🟢 The per-job ETA column is back. It was dropped in the redraw because every estimate read 0 — the render queue collection the estimates key off was never filled (entry 73) — so the column showed nothing but took width. With that fixed it has content, so a fixed _ETA_UNITS cell sits between the bar and the overflow button, dimmed, carrying job['eta'] from get_display_estimate with its ~ prefix marking a prediction rather than a measurement. Header title 'ETA'; de_DE entry added. 75. 🟢 The queue estimate moved beside the total bar; per-job estimates are boxed. In the header's right-aligned group the rescan button, the _RENDER_BUTTON_UNITS launcher and the width grip squeezed it out entirely — a probe confirmed the value reached the draw and simply had no room. It now sits right of the bar as boxes the width of a job's own estimate (_ETA_BOX_UNITS), so the queue total reads as the same kind of number as the column it lines up with — one box idle, elapsed then remaining while rendering. The naming helper _time_text and its 'ETA {t}' / 'Elapsed {t}' / 'Left {t}' strings are gone with it: a box that narrow holds a duration, not a phrase. _draw_frame_box generalised to _draw_value_box(cell, value, width, dimmed) and reused for both. de_DE entries removed in lockstep. 76. 🟢 A take in Animation mode renders its whole range. Both engines asked Blender for a single frame: batch_pipeline._phase_5_render called render.render('INVOKE_DEFAULT', write_still=...) and cli_worker called render.render(scene=...), neither with animation=True, and no frame loop existed — _vl_cost_proxy even documented the batch as per-frame ON PURPOSE. Both now pass animation=True when sc.frame_end > sc.frame_start (the range is already applied by apply_render_overrides, so the scene's own bounds are the honest question). The completion signal had to move with it: render_complete_handler was registered on render_post, which fires once per FRAME — an animation take would clear _busy after frame 1 and hand the queue on mid-sequence. It is on render_complete now, which fires once per job for a single frame and a sequence alike; both unregister sites in batch_render_cleanup follow. _vl_cost_proxy multiplies by a new _frame_count(sc, vl) built on job_frame_range, so an animation job no longer estimates as one frame. NOT verified by an actual render — the headless suite cannot drive a batch; this needs an in-app run of a multi-frame take, a cancel mid-sequence, and a background render. 77. 🟢 The per-job bar spans a whole sequence. render_stats reports samples for the CURRENT frame, so progress = current / total filled the bar during frame one and the monotonic guard in fg_render_stats_handler then pinned it there for the rest of the run. New pure job_snapshot.job_progress(frame_current, start, end, sample_fraction) places the samples inside their own frame — (index + fraction) / frames, index clamped into range so a stale frame number cannot leave 0..0.99 — and both engines use it: render_hooks.fg_render_stats_handler directly, cli_worker._render_stats_handler inline (it has no addon import). The CLI worker's POST emit also had to learn the difference: current >= total is the end of a FRAME, and only the end of the job on the last one, so it now checks frame_current >= frame_end before declaring the job done. Cap stays 0.99 — completion is the render's own signal, since samples say nothing about compositing and denoising still to come. NOT verified by an actual render. 78. 🟢 A written frame is not a finished job. render_write_handler fires once per FRAME WRITTEN; it stamped DONE and cleared shared._pending_render_vl every time, so an animation take read as finished after its first frame and every later frame reported nothing at all — the sample handler bails when _pending_render_vl is None. It now compares sc.frame_current against sc.frame_end and only finishes on the last frame (a cancel still finishes immediately, since the engine wrote a partial file). render_complete_handler gained a guard with it: moving it to render_complete (entry 76) put it AFTER the last write rather than before, so its POST stamp would have walked DONE back a step. A probe against a real Blender pinned the firing order and counts — three frames give three render_post, three render_write, one render_complete. 79. 🟢 The in-flight bar reads the frame counter for a sequence instead of guessing from time. update_live_progress fills the bar from elapsed / tks_last_render_time until the render_stats handler takes over on the first real sample. For an animation take that recorded time was measured on ONE frame, so the ratio reaches its 0.99 cap within seconds and the monotonic guard then pins it there for the rest of the sequence — and on an engine whose stats lines never match _RE_FG_SAMPLE, nothing ever takes over. A multi-frame job needs no guess: sc.frame_current IS progress, so it now feeds job_progress(...) with a zero within-frame fraction, stepping once per frame. Single frames keep the time curve unchanged. prev hoisted above the branch, since the one-shot diagnostic below logs it either way. 80. 🟢 Every render bar formats its percentage to two places. One frame of a 250-frame job is 0.4% of that job and a fraction of that across the batch, so int(x * 100) left both bars reading the same whole number for minutes. job_snapshot.total_bar and progress_display now format .2f, and the Render Queue tab's two copies (render_queue_panel total, render_queue_lists RENDERING row) call those helpers instead of formatting their own, so the popover and the queue cannot drift apart. 81. 🟢 The whole-batch bar moves during an animation take. Its in-flight slot only uses a take's own progress when that progress is REAL — _has_real_progress, set by the sample handler — and falls back to wall-clock projection otherwise. Frame-counter progress (entry 79) is measured too, so a new TKS_OT_BatchRender._has_frame_progress is set beside it when a multi-frame take's bar is driven by sc.frame_current, reset per take alongside _has_real_progress, and get_batch_progress accepts either. 82. 🟢 Real progress wins the in-flight slot outright. The slot took max(elapsed / snapshot_estimate, real_progress), capped at 0.99. That max() was right while every take was one frame and the only risk was an estimate running LONG. An animation take inverts it: the snapshot estimate can still hold a single frame's measured time, so the wall-clock ratio reaches the cap within seconds and max() locks the slot there — the batch bar read 14.14% (0.99 of one slot in seven) while the take itself showed 0.80%. Real progress is now taken alone when present. 83. 🟢 The sidebar render button stops becoming the cancel button. _draw_render_mode_control returned early down three busy branches, each drawing an X in the render button's place — which put cancel exactly under the pointer that had just started the render. The menu button is now always drawn first and merely disabled while busy (it could never start a second render), with the matching cancel operator (tks.calibrate_render_times, tks.batch_render, tks.batch_render_bg_fast) in a row beneath it. The already-cancelling state keeps its greyed, non-alert CANCEL icon. 84. 🟢 The whole-batch bar is weighted by duration, not by an equal share per take. overall = (completed + in_flight_fraction) / total gave every take the same slot, so a one-frame Still counted as much as a 250-frame animation and finishing it moved the bar an eighth — 15.71% with one Still done and the first animation at zero. New pure job_snapshot.weighted_overall(weights, done, in_flight, in_flight_fraction) divides the finished takes' estimates plus the in-flight take's share by the sum of all estimates, and get_batch_progress feeds it the same frozen estimates snapshot the bar already used for monotonicity. It returns None when no estimate exists, which is when the old count-based formula still runs. DONE only, never FAILED or CANCELLED — unchanged, and for the same reason: a cancelled take never rendered, so counting it would send the bar to 100% on cancel. 85. 🟢 Borrowed estimates are scaled to the borrowing take's own length. Weighting the bar by duration (entry 84) only helps if the durations differ, and they did not: a 250-frame animation estimated ~20s beside a one-frame Still at ~14s, so the Still still took 8.68% of a seven-take batch. _estimate_vl_render_time falls back to the median of its SIBLINGS' measured times, and to the tks_estimated_render_time probe — both measured on ONE frame (cli_probe_worker renders a single frame), both handed over as raw seconds. Both are now multiplied by _frame_count(sc, vl), and the two sibling pools (_refresh_display_estimates, get_batch_progress) store PER-FRAME values so the median is a per-frame number to scale. A take's own history and tks_last_render_time are untouched — they were measured on that take's own range. 86. 🟢 A missing frame counter is inserted BEFORE the extension. Blender appends the frame number to the end of the output path, so a name that already carries its own extension — which Smart Output produces, and which apply_render_overrides then confirms by switching use_file_extension off — writes 'hero.png0001'. New pure job_snapshot.ensure_frame_number(path, ext) inserts a #### run ahead of a trailing extension, and apply_render_overrides applies it for multi-frame jobs only, skipping movie formats (one container, no counter). A path that already holds a # run is left alone — where the counter goes is the user's choice — and so is a path with no extension, where append-number-then-extension is already right. It sits OUTSIDE the tokenised-path branch, which never ran for a plain filename. Both engines get it, since the CLI worker calls the same apply_render_overrides; the background path's later normpath on the filepath keeps the hashes but is NOT verified by a real background render. 87. 🟢 The inserted counter carries a separator. ensure_frame_number produced hero####.png; it now produces hero_####.png, skipping the underscore when the stem already ends in _ - . / or a backslash so a deliberate separator is never doubled. 88. 🟢 The Image column resolves the counter, and drops it for a Still. apply_render_overrides writes the numbered path onto sc.render.filepath, which is per SCENE — so every take sharing that scene, Stills included, showed a raw #### while a sequence was in flight. New pure job_snapshot.preview_path(path, still, frame) zero-pads the hash run to the job's first frame, and for a Still strips the run AND a leading _/- with it, since a Still writes no counter at all. build_job_snapshot puts it on the path key, so the folder tooltip and the disk scan see the same string the reader does. 89. 🟢 A recorded render time now says how many frames it covered. Estimates borrowed from tks_last_render_time — the take's own, and the sibling medians — were measured when the batch rendered ONE frame, so a 250-frame animation still estimated ~20s beside a one-frame Still at ~14s and took a twelfth of the batch bar (entries 84, 85 weight correctly; the weights themselves were wrong). record_render_actual stamps vl['tks_last_render_frames'] (a plain ID property — session bookkeeping, not a setting, so no preferences count to bump), and _recorded_frames(vl) reads it back with a default of 1, which is exactly right for every value recorded before this. The estimator rescales the take's own last time by frames_now / frames_recorded, and both sibling pools divide by the frames the time was MEASURED on rather than what that sibling would render today. 90. 🔴 Diff State ships with the outline + fill on, box off, and half-strength box/outline opacity. preferences/props/props_diff_state.py: _OPACITY_DEFAULTS is now box 0.5 · outline 0.5 · fill 0.25 (was 1.0 · 1.0 · 0.25) and the master-mark default reads from a new _MARKS_ON_BY_DEFAULT = {outline, fill} instead of mark == 'box'. Both states (keyed and drift) get the same defaults; colours, line width, empty style/size and the whole per-kind table are unchanged. Only default= values moved, so a saved user_preferences.json still wins - existing users see no change, fresh installs and Reset see the new look. dev/tests/test_diff_state_prefs.py pins the new defaults (outline + fill on, box + empty off, box/outline at 0.5).

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Camera Visibility writes deferred out of the depsgraph tick — intermittent EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in deg_check_base_in_depsgraph on switch-then-transform. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-20.) apply_camera_visibility (Show Assigned / Hide Others) wrote hide_viewport / hide_render / hide_set(view_layer=…) INLINE from apply_overrides inside depsgraph_update_post; hide flags rebuild depsgraph relations and per-view-layer Bases — the structures evaluation is walking (dump: null Base lookup while workers copy the Scene in SceneBackup::init_from_scene). Found by a four-level seeded bisect: six handlers → only VL Switch Handler off stops it; handler phases → the whole fast sweep off STILL crashes, apply_overrides off does not; inside it → camera/world pointer writes innocent, apply_camera_visibility off survives every run; prefs dependency confirmed (factory startup survives — auto_camera_visibility defaults off). Fix: per-scene coalesced requests applied by a one-shot timer (_schedule_camera_visibility / _drain_camera_visibility in core/cascade.py). Failed approaches (recorded): a view-layer membership guard in the sweep (wrong hypothesis, crashed with guard in place), and routing through enqueue_mutation (vl_switch_scope drains that queue in its finally, still in-tick — crashed attempt 1). Verification: 2-step repro (seed 48291: switch_vl → rotate) 28+ runs clean vs died-on-attempt-1 before; suite 2408 passed. doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_transform_deg_base_crash.md. Commit 49780182.
    2. 🟢 The way back is bound where events actually arrive. Both 3D View keymap items registered live and active (MOUSEMOVE ANY trigger='HOVER', LEFTMOUSE PRESS trigger='CLICK'), the outbound switch fired twice in the same session, the origin was remembered - and tks.sequencer_go_back logged ZERO arrivals. Registered, correctly scoped, never matched: verbatim the SequencerCommon failure from the outbound campaign, unrecognised in the other direction. Now bound on the global Frames map too - the one this feature has MEASURED to deliver, since PLAY and all four arrows come from it - with the operator's context.area.type == 'VIEW_3D' check, the area under the mouse, as the filter that makes a global binding safe. The Frames LEFTMOUSE does not repeat the entry removed in 0.8.0 Fixed 118: that one was tagged as the PLAYHEAD rung, so an ordinary click claimed to be a scrub; here the rung IS CLICK. The 3D View entries stay - correct home, no cost, and a return is idempotent because the first clears the origin the second would read. The two extra field rounds were spent on INSTRUMENTATION, not the keymap: invoke had two deliberately silent early returns (it rides MOUSEMOVE, and an unlatched log there writes hundreds of lines a second), so an empty log meant three different things and named none. Replaced with a latched verdict - log only when the answer changes - which is the same pattern that cracked the scrub detector. The origin check also moved ahead of the area lookup: one module-global against None, on a binding that now sees every mouse move in the application. See doc/troubleshooting/sequencer_scene_autoswitch_triggers.md.
    3. 🔴 Metaball cascade slot lookup could never match, and the miss path CLEARS the action. core/cascade_actions.py's inlined ID-type chain mapped bpy.types.MetaBall to 'METABALL'; Blender's enum member is 'META' (probed live on 5.2.0: slots.new('METABALL', ...) raises TypeError, and the member list has META and no METABALL). Both cascade paths build the slot table from Blender's own slot.target_id_type — ('META', name) — then probed it with ('METABALL', name), so EVERY metaball lookup missed. cascade_actions.py:405-415 treats a miss as "this target should not be animated by this action" and unassigns ad.action_slot then ad.action — the same path the file's own comment calls catastrophic (84-object incident). Silent: the diagnostic log at :394 only fires for SCENE/WORLD/NODETREE/MATERIAL/LIGHT/CAMERA. Reachable: core/vl_targets.py:58-61 yields id_data.data for any object with data, and metaballs are a supported animated case (naming template naming_utils.py:592). Core fix + features/rest_state/assimilation.py's unreachable GENERIC_NAMES key shipped on main as 9b7db0fe with dev/tests/test_metaball_id_type.py; doc/troubleshooting/metaball_id_type_spelling.md. This entry records it — it had no changelog line.
    4. 🔴 slots.new(id_type='OBJECT') for metaball and particle data produced a slot Blender then REFUSES to bind. core/path_utils._TYPE_MAP and core/anim_utils._SLOT_ID_TYPE_MAP (byte-for-byte twins, class-name keyed, .get(cls, 'OBJECT')) listed neither MetaBall nor ParticleSettings. 'OBJECT' is a real enum member so slots.new SUCCEEDS; binding then raises RuntimeError: ... not suitable for this data-block type (MB) one step away from the wrong answer. Reached via features/rest_state/keyframe_write.py:73 and panels/inspector/sync_jit.py:245. Same pass: panels/inspector/sync_actions.py's data sub-target tuple asked for 'METABALL' — but tracing what FEEDS target_type showed the tuple was not even the reachable half. The two isinstance chains in panels/inspector/sync_viewport.py (_sub_id_type :418, _id_type :563) had no MetaBall branch, so a metaball arrived as 'OBJECT' and could never reach that case however it was spelled; the sub-target chain was also missing Curve/Armature/Lattice, which both the tuple and the sibling chain already expected. That same value goes straight to merge_action_into_cascade(id_type=) -> slots.new(). Tests probe the LIVE enum rather than hard-coding it, put a real datablock through every callable resolver, prove the wrong id_type really does refuse to bind, and sweep the tree for the invented spelling in STRING TOKENS only (a naive grep failed on its own explanatory comments). Follow-up in the same branch closed the class: all four resolvers merged into core/anim_utils.resolve_id_type (memoized chain), with path_utils/vl_switch_fast re-exporting and cascade_actions calling it — _ID_TYPE_MEMO re-exported too so it stays one dict. NOT neutral in one direction: the dicts also had no TextCurve/LightProbe/Speaker entry, so those answered 'OBJECT' and now get their real types; TextCurve keeps answering 'CURVE' (pinned by test_sweep_round2.py:127, not a fix). doc/troubleshooting/metaball_id_type_residue.md. Commits 8545ed22, 5c66606c.
    5. 🔴 _process_target tagged the sweep's loop variable, not the datablock it wrote — and NameError out of the sweep when the object loop yields nothing. core/vl_switch_fast.py — the closure's snap step ended if hasattr(obj, 'update_tag'): obj.update_tag(), where obj is the free variable of for obj in scene.objects:. Three call sites: the object sweep (right by luck), the scene+world loop and the instance-source loop (both refreshed whichever object the sweep saw LAST). With no objects at all — an objectless scene, or TKS_STRESS_SKIP=objects — obj is never bound (the instance-source discovery loop iterates scene.objects too, so it does not rescue the empty case) and a world snap raised NameError: cannot access free variable 'obj' where it is not associated with a value in enclosing scope at :575. NameError is not in the snap block's except list and the enclosing try has only a finally, so it escaped the whole sweep. Fix: tag target and getattr(target, 'data', None) — identical to the old code when target IS the object. Tests: a structural one (the code object must have no obj free variable) plus the end-to-end objectless-scene world snap. Test gotcha recorded: core/mutation_queue.is_snap_suppressed is a 1-SECOND WALL-CLOCK gate on a module global, so any earlier undo-path test in the suite armed it and the new test passed alone / failed in a full run for reasons unrelated to the defect — it now holds that gate open explicitly. doc/troubleshooting/sweep_tagged_the_wrong_datablock.md. Commit ce4472b3.
    6. 🔴 _on_variant_select imported three names from a module that defines none of them. features/variant_switch/properties.py:650 — from .operators import parse_multi_cascade, build_multi_cascade, apply_variant_cascade. Real homes: core/variant_queries.py:42,54 and cascade_engine.py:81 (re-exported by ops_cascade.py:17). operators.py mentions apply_variant_cascade only in a function-local import inside one of its own operators, which is what made it look plausible. The callback IS armed (update=_on_variant_select at properties.py:821) and has stayed quiet only because nothing writes wm.tks_vsw_sel_variant — the sole reader is a getattr at ops_cascade.py:470. First write from anywhere, script included, would raise ImportError instead of applying the variant. Imports stay function-local: the picker resolves its menu through a deferred import to break a proxy<->menu cycle. Test gotchas: setting the real enum is refused (enum "2" not found in ('0') — retained dynamic items do not have to rebuild for a synthetic world), so the callback is driven directly with a stub context; and the guard at :644 returns before the import while addon_is_mutating holds, which is a computed property with NO setter — the test clears is_applying/is_undoing/is_redoing, since a headless suite leaves is_applying standing after a file read. No UI is re-surfaced; the callback stays dormant, just no longer armed with a broken import. Auditor CORR-19 flags this class and 44 more sites remain — their own campaign. doc/troubleshooting/variant_select_phantom_import.md. Commit 11ebae19.
    7. 🔴 Cached VL-switch rest-snap silently dropped ENUM and INT properties. features/rest_state/cache.py's snap_cached_diffs — the path a view-layer switch actually runs — re-inlined the value writer instead of calling the shared logic._apply_value:836-884 that _snap_one_target (:237,:242) and snap_single_to_rest's _write (:769-773) already use, and had fallen THREE fixes behind: (a) hasattr(prop, '__len__') instead of core/path_utils.is_array_value — a dropdown reads back as its identifier STRING, which answers __len__, so enums were routed into the array branch and died on 'str' object does not support item assignment; (b) no coerce_rna_value, so an INT property refused the float the rest cache holds (expected an int type, not float); (c) no known-boolean safety net for hide_viewport/hide_render/mute. All three raise inside the ladder's bare except (...): pass at :427-428, so the property kept its old value with nothing reported — Alt+I and the per-object path were fine, which is what made it look switch-specific. The fork also carried a verbatim duplicate of its own boolean-cast block (:397-409 == :413-425). Fix replaces the generic branch's write mechanics only; the fast-path transform ladder and per-site logging are untouched, and the scalar diff check now COERCES before comparing so a dropdown already at its rest value is not rewritten. The swallow stays (rest-state is autokey/undo hot territory; removed fallbacks stay removed). Repro: obj.rotation_mode stuck at 'XYZ' when rest wanted 'ZXY', obj.pass_index stuck at 0 when rest wanted 7. doc/troubleshooting/cached_rest_snap_dropped_enums_and_ints.md. Commit 75fc54b8.
    8. 🔴 Inspector rest-snap queue that nothing ever filled. panels/inspector/sync_actions.py — _pending_rest_snaps was declared (:14), cleared on every VL switch (:150) and read by a 132-line drain engine _process_rest_snaps (:159). No line in the addon appended to it (grep: clear + read only). handlers.py:6 imported both names and called neither. Reads as the remnant of a deliberately removed fallback, and the standing ruling is that rest-snap fires only on witnessed key-count loss (69ba211) — removed fallbacks stay removed — so deleting agrees with that ruling rather than quietly reopening it. Also collapses the doubled module-level _pending_fresh_actions binding (:15 and :134; the second replaced the list object after the module body had run, harmless only because handlers.py imports later). dev/tests/test_no_dead_rest_snap_queue.py pins the absence, so a queue like this can only return WITH a producer. Auditor CORR-21 Never-Filled Collection 2->1. Commit eef69432.
    9. 🔴 Seven more deferred imports named a module that does not define what they ask for. Same class as Fixed 6, found by sweeping rather than reading. SIX pointed at features/variant_switch/operators: ops_manage.py:125 (get_cascade_target, apply_variant_cascade) and ops_variant.py:35/51/210/258 (get_world, get_variant_display, parse_multi_cascade, build_multi_cascade, apply_variant_cascade). Real homes: core/variant_queries.py for the four query helpers, features/variant_switch/cascade_engine.py for the apply, utils/store_world.py for the world resolver. The callers are a tooltip (description() at :35), a popover draw (:51), two operator execute paths and a bulk-apply branch — every one an ImportError waiting for a user to reach it. The SEVENTH: panels/inspector/__init__.py:115 asked .handlers for mark_inspector_dirty, which lives in .cache, and the same file already imports it correctly from .cache twice. get_world had to be CHOSEN, not just repointed: features/variant_switch has two wrappers with that name and opposite semantics — ops_crud's calls get_or_create_vsw_world (its docstring: "NOT draw-safe - allocates bpy data. Operators only.") and panel's calls get_vsw_world ("Draw-safe."). Both sites here are draw paths, so both take get_vsw_world straight from utils/store_world. The tooltip also gains a if world: guard: get_variant_display dereferences the world for a single-product cascade, so making a never-run site reachable without it would swap ImportError for AttributeError. All imports stay function-local (the picker's proxy<->menu cycle). New guard dev/tests/test_no_phantom_deferred_imports.py walks every function-local from ... import ... in the addon and resolves it for real — deliberately a RUNTIME check, because panels/popovers/__init__.py re-exports through import * and a name can be resolvable without appearing in any import line a static scan can see. That distinction is not academic: the auditor's CORR-19 reported 44 sites here, and probing each pair in a live Blender showed 7 real and 26 that resolve fine through that hub. The check was fixed on the auditor side (build_namespace_table now follows readable star sources to a fixed point; blender-addon-auditor commit 999c03e, doc/troubleshooting/corr19_star_import_false_positives.md) and CORR-19 now reports 0 against this branch, with quality 3.00 -> 3.88. doc/troubleshooting/phantom_deferred_imports_sweep.md. Commit e2c14507.
    10. 🟢 _poll_slot_removal snapped to rest DURING undo - the last undo step showed the action pose instead of the rest pose. The poll exists to catch USER-initiated clears (the native template_ID 'X' fires no depsgraph event), but an undo also turns ad.action from set to None and the poll had no addon_is_mutating / grace-window check at all. Field log 2026-08-26 14:24:59: Aborting _handle_autokey_mirror: addon_is_mutating (undoing=True ...) immediately followed by SLOT POLL: action cleared on Object::Suzanne_MESH action:'01-01_blue'->'None' ..., snapping to ref - the flag was visibly up and the poll fired anyway, painting ref=0.0816 over the live=-0.0299 state Blender had just restored. Its sibling honours the window (_revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred: ABORTED (Undo/Redo grace) in the same log); the poll predates that discipline. Fix: after the clear is detected AND the tracker is updated, consume the event without snapping when TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating or mutation_queue.is_snap_suppressed() holds. The tracker update stays unconditional on purpose - an early return would leave the stale pair and the first poll after the window would late-fire the very snap that was suppressed (test_the_suppressed_clear_is_reobserved_not_postponed pins it; re-observe-never-snap is rest_cache's own documented rule). 6 tests in dev/tests/test_slot_poll_undo_guard.py; a genuine user clear still snaps. FOLLOW-UP FILED, not fixed here: the snap showed the ACTION pose because the rest baseline itself was poisoned - the autokey mirror re-captures insert_rest_keyframe baselines from the LIVE pose (log shows captures at frame 6 with the cascade action posing the object) after the rest slot's keys are removed by undo (they were written in undo-recovery windows with skipped undo_push). That capture-while-posed defect also skews Alt+I revert and needs its own pass. doc/troubleshooting/slot_poll_snapped_during_undo.md.
    11. 🟢 The rest cache snapshotted the ASSIGNED action's pose as the neutral baseline - "rest state is being poisoned". rest_cache._snapshot_id_block captures live values as neutral, and the cache is cleared + re-snapshotted on every undo (invalidate_and_rebuild -> _initial_snapshot_timer), on selection change and on file load. Nothing asked WHO was posing the object: a re-snapshot at frame 6 with cascade action 01-01_blue assigned read location = 0.0965 - the ACTION's output - and cached it as neutral. The autokey mirror prefers the cache (get_cached_value, source tag REST-CACHE) when writing insert_rest_keyframe baselines into the Rest action, so the action pose became "rest"; every revert then restored the action pose and the drift panel agreed with it (zero drift against a poisoned reference). The log shows the baseline re-captured repeatedly - 0.102... action-era at 14:24:25, -0.009... true rest at 14:24:54 - last capture wins. The existing _rest_has_path guard only protects channels the Rest action ALREADY covers; the vulnerable ones are exactly those not yet in it (they keep falling out because rest keys written in undo-recovery windows carry skipped undo_push and vanish with the undone step - that durability question is its own follow-up). Fix: driven_paths = the assigned action's slot-fcurve (data_path, array_index) set, skipped in both capture loops; a live value is only neutral if nothing is posing it. Undriven channels still cache from live; the Rest action posing itself does not populate the set, so rest-mode behaviour is byte-identical (rest-covered channels were already skipped as the Rest action's business - a test pins that expectation, corrected during TDD). Rejected: skipping the whole snapshot while any action is assigned - too broad, it would starve the mirror of correct baselines for undriven channels. NOTE for already-poisoned files: the fix stops NEW poison; re-store rest state from a clean pose to overwrite old poison. 4 tests in dev/tests/test_rest_cache_not_poisoned_by_action.py. doc/troubleshooting/rest_cache_poisoned_by_action_pose.md.

    13. 🔴 Preset verbs for the facade (list_presets, apply_preset). Reading precedes applying because an agent cannot apply what it was never shown — the same reason list_variants precedes switch_variant. Each entry carries key (the sanitised filename it is addressed by), name (what the user typed) and tier, because the same name can live in several of PROJECT/LOCAL/SHARED/ADDON and "apply the HQ preset" is otherwise ambiguous — an agent picking the wrong tier is silently wrong, the failure mode with no symptom. An unknown kind is REFUSED with the real kinds rather than answering empty, which is why PRESET_KINDS is named rather than discovered: an empty list for a typo reads as "no presets exist". apply_preset is deliberately NOT gated behind confirm=True, unlike delete_take — the click path (tks.apply_render_preset, no invoke()) asks nothing, so gating the agent path would make clicking and asking disagree about the same action; the undo step carries reversibility. The answer reports which tier won. Tests: test_ai_presets.py (7), test_ai_apply_preset.py (8). TWO test traps are recorded in the fixture because both cost a debugging pass: resolution is captured by the OUTPUT kind, so a render preset round-trips cleanly while changing no resolution at all (green test, opposite of its name); and LOCAL/SHARED/PROJECT are preference-driven, so a REGISTERED operator resolving the addon module under a different name than the caller reads prefs as None and those tiers collapse to '' — a preset the test can see is invisible to the operator applying it, so any save-then-apply test must use ADDON (bpy.utils.user_resource, no prefs involved). AI-04 clean afterwards: 16 verbs, 16 documented. Commits 46b7bad1, 4e57e340.
    14. 🔴 Render job verbs (render_status, cancel_render). The AI-Ready card's last phase, and TWO verbs rather than the three AI-03's remedy names: starting was already scriptable because the batch operators keep their confirmation in invoke(), so execute() runs from a script. Seeing and stopping were the gaps — a job an agent can start but neither watch nor cancel is worse than one it cannot start, since it cannot know when to stop waiting or report what happened. Nothing is invented: BGRenderManager / FastBGRenderManager already tracked active_task, completed, queue, total_count and had cancel(). BOTH managers are checked — watching one would leave a render started through the other invisible. render_status answers WHILE the engine is busy, since a status call that refused because of a running render would be useless exactly when needed. cancel_render is idempotent (nothing running → cancelled: False, not a refusal), because an agent's commonest failure is retrying a call it believes timed out. It carries NO undo label while still being listed as mutating: killing a subprocess is not something Ctrl+Z takes back, so claiming an undo step would misrepresent what is recoverable. 11 tests drive a fake manager — starting a real render in the suite would be slow, machine-dependent, and would strand subprocesses on a mid-test failure. Commit dd1223c1.

    15. 🔴 create_preset — the facade saves live settings as a NEW preset. Closes the AI-Ready card's last phase. Named create_preset rather than save_preset because it REFUSES a name already in use instead of overwriting: reusing a name destroys saved work silently and with no symptom, while refusing costs one retry — and the refusal lists the names in use so the retry is informed. Delegates to tks.create_render_preset, which already captures across all nine kinds; the facade adds the clash refusal and an answer naming the tier it landed in, since the tiers are not interchangeable. tier defaults to ADDON deliberately — LOCAL/SHARED/PROJECT are preference-driven and resolve to nothing unless configured, so another default would fail on a clean install for reasons an agent could not diagnose (the trap that cost a debugging pass on apply_preset). Kinds needing something present refuse clearly: camera capture needs an active camera, world capture a world, and the message says which. 9 tests including create → apply back → assert the setting returns, so an empty file with the right name cannot pass. Commit 696315af.

    25. 🟢 Rest seed memory: the rest baseline survives undo eating the Rest action (the poison-pair's open follow-up). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-29.)     27. 🟢 Every checkout wrote to one log file, and no line said which wrote it. (Verified 2026-08-30 by automated proof, on the user's explicit "verify by yourself" request — evidence listed at the end of this entry.) Field incident 2026-08-30: a headless suite run against a worktree via the BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS override and the user's live Blender (rendering in the background from main) both appended to takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log — 3.8 GB in which a real render was buried under test fixtures reading as genuine failures ('message': 'out of memory', 'message': 'boom', ai.cancel_render() -> ok). Two causes, both in utils/logger.py: get_log_dir() falls back to bpy.utils.user_resource('SCRIPTS', …), the Blender USER CONFIG root, and BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS redirects only where extension CODE loads from — never user_resource(); and get_log_filepath() built <base>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.log, where only the date varies. The collision is not override-specific: two Blender versions on one junction, or a second instance, share a file on the same day too. Fix. New bpy-free utils/log_source.py. resolve_source_suffix(package_dir) reads the parent folder of the takes_for_blender/ package and returns a short filename-safe tag, deliberately returning "" for the canonical Takes-for-Blender folder AND for every ordinary install (_INSTALL_PARENTS = user_default/blender_org/addons/…, plus an _INSTALL_ROOTS grandparent check so a custom extension repo id is still an install) — that empty string is what keeps the historical filename byte-identical for main and for real users, so there is no migration and no churn in the normal case. A worktree (.worktrees/Takes-for-Blender-maint12) or sibling clone (Takes-for-Blender-spike) has the repo prefix stripped and yields maint12 / spike, sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and capped at 32 chars. build_log_filename(base, date, suffix) holds the naming rule itself so it is provable without Blender. Wiring. logger.get_addon_root() = os.path.realpath(__file__) walked up two levels — realpath is what resolves the extension junction to the real working tree, since __file__ reports the junction path and main and a worktree would otherwise look identical. Cached in _addon_root_cached / _source_suffix_cached; realpath is a syscall and must never run per line. Both helpers swallow everything (# CORR-05-OK) and fall back to "", i.e. to today's exact filename — logging must never break the addon. debug_log_path / debug_log_filename semantics are untouched: a worktree must never edit live user prefs (same reasoning as TKS_TEST_MODE), and a per-run env tag was rejected because the run that caused this is the run nobody would have tagged. Banner. New _session_banner() / _write_lines(): the first write to a given file in a session is prefixed with [SESSION] Addon source: <resolved path> (pid <n>). Emitted lazily by the writers rather than at register time, so a user with enable_debug_logging off never gets an empty file created; both _flush_log_buffer (timer) and _flush_sync (--background, unregister) route through _write_lines, so neither path can lose it. register_logger() resets _banner_path, re-bannering after a disable/enable cycle. The pid separates two sessions running the same code. Untouched by design. _cleanup_old_logs() already globs <name>_*<ext>, which matches a suffixed file (pinned by a test, so a worktree log cannot become immortal); log_reader.list_log_files() already globs *.log, so a worktree log appears in the Debug Monitor as its own named entry. Tests. dev/tests/test_log_source_suffix.py — 13 pytest.mark.pure tests, module imported by path, with an AST check proving it imports no bpy. Pins main to takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log byte for byte, a worktree to …_maint12.log, a normal install to no rename, a custom debug_log_filename to keeping its extension, and two checkouts on one day to two filenames. Live proof: re-running the suite through the override while the user's Blender ran from main produced takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log (3702 MB, live) and takes_for_blender_2026-08-30_logsrc.log (105 MB, suite) side by side, the latter opening with the SESSION banner naming the worktree. Suite 2797 passed / 1 skipped under Blender 5.2. Doc: doc/troubleshooting/log_file_shared_across_checkouts.md. Verification. Two headless Blender 5.2 runs of dev/temp/verify_changelog.py, each loading the SAME branch code through a different extension junction, so the only variable is the path realpath() resolves to. Run A (main-shaped path) — a real directory copy at <scratch>/mainsim/Takes-for-Blender/takes_for_blender (a copy, not a junction, since junctions resolve through): addon_root = that path, suffix = '', filename = takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log, i.e. byte-identical to the historical name. Run B (worktree path): addon_root = .worktrees/Takes-for-Blender-logsrc/takes_for_blender, suffix = 'logsrc', filename = takes_for_blender_2026-08-30_logsrc.log. Both runs additionally proved, live: the resolved root is a real directory and not the junction Blender loaded (root_is_real); the cache is what serves the second call, so realpath cannot run per line (root_cached, via a sentinel); the banner names the resolved root and is emitted exactly once per file (banner_first / banner_repeat = None); a real tks_log line reaches that file (wrote_marker); log_reader.list_log_files() still lists it, so the Debug Monitor is unaffected (monitor_sees); the age-cleanup glob still matches a suffixed name (cleanup_glob); and with os.path.realpath monkeypatched to raise, the filename falls back to today's exact unsuffixed name instead of propagating (fallback_ok). Cross-proof: full headless suite 2797 passed / 1 skipped against the worktree via the BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS override; 13 pytest.mark.pure unit tests; and a fresh auditor AST scan with AUDITOR_SCAN_ROOT pointed at the worktree (502 files — exactly the worktree's .py count, so the new module WAS scanned) returns zero findings naming log_source.py. Not covered by automation, and the only thing left for a hands-on look: that the Debug Monitor's file dropdown reads well with two same-day entries in it.

      Out of scope, filed as roadmap ideas: the log FLOODS (3.8 GB on 2026-08-30, 6.4 GB on 2026-08-25 against 0.3 MB on 2026-08-26; one suite run alone wrote 105 MB; commit 89b2123f names keymap_audit as a suspect), and nothing CAPS a log — _cleanup_old_logs prunes by age (7 days) only, so a single day can fill a disk.

    28. 🟢 The cached log filepath was only refreshed on a DATE change, so moving the log was ignored until midnight. _flush_sync / _flush_log_buffer cache _log_filepath_cached and recomputed it only when _log_date_cached != today. User-facing consequence: repointing debug_log_path in Preferences kept writing to the old file for the rest of the session. Test consequence, and how it was found: Blender enables the extension at startup, BEFORE dev/tests/run_tests.py sets TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, so the startup flush cached the real profile path and the override that arrived moments later was never consulted again — the whole suite's output, keymap audit included, went into the developer's live log while the assertions read the isolated one. Diagnostic printed from inside a test: get_log_filepath() ended tks_test_cfg_iks6fzjj/logs/takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log while _log_filepath_cached still ended Blender/5.2/scripts/presets/takes_for_blender/logs/takes_for_blender_2026-08-30.log (separators shown as / for legibility). Fix: new _log_destination_key() — the tuple (TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, debug_log_path, debug_log_filename) — compared on every flush alongside the date. A dict lookup and two getattrs, no syscall, so the per-line background flush does not pay for get_log_filepath()'s user_resource(create=True). Both flush functions share it, and the existing midnight-rollover test still passes because a date change alone still forces the recompute. Two supporting changes. (a) New _test_log_dir() in utils/logger.py mirrors persistence_io._test_config_dir: same TKS_TEST_CONFIG_DIR, unconditional (NOT gated on TKS_TEST_MODE), checked BEFORE the debug_log_path preference because isolation a test can switch off is not isolation. BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS redirects only which CODE loads, never bpy.utils.user_resource, which is why test fixtures had been landing in the live log at all. No change to run_tests.py — it already sets the variable. (b) test_ai_call_log.py's _tail(path, nbytes=8000) replaced by _mark(path) / _since(path, mark): one file load writes ~70 KB of [UI:HOTKEYS] [AUDIT] rows, nine times that window, so a probe line was routinely pushed out of view — and on a shared daily log a match could come from an EARLIER run's identical line, meaning these tests could pass without having written anything. With the isolated log in place but the tail read still there, all four failed deterministically, which is what exposed the caching bug. Reading from a recorded offset asserts THIS test wrote the line. Deliberately NOT done: quietening the keymap audit (keymap-audit-log-noise) would have hidden the tail problem rather than fixed it and touches neither of the other two findings. Tests: dev/tests/test_log_isolation.py (6) plus the four previously-flaky tests. The flake itself is only provable by repetition — full suite three times back to back. Companion to Fixed 27, which landed from another session while this was in flight and solves the adjacent half: a per-checkout filename suffix stops two CHECKOUTS interleaving. It does not replace this one — the suffix is empty for the canonical checkout, so a suite run against main still wrote into the live profile log, and it touches neither the date-only cache invalidation nor the tail read. Both were kept in the merge; _log_destination_key deliberately omits the source suffix, which is resolved once per session from a folder that cannot move. (Verified 2026-08-30 by a live probe, no mouse needed: a session logs a line, then mid-session the debug_log_path PREFERENCE is pointed at a fresh folder. The resolved path follows the preference, the cache follows it, the NEXT line lands in the new file, the old file does not also receive it, and the real profile log is untouched. Before the fix the flush kept the start-up path until midnight.) Card doc/roadmap/active/ai-log-test-flake.md. Branch fix/test-log-isolation.

    30. 🟢 A 3-channel colour preference truncated the whole config file (_serialize_pref_value). (Found while adding the Diff State colours; in-app confirmed 2026-08-24.) FloatVectorProperty(size=4, subtype='COLOR_GAMMA') returns a bpy_prop_array (has __iter__ → converted); size=3, subtype='COLOR' returns a mathutils.Color, which is INDEXABLE but has no __iter__, so it slipped the iterable check and json.dump raised TypeError: Object of type Color is not JSON serializable MID-WRITE — leaving user_preferences.json 30 bytes long, a single { plus half an entry. Latent since the serializer existed; every colour preference until now was size-4. Fix broadens the check to anything sequence-shaped (__len__ + __getitem__), with str/bytes excluded. Process note: the failing guard test was first written off as a worktree artifact because it passed from the main checkout — wrong, because a run launched from a worktree WITHOUT BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS still imports the worktree's own code from sys.path. doc/troubleshooting/prefs_three_channel_colour_truncates_config.md. 2 regression tests. Commit 4d4b11c6.

    31. 🟢 Keying one object snapped every drifted object back to rest (keyframe mass-snap). Root cause: _deferred_jit_merge / _deferred_sub_jit in panels/inspector/sync_jit.py call merge_action_into_cascade, whose slots.new/channelbags.new/fcurves.new structurally mutate the SHARED cascade action; Blender then re-evaluates that action for every bound ID on the next depsgraph pass, and a hand-dragged value on a keyed channel is a borrowed value that evaluation discards — scene-wide, in one tick. Proven from the user's live log (2026-08-31): three drift-count collapses to zero, each coinciding to the second with a JIT2 COMPLETE … (merge OK) fold; the long-suspected _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred skipped every target ('no witnessed loss', counts only ever grew) and snap_cached_diffs never ran — both exonerated. Four earlier fixtures were silent because a hand-assigned action is never folded. Fix: both fold bodies snapshot the live values of every keyed channel bound to the cascade action (_snapshot_bystander_drifts — exactly the stompable set, independent of the Rest feature, skipped under Value Lock), then consume the re-evaluation themselves (view_layer.update()) and write the values back by name (_restore_bystander_drifts, mirror-suppressed via arm_suppress(1.0, hard=False), epsilon-gated). Round 2 (sandbox verification failed, same day): the in-app sandbox test still snapped with ZERO JIT lines — a third fold path: _process_fresh_actions (panels/inspector/sync_actions.py, branch 1) merges a queued fresh action into the resolved cascade. The guard became a shared capture/restore pair + preserve_keyed_live_values context manager in features/rest_state/logic.py (snapshots ALL keyed-channel live values scene-wide — no action filter, so every fold is covered; inert under Value Lock and addon_is_mutating), wrapped around every merge_action_into_cascade call site: both sync_jit deferreds, the _process_fresh_actions drain, both ops_action_merge merges, and the ops_watchlist unpin-merge. New test dev/tests/test_fresh_action_merge_preserves_bystanders.py (3) reproduces the sandbox path. New public apply_channel_value in logic.py keeps the cross-package import public (ARCH03). Tests: dev/tests/test_jit_fold_preserves_bystanders.py (4) — reproduces the field bug deterministically in an isolated scene (the harness .blend's live cascade otherwise adopts and snaps bed objects mid-dispatch, which re-demonstrated the bug during test development). Full suite 3035 passed / 1 skipped. Doc: doc/troubleshooting/keyframe_mass_snap_cascade_fold.md. Card doc/roadmap/active/keyframe-mass-snap.md. Branch fix/mass-snap-fold. (Confirmed in-app 2026-08-31, worktree sandbox: six 'fold guard: restored' lines, drift surviving every fold, user-verified no snap.)

    32. 🔴 "Show Overrides…" refused to open, reporting a scripted-call error. Reported from the running addon 2026-08-31: clicking the entry produced "TKS_OT_cascade_overflow_popover opens a UI element, so a scripted call does nothing. This capability has no scripted route yet." Root cause is not in the operator. A popup menu's layout carries an EXEC operator context, so every entry runs execute() and never invoke(); TKS_OT_CascadeOverflowPopover.execute finds no _tks_invoked marker, correctly concludes it was reached by a script, and refuses through refuse_scripted. The refusal was doing its job on a caller that was not really a script. Fix: layout.operator_context = 'INVOKE_DEFAULT' at the top of TKS_MT_TreeContextMenu.draw, which is how Blender's own menus do it (bl_ui/properties_data_curves.py:109) — no Takes menu set it anywhere, so the same latent defect sits in every other menu whose entries open something; only the one with a reported symptom is fixed here. The ten dispatcher entries were unaffected and would have hidden this indefinitely: each one's execute re-enters its own invoke, so they worked under the wrong context. Pinned by test_entries_run_invoke_not_execute, whose fake layout deliberately starts at Blender's real EXEC_REGION_WIN default so a menu that forgets the line fails.

    33. 🔴 Invert Selection did nothing and reported success — since the day it was written. The provider was registered as TKS_OT_MultiSelect.__new__(TKS_OT_MultiSelect).invert_selection(...), and Blender refuses to build an Operator that way: TypeError: bpy_struct.__new__(struct): expected a single argument. Measured with dev/tmp/probe_invert.py. So the provider raised on its first line every time it was ever called, for every list, not just the tree. Two tolerant layers hid it completely: core/providers.query swallows a provider crash by design and returns the caller's default, and TKS_OT_InvertMultiselect.execute ignored the result and returned FINISHED regardless — the exact shape Constitution rule 7 calls the most misleading an addon can offer. The provider returned None on success too, so even a caller that HAD checked could not have told the cases apart. Fix in three parts: the walk helpers became @classmethods (they never touched instance state — only invoke/execute read self.list_type), so a provider can call them with no object to build; both public halves return True; and a shared _run_multiselect reports and CANCELS instead of lying — WARNING when multi-select is off, ERROR when the provider did not answer True. dev/tests/test_multiselect_walk.py passed for the whole life of the bug because it drove the helpers directly and never crossed the seam; its probe copied vars(cls) items passing callable(value), and a classmethod object is not callable, so the fix silently emptied it until the filter learned about descriptors. doc/troubleshooting/invert_selection_did_nothing.md.

    34. 🔴 Select All dragged the highlight to the last row, and so did Invert. tks_selected carries an update= callback, _on_row_ticked, whose whole job is to move the blue bar to the row just ticked — correct for ONE deliberate tick, and what makes the move arrows agree with the selection. A sweep writes every visible row in order, so each write fired it and the bar walked the list, stopping wherever the walk stopped. Nothing was broken in Select All; two correct behaviours met. Not obvious because the coupling is an RNA update= hook — the callback is in panels/, the sweep in operators/inspector/, and neither file mentions the other, so no call graph shows it. test_multiselect_walk asserts which rows end up ticked and never looks at tks_all_viewlayers_index, so it passed throughout. Fix: a bulk_tick() context manager in properties.py that _on_row_ticked returns early under, wrapping the whole body of BOTH sweeps — Invert had the identical fault. The flag restores in a finally, so a raising walk cannot leave the guard up and silently kill highlight-follows-tick for the session. Rejected: suppressing inside _walk_visible alone (the CONTEXT branch writes outside it, so half the rows would still move the bar) and restoring the index afterwards (a number, not the reader's place, and it would flicker through every row on the way). doc/troubleshooting/select_all_moved_the_highlight.md.

    36. 🟢 A tagged tree line pushed its row's icon and name right of the untagged rows. A tag-coloured strip widens with tks_tree_line_width while an untagged one keeps the thin default, so at MEDIUM / WIDE the columns drifted. Two wrong fixes came first, both instructive. (1) Park the difference beside the untagged strip as a blank label scaled by the same factor - changed nothing, because scale_x multiplies a widget's OWN natural width and a blank label is far narrower than a colour prop(). (2) Widen the untagged strip to the tagged width - aligned correctly, but by changing the tree lines themselves, which the user ruled out: the lines stay, only the spacing moves. Shipped: the untagged strip keeps its thin colour and reserves TAG_GAP_UNITS beside it as ui_units_x, which is ABSOLUTE and so actually is the width it says. Only the tag column compensates - spacing every strip would shift whole rows right instead of lining them up - and that column is NOT the same loop index on every tier: a view layer row draws it with is_last, a take row echoes it one level deeper with is_last off, which is why draw_tree_line takes an explicit match_tag_column rather than inferring it. The first pass had that index wrong in both files. The width table itself had drifted into three copies and now lives once in utils/tree_metrics.py - in utils/ because features/variant_switch/ui_helpers.py needs it too and a feature may not import panels (ARCH-01). Gap values are tuned by eye against the strip widths; one dict, one line to nudge. See doc/troubleshooting/tree_row_column_alignment.md.

    41. 🔴 _on_depsgraph walked depsgraph.updates during undo/redo/cascade (auditor CRASH-01 K1, CRITICAL). Undo and the cascade apply free and rebuild datablocks mid-flight; touching update.id then is the freed-data class the Constitution's handler rules exist for. The handler now early-outs through the house guard (TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating or is_undoing) — and because anything may have changed shape by the time the flag clears, it drops the whole geometry store (clear() + _dirty_scan()) instead of trusting per-update info it never saw: marked objects rebuild lazily on their next draw, so an undone modeling change can never leave a stale hull. Cheap: the store only ever holds the marked set, and a clear during a long cascade hits an already-empty dict.

    17. 🟢 AI facade — takes_for_blender/ai/, the scripted-caller entry point (read verbs + switch_take). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-10 in Blender 5.2 over the official Blender MCP bridge: status()/describe() read the user's live production file — 1 scene, 11 view layers — and a take switch driven through the bridge landed correctly in the GUI.) Five modules, top layer, never imported upward into: errors.py (the fixed envelope {ok, api, data, error{code,message,hint}, warnings, undo} + plain-string codes an agent branches on — an enum member would serialise as ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND and break that branch — plus guard(), so no exception ever crosses the bridge as an opaque failure; bpy-free and relative-import-free, so the contract is checkable under a bare interpreter); policy.py (pure decisions: busy_reason splits the three independent busy sources — mutation lock, preload, BG render — because one flag cannot tell an agent whether to retry in a second or in ten minutes; is_stale_lock, TTL 5.0s); session.py (ai_session context manager: owner token + monotonic stamp, _push_undo, engine_state(), reset()); api.py (the verbs); AI_GUIDE.md (shipped INSIDE the extension — verified present at the root of the built ZIP, 469 files, with doc/+dev/ excluded — so help() serves it from the install folder rather than the repo). switch_take is deliberately NOT a thin delegate to tks.activate_vl_version: that operator is a TOGGLE, so calling it on the already-active take would deactivate it, and an agent's most common failure mode is retrying a call it believes timed out — a retry that silently turns the take OFF is exactly the AI-01 lying-to-the-agent shape this facade exists to prevent; here it is a no-op that says so. Bug caught in the guard tests' first real run: _depth was incremented only for mutating sessions but decremented unconditionally, so every read-only session drove it negative and ALL later sessions silently skipped locking and undo — __exit__ now mirrors __enter__. Headless fixtures must normalise TKS_VL_STATE.is_applying: the read_homefile load_post handler sets it and its clearing timer never fires under --background. Verified end-to-end 2026-08-10 by two headless spikes: a natively-assigned world survives two facade-driven take switches under the default ADOPT mode and explain("world") attributes it to the SCENE tier (the accident of 2026-08-09, now closed by the world work); and one switch_take costs exactly one bpy.ops.ed.undo(), labelled AI: Switch take to <name>. Commits 04c0aba, 491463b, 12b3e6e.

    18. 🟢 AI facade — mutating and explanatory verbs (create_take, set_override, clear_override, explain, help, reset). create_take delegates to the engine's own new-take path and returns the template-generated name (the agent cannot predict it, so it must be told). set_override/clear_override validate the value against the real datablocks BEFORE storing: the engine setter stores whatever string it is handed — fine for a picker menu that can only offer real datablocks, but an agent TYPES names, and a typo silently stored as a dangling reference is another quiet lie (the assignment "succeeded" while the cascade resolves to nothing), so a refusal carries the actual candidates. help() introspects the LIVE module via _verb_catalogue() rather than a hand-kept list, so a new verb cannot be missing from the agent's own view of the API; it serves AI_GUIDE.md from the install folder. reset() was found missing during the first real bridge run — help()'s gotchas told agents to call it while it lived unexposed in session.py (12b3e6e). Tests: test_ai_create_explain.py (12), test_ai_set_override.py (12), test_ai_help.py (19). Headless- and bridge-tested; not yet exercised by hand in the GUI. Commits 04c0aba, 491463b, 12b3e6e.

    19. 🟢 Shift+Click moves a multi-selection (roadmap: move-multi-selection). Closes the thread that ran Fixed 27 → 30: arrows disabled in multi-select → group auto-exited the mode → auto-exit reverted and arrows decoupled (act on the highlighted row) → now the arrows can take the selection. TKS_OT_MoveAllViewLayerItem gains use_selection: BoolProperty(options={'SKIP_SAVE'}) set from event.shift in a new invoke() (SKIP_SAVE so a shift-click never leaks into the next plain click); execute() tries _move_selection() first and returns None to fall through to the existing single-row dispatch when fewer than 2 rows are ticked. RULED CONSTRAINT (user): same PARENT, not same level — two VLs share depth 3 whether grouped or not, but _move_vl reorders vlg.members, so same-level-different-container has no single correct reading. _parent_key() returns ('SG', group), ('VLG', scene, group) or ('TAKES', scene, vl); a selection with >1 distinct parent refuses. Mixed row types and group rows (SCENE_GROUP/VL_GROUP) also refuse — all via _refuse_report (Fixed 28), so the status bar explains it. Ordering lives in operators/_tree_ops_core.shift_selection(order, selected, direction) — pure list arithmetic, no bpy: each selected entry moves one step but only swaps with a NON-selected neighbour, so a contiguous run travels as a unit and an edge-blocked entry stops the rest of its run; relative order is invariant. This answers the old non-contiguous open question with no special case (rows 2/5/7 each advance one). apply_order() writes back via collection.move() so element identity survives. Containers: sg.members / vlg.members / take_set.versions, resolved by _selection_container(). Tooltip rewritten to describe both clicks, de_DE in lockstep (INFO-09). 15 tests (11 pure ordering + 4 bpy end-to-end incl. cross-group refusal and single-tick fallback). NOTE: two self-inflicted stumbles caught by those tests — a dirty fixture (a leftover scene tick made the selection 'mixed', which the code correctly refused) and a relative import one level too deep (..._tree_ops_core from operators/context/, where groups/ needs three dots and context/ two). Suite 1734. Commit b1dc139.

    20. 🟢 Highlight/selection coherence for the block move (follows Added 19). Three coupled parts, all user-ruled: (a) Leading-edge highlight — after _move_selection, the tree index lands on the topmost ticked row for UP and the bottommost for DOWN, i.e. the row in front and the one a following plain click would move. (b) Highlight follows the tick — _on_row_ticked (panels/context/properties.py) wired as update= on Scene.tks_selected and ViewLayer.tks_selected, reacting ONLY on the True edge so a batch clear (consume_multiselect, Select None) does not drag the blue bar around. Resolves the row via the shared selection_owner(). (c) Arrow gate ORs both clicks — the arrows serve plain (highlighted row) and Shift (selection), so draw_tree enables each direction when EITHER can use it; a highlight parked outside the selection (classically on the bottom row) previously greyed out a direction the block could still travel. Impossible clicks report via _refuse_report, so a half-live arrow is honest rather than dead. Availability is computed by block_can_move(items, selected_idx, depth_of, boundary) — a direction survives while ANY selected row has a non-selected sibling that way, exactly mirroring shift_selection. Asking only the leading row dims too early: in a GAPPED selection the topmost can be pinned at the edge while the ones behind still close up, needing further clicks (user's requirement: 'must click again … then it greys out'). Also fixed in passing: the selection path returned early from execute() and skipped notify_move_completed(), so the 4 Hz timer's index-snap guard was never armed and the new highlight was undone ~250 ms later; it now shares the single-move tail. _selection_owner promoted to _tree_ops_core.selection_owner + selected_indices() so the panel can reuse them (panels↔operators is a lateral, same-tier import). 11 new tests (5 pure block_can_move, 6 bpy). Test hygiene: the module-level pytest.mark.pure was sweeping the bpy tests into Blender-free runs — markers are per-test now. Suite 1745. Commit a3d9254.

    21. Take-data safety copy with automatic restore. The take/group store, Variant Switch products, Tag Library and Inspector watchlist all live on a carrier World (utils/store_world.py), so deleting or purging every World erased them. utils/store_snapshot.py mirrors all four to <presets>/snapshots/<uid>/<utc>.json; core/store_guardian.py decides when. Triggers: health-gated generation on load, one synchronous flush in save_pre, and a 2s heartbeat that is the ONLY routine writer (actions set a dirty flag, never write), so a cascade touching fifty takes costs one atomic tmp+os.replace write and an idle session none. File identity is a uuid4 stamped HIDDEN on every Scene - never only the carrier, whose death is the event being defended against - and candidates() falls back to matching the .blend path when a uid was re-minted. Carrier gets use_fake_user. Retention: 5 generations, dropped when a file closes matching its copy (load_pre), plus a 30-day sweep for sessions that never closed cleanly.

    22. Snapshots & Recovery preferences. New collapsible section under Data > Storage (preferences/draw_data_storage.py): store_restore_confirm (default False) and a read-only snapshots path with the same open-folder row shape as the storage tiers.
    23. NEEDS_RESTORE gate on the AI facade. A scripted caller can clear bpy.data.worlds in one line and never see a panel, and the tree then rebuilds itself flat so the file still looks usable. ai/errors.guard() refuses every acting verb with the new NEEDS_RESTORE code while an offer stands; status/describe/help stay open (an agent that cannot look cannot report), and restore_takes() / keep_current_takes() are the two ways out. The message names the constraint a human needs: Takes keeps its store on a World, so at least one must remain in the .blend.
    24. 🟢 Variant Switch Live Apply. features/variant_switch/live_apply.py: while armed, every look-changing edit re-applies the EDIT state (product.active_index) to the viewport, debounced through the DeferredSync timer — never from draw, never through bpy.ops on the timer path (variant_ui_block_corruption.md). Apply is total+idempotent, so disarm = apply the cascade-resolved variant on top, no snapshot. Dirty markers: part visibility, pool index, collection assignment, structural add/remove/reorder, edit-state pick; browsing (rename, chevrons, ticks, selection) deliberately never applies. Companion behaviors: LIVE column in the tree rows (ui_row_renderers.py), list frozen during a live switch (panel.py), autokey guard bound where I actually fires (operators.py), Live no longer auto-disarming behind the user (ops_crud.py), toggle moved in with the other modes (panels/navigation/panel.py). Merge 15b999c2 (branch daeb7cb5..0641cd32).
    25. 🟢 Camera cross-scene link repair (D3). core/camera_link.py (pure, bpy-free, tested standalone in dev/tests/test_camera_link.py): classify_inherited_camera() → NONE / INHERITED_OK / INHERITED_UNLINKED, link_scope_scenes() → SCENE/GROUP/ALL coverage. Consumers: operators/cascade/ops_link_camera.py::TKS_OT_LinkInheritedCamera (links mirroring collection placement, refires the camera cascade, invalidates vl_cascade via the cache registry), repair entry in the cascade picker menu (menus_picker.py, under (Clear)), and the camera popover swaps Add→Fix on the red-flag state (ops_viewlayer_camera.py, ops_camera_levels.py, draw_layers.py). Merge 62371ed6 (branch 8ec94579..f2d61c71); post-merge repairs in 90fb609b (take_index/'TAKE' rename fallout, i18n templates — see doc/troubleshooting/stale_branch_merge_fallout.md).
    26. 🟢 Mode toggle pie (Shift+Alt+Q). panels/pie_menus/modes.py::TKS_MT_PIE_Modes, structured on channels.py. State comes from the new panels/mode_toggles.py — one read-only mode_entries(context) -> [ModeToggle(key, label, icon, on, available, op, props)], so the pie cannot drift from the navigation header's enable rules. Availability is a guard, not decoration, and reproduces all seven header rules: tks.rest_mode_toggle.poll() (no rest action), bool(bpy.data.scenes) for Still, core.vl_preload.is_preloading() holding the Value Lock, not vlock and not rest_on for Autokey, resolve_still(scene, view_layer) for Timeline Sync, tks.vsw_live_apply.poll() (a vsw World with ≥1 product) for Variant Live, and core.store_guardian.recovery_pending() closing all of them. An unavailable mode renders pie.separator() — hide-don't-grey, per keyframe_pies.py:113-119: Blender can only disable a pie slot by wrapping it in pie.row(), which strips the native pie styling, and the eight directions must stay positionally stable. Two slices needed their own answer: Still is tri-state and its header button opens TKS_MT_StillGlobal from invoke() (value='MENU'), so it contributes THREE slot ids (STILL/STILL_ANIM/STILL_OFF) each passing an explicit value, with the active state's slice sending OFF so Off is one click from anywhere; Timeline Sync is a WM property, so it rides wm.context_toggle with data_path="window_manager.tks_timeline_sync" and stays a real pie button. Keymap: 3D View/VIEW_3D, addon kc only — never Window (Blender 5.x dispatches Window from user kc alone, so an addon-kc entry there reads active=True and never fires, keyframe_keymap.py:273-277), never keymap_items.new() on wm.keyconfigs.user (Blender's rebuild pass wipes is_user_defined items wholesale), matched by idname + properties.name and never by key combo. Shift+Alt+Q avoids Ctrl+Alt (German AltGr sends it); Q alone is Quick Favourites. Master-off deactivates the kmi instead of removing it, preserving a rebind. panels/navigation/panel.py deliberately untouched — feat/vsw-live-apply was rewriting that row — so pointing the header at the shared reader is the follow-up. 27 tests in dev/tests/test_mode_pie.py, four of which run the real draw() body against a recording layout (headless Blender cannot open a pie): eight children always emitted, the West slot drawing the West mode, a held-off mode leaving its slot empty. Commits 39b4638f, 91655024, 85d4b9c8.

    27. 🟢 Mode Pie preferences section. MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS (addon_prefs_constants.py, 8 entries + NONE) + TKS_ModePiePropsMixin (preferences/props/props_mode_pie.py, 8 direction enums with _resolve_mode_pie_duplicates de-dup and the is_prefs_loading() guard), mode_pie_enabled in props_misc.py (default False; update= autosaves then queries the keymaps.sync_mode_pie provider — must return None, see _update_navigation_pie), expand_pie_modes in props_logging.py + ACCORDION_GROUPS. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 537→547 with a reason line; indexed in prefs_search.py under WORKFLOW/PIE. Slot enums rather than overlay_mode_*-style booleans: that shape answers presence AND order in one control, where booleans on top would give two competing ways to hide a mode. The configurator reuses the generic _draw_pie_grid (ui_draw_hotkeys.py:254), so the rebindable hotkey centre and the Reset button come from the existing tks.reset_pie_hotkey / tks.reset_pie_grid — no new operator, hence no manual_map.py operator entry (only the two pref entries). _PIE_HOTKEY_DEFAULTS gains TKS_MT_PIE_Modes: ('Q', False, True, True), asserted against the kmi we actually create. i18n gotcha recorded in doc/roadmap/_dev/mode-pie.md: i18n_extract harvests text= kwargs and texts/ constants but NOT module-level item lists, so MODE_PIE_SLOT_ITEMS labels are invisible to the drift guard — the Still slices therefore reuse features/still_mode/menus.py wording verbatim ("Still Mode"/"Animation"/"Off (per-take)"), which already carries German. 14 new strings translated in de_DE.py; extractor reports 0 untracked / 0 orphans.

    28. 🟢 Bulk switches for the logging topics. TKS_OT_ToggleAllLogTopics (preferences/ops_misc.py), drawn as a pair above the topic stack in draw_debug.py. scope is TOPICS or SUBTOPICS; state is TOGGLE (the button) / ON / OFF (a scripted caller). Deliberately NOT click-only (Constitution rule 7): it writes preference booleans and opens nothing, so a script gets exactly what a click gets — unlike TKS_OT_ToggleLogTopic beside it, whose behaviour depends on modifier keys and which correctly refuses. The switch list is read from RNA, not hardcoded. It already exists in three places (properties, drawer, accordion-flag tuple) and drifting them apart is the class of bug CORR-16 and MAINT-08 exist to catch; a fourth copy would be a fourth thing to forget. The log_topic_ / log_sub_ prefix test excludes expand_log_topic_*, which is accordion state. One disk write, not 63. Every logging property carries update=_autosave_preferences, which saves the WHOLE config, so a bulk flip of 63 switches would have been 63 JSON writes — the same shape as the keymap tick fixed in entry 99. New persistence_io.suspended_autosave() context manager (re-entrant; the outermost exit saves once) guards it. Icons read the live state, so the button says what the click will do rather than always claiming "all on". Manual-map entry added (INFO-04), de_DE +2.

    29. 🟢 Camera Links navigation warning (camera-cross-scene-linking P3). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-16.) Detector core/camera_link_scan.py::find_camera_link_gaps() — read-only scan of the scene-spanning camera tiers (Global via master.tks_global_camera, each SG via sg.tks_camera) returning {camera, source, group_name, missing_scenes} per gap; broken references (name with no CAMERA object) are excluded — that is assignment_health's domain. Cached in panels/navigation/panel.py (_camera_link_cache, the standard dirty-flag dict, wired into invalidate_nav_warnings()); writers bump nav_warnings from tks.set_cascade_prop (CAMERA branch, _picker.py) and tks.link_inherited_camera (ops_link_camera.py). Subpanel panels/navigation/warnings/camera_links.py::draw_camera_link_warnings — per camera: missing-scene rows each with a [Link] (tks.link_inherited_camera, scope SCENE) plus a link-all footer (scope GROUP for SG entries / ALL for Global; the linker's already-linked skip guard makes over-coverage harmless). WM toggle tks_show_camera_link_warnings joins _warn_props mutual exclusion, CAMERA_DATA badge with the inverted-alert idiom. Manual-map entry; de_DE in lockstep. Tests: dev/tests/test_camera_link_gaps.py (3).

    30. 🟢 camera_link_warning_mode preference (P4). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-16.) EnumProperty ALWAYS/ACTIVE_SCENE (default ALWAYS) in props_automations.py beside the camera-handling enums, drawn via draw_split_prop_row in the Cameras section (§11.2); prefs-search row; tooltip const PROP_ADDONPREFERENCES_CAMERA_LINK_WARNING_MODE. ACTIVE_SCENE filters per draw through the pure core/camera_link.py::gaps_touching_scene() — a list scan, so active-scene switches need no cache invalidation. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 560 → 561.     31. 🟢 Render queue pre-render skip visibility (P5). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-16.) New read-only twin of the camera pre-flight: features/batch_render/queue_camera_check.py — a CacheCell over topics ("vl_cascade", "nav_warnings") mapping (scene, vl) → reason, built on the shared resolver batch_render_preflight.resolve_task_camera() (extracted from _validate_tasks_cameras so marker and gate cannot disagree). Queue rows (render_queue_lists.py, PENDING branch, gated on vl.use) show "Will skip" via the tks.rq_stat_tooltip carrier with the reason on hover; render_queue_panel.py draws an INFO summary ("N takes will be skipped — camera missing") between the stats strip and the list. The pre-flight FAILED reason now distinguishes 'Camera not linked in scene' from 'No camera assigned'. Draw cost: one dict get per row.
