    32. 🟢 world_needed_warning preference (opt-in "no World" warning). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) BoolProperty on AutomationsPropsMixin, default False, drawn in Workflow > Automations > World under world_adopt_tier (Adopt mode only) and registered in prefs_search. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 561 -> 562. The reminder used to fire unconditionally in ADOPT mode; a scene with no World is an ordinary deliberate setup, so it is now a reminder for people who asked for it rather than a fault report for everyone. The gate lives in the SCAN (core/cascade_drift.py::_world_needed_warning_enabled), not the draw, so with it off the drift is never raised at all - no panel, no toggle lighting up, no cost. _on_world_needed_warning_changed emits NAV_WARNINGS_INVALIDATE + signal_redraw() so ticking the box shows the result of ticking the box (the nav panel caches its warning scan), and the scan gained an elif scene.world is None fallback for scenes the cascade has not visited this session - the tracker-keyed branch can only speak for scenes it has already witnessed, which is exactly not the scene the user just ticked the box in. Commit bfbccae6.

    33. 🟢 Pick Tag render scope — tags become a render-selection axis (roadmap: pick-tag-render). build_task_list() (features/batch_render/batch_render_task_builder.py) gains tag_filter=None, applied inside _keep_vl as a single string compare against the VL's OWN tks_assigned_tag. VL-only by user ruling 2026-08-18 — scene, VL-group and scene-group tags are deliberately INERT here, unlike the tree's Filter-by-Tag popover which matches upward (a scene shows because a child VL matches). The two axes read the same property and must not be assumed to share semantics: the tree filter answers "what should I look at", the render filter answers "what should I render", and inheritance would silently queue every layer of a tagged scene. Menu: TKS_MT_RenderTagPick / TKS_MT_RenderTagPickForce (panels/pie_menus/render_scope.py) mirror the Pick Scene pair one-to-one — FG/BG read live from wm.tks_render_mode, rows grey out on a 0 count, counts come from _scope_task_count(wm, action, tag_name=...) routing through the REAL builder so a shown number cannot drift from what execute() renders. _assigned_vl_tags() sweeps view layers only and orders by tag-library category order, appending library-orphaned tag strings so a stale assignment stays reachable rather than becoming unrenderable. Both "Pick Tag" rows sit under their Pick Scene sibling and disable (not hide) when no VL carries a tag — a hidden row reads as a missing feature, a greyed one as an empty state; the sweep runs once per menu draw, never on the panel redraw path. Dispatch: actions TAG_PICK / TAG_PICK_FORCE + a tag_name StringProperty on TKS_OT_RenderScopeDispatch (render_scope_ops.py, HIDDEN+SKIP_SAVE like scene_name), with a matching description() branch so the row tooltip names the tag. Both batch operators (TKS_OT_BatchRender, TKS_OT_BatchRenderBG[Fast]) expose tag_filter and thread it to the builder, so the capability is scripted-reachable without the menu (AI-01 clean — no click-only path was created). Deliberately deferred: multi-tag OR selection, a tag search popup, and an F12 pie slot (pie slots are fixed actions; a picker needs a submenu, and a dynamic enum there would require utils/enum_cache.retained_enum). No PointerProperty anywhere — tag identity is the name string, and properties/tag_library.py already migrates every assignment on rename. TDD: dev/tests/test_batch_tag_filter.py (4 — own-tag match with scene tag proven inert, force/no-filter composition, count routing for both actions, operator RNA exposure) written first and watched fail on all four before the implementation. Full suite 2137 passed (Blender 5.2, worktree build via BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS). de_DE re-keyed in lockstep (INFO-09): 6 new strings. Commit 7f870c04, branch feature/pick-tag-render.

    34. 🟢 Sequencer Take Follow — the playhead drives the cascade. features/sequencer/: follow_core.py (pure pick_strip/binding_of/should_apply), engine.py (apply_binding = apply_overrides(skip_action=True) + apply_vl_switch_unified + the variant provider, addressed at a scene the window is NOT showing), handlers.py (a 0.1s timer for scrubbing, because frame_change_post does not fire while a sequencer timeline is dragged, plus a frame_change_pre handler for playback, where 41ms/frame at 24fps outruns any timer). Blender 5.2 API notes: SceneStrip.view_layer is new in 5.2, and sed.strips replaced sequences — an EMPTY strip collection is FALSY, so getattr(sed,'strips',None) or sed.sequences crashes; matched with hasattr. The frame cache is held off while the follow drives (use_prefetch/use_cache_raw/use_cache_final): a cached frame keeps the take it was rendered with and is the one thing that makes a correct follow look broken.

    35. 🟢 Sequencer Scene Auto-Switch (sequencer_scene_autoswitch, default True). A Window shows exactly one Scene, and SpaceSequenceEditor has NO scene property of its own — verified against RNA on 5.2. So a sequencer always shows the ACTIVE scene, and while that scene holds no strips the follow has nothing to follow. tks.sequencer_focus_switch moves the window to the scene that owns the strips. ON by default unlike the follow itself: shipping it off ships the follow broken. timeline_target / switch_to_timeline are PLAIN functions the timer calls directly — an operator invoked from a timer can refuse on context, and reaching it through bpy.ops is what made the frame-detected triggers look dead while the detector was correctly reporting movement.

    36. 🟢 Five triggers, separately switchable (sequencer_autoswitch_on, ENUM_FLAG). HOVER/CLICK/PLAY arrive via keymap items carrying their rung in an operator StringProperty — an EnumProperty always carries a value, which would make "no trigger" inexpressible and filter the sidebar button as a hover. SCRUB and ARROWS come from the timer, told apart by screen.is_scrubbing: a drag is the playhead, a bare frame change is a key. Keymap placement is the whole lesson — SequencerCommon sits behind the region maps; the scrub bar's press is consumed by anim.change_frame modally; arrows live in the GLOBAL Frames map where Blender binds screen.frame_offset. Five routes were measured with the operator's own arrival log. A key press has no location, so the operator's context.area check is the right filter and a global binding is safe; a CLICK carries one the guard cannot see, which is why a Frames LEFTMOUSE entry made every click a playhead gesture and had to be removed.

    37. 🟢 The way back (tks.sequencer_go_back). Restores the (scene, view layer) the switch took you from, remembered by NAME — a remembered scene can be deleted while you are away, and a stale pointer would crash where a name declines. It APPLIES the destination via engine.apply_binding rather than only repointing the window: the scope that protects the move is the same thing that suppresses the depsgraph handler which would otherwise run the cascade, so the change is delivered while suppressed and nothing is left to trigger it. Field report with pictures — the shared cube kept the strip's Mat_C_Purple until it was clicked in the viewport.

    38. 🟢 Optional automatic return (sequencer_autoswitch_back, default False; sequencer_autoswitch_back_on = HOVER/CLICK). OFF by default: with both halves on, the window follows the mouse between the two editors and every crossing runs a full cascade. Known interaction, documented rather than fixed — with ONE shared datablock across scenes the viewport and the VSE preview cannot show different takes at once, so returning re-applies the origin's take and the preview then renders the strip with it.

    39. 🟢 Sequencer sidebar (TKS_PT_SequencerTakes). Names the binding under the playhead and the one actually applied when they differ, warns when the frame cache is on with a one-click fix, and tells the two silences apart: "no strip under the playhead" (on the timeline, between cuts) versus "this scene has no strips" (not on it at all), the latter with a Go To Timeline button running the SAME operator as the keymap and a scripted caller.

    Changed¶

    1. 🟢 Internal: removed the orphan get_entries_for_id helper from the rest cache — no behavior change. Auditor MAINT-01 (orphan top-level functions): features/rest_state/rest_cache.py::get_entries_for_id lost its only caller when the rest-revert evidence-gate fix removed revert_snap's rest-cache fallback (Fixed entry 1, commit 69ba211); verified zero callers on main — the remaining references on the stale feat/* worktree branches predate that fix, so a merge takes main's caller-free revert_snap.py. Full suite 1294 passed / 0 failed post-removal. Commit 62eecac.
    2. 🟢 Internal: test_undo_removes_object is locale-agnostic — no behavior change. The test asserted the hardcoded English name "Cube" after primitive_cube_add, which fails on installations where Blender translates new data names (German UI creates "Würfel" — surfaced once the i18n pilot put the dev machine on de_DE). The add is now detected via the IDSnapshot delta, the same mechanism the test's undo assertion already uses. Commit 348bd33.

    3. 🟢 Internal: draw_wrapped_paragraph honors manual line breaks — no visible change until a text uses one. New pure seam ui/styles.py::split_paragraphs: \n in an INFOBOX_* constant starts a new wrapped line, a blank line becomes a paragraph gap (separator(factor=1.2)), blank runs collapse, and whitespace-only text still draws nothing — the empty-body wrapped_info_box call in the autokey-blocked warning depends on that. Authors control info-box layout from texts/infoboxes.py without touching draw code (previously wrap_measured's text.split() swallowed newlines like spaces). 4 tests beside the other wrap tests in test_naming_validation.py; suite 1214 passed. Commit c5d756c.

    4. 🟢 Internal: phase 1 of the texts/ centralization campaign — 18 sites migrated, plus the tool that does it. New dev/scripts/apply_text_centralization.py: reads the auditor's INFO-09 rows (kind / file / line / target module), lifts the literal at each site via AST anchors, appends NAME = <text verbatim> to the destination texts/ module and rewrites the site to reference it, adding or extending the relative import. Dry-run by default; --kind / --area scope a batch; already-migrated sites are skipped so re-runs are no-ops. Phase 1 cleared bl_description (9 → 0) and the static infobox_literal sites (11 → 2; the 2 survivors are f-strings needing a template constant): 18 constants across infoboxes.py, tooltips_preferences.py, tooltips_misc.py, tooltips_batch_render.py, tooltips_render_presets.py. Two tool bugs caught by tests before they shipped: (a) Blender's property syntax is an ANNOTATION (prop: BoolProperty(...)), so the Call hangs off .annotation not .value — every prop_desc constant would otherwise be named PROP_<CLASS> with no property segment; (b) the texts import must be placed after the last top-level import located via AST — a line-scan inserted INSIDE a parenthesised multi-line import and split it (features/smart_syntax/registry.py). Multi-line implicit-concat literals are now refused outright (splicing head+name+tail across the span drops the separating comma — it produced invalid Python at registry.py:662 on the first run) and reported for hand migration. 15 tool tests in dev/tests/test_text_centralization_tool.py; full suite 1341 passed on Blender 5.2; auditor re-scan 619 → 601 findings with orphans unchanged at 31 (a rewrite that stranded a constant would show up there). Remaining: 196 prop_desc, 403 op_docstring (phase 4 — ADD bl_description, keep __doc__), 2 f-strings, 31 orphans. Plan: dev/plan_text_centralization.md. Commit bd698c9.

    5. 🟢 Internal: phase 2 — 143 single-line property descriptions centralized (prop_desc). Same REPLACE mode as phase 1: the description= literal at each property definition becomes a PROP_* constant in the matching texts module and the site references it. INFO-09 prop_desc 196 → 53 (the multi-line remainder closed in Changed entry 9). Commit 4ae54c2. (Backfilled — this mirror entry was missed when the user-facing entry landed in e0854e5.)

    6. 🟢 Internal: the i18n collector harvests texts/ module constants. dev/scripts/i18n_extract.py walked draw/property/operator sites only, so a centralized string went invisible the moment migration replaced its literal with a constant reference — roughly 500 already-centralized strings were missing from the catalog. The collector now walks the texts/ package's module-level string assigns as first-class sources; _pending.py regenerated to record the newly-visible strings. Commits db2638e, 0199796. (Backfilled, same gap as entry 5.)

    7. 🟢 Internal: phase 3 — 403 operator tooltips centralized (op_docstring). Blender promotes cls.__doc__ to the tooltip only while bl_description is absent, so 403 operators were shipping their developer docstring as user-facing UI. New ADD mode in dev/scripts/apply_text_centralization.py: instead of replacing a literal it inserts bl_description = OP_<NAME> directly after bl_idname at matching indentation and copies the RAW docstring value (ast.get_docstring(clean=True) re-indents, which would silently change the tooltip); the docstring stays for developers. Idempotent — skips classes already declaring bl_description, and those with no docstring (nothing to move). 403 constants across 9 texts modules (195 → tooltips_misc; splitting that module by area stays open), 109 files. Verified NAMESPACE-AWARE: each of the 403 constants resolved through its own file's import and compared to that class's docstring — 0 wrong tooltips. (A flat cross-module check first reported 2 false mismatches: OP_VLVVARIANTPOPOVER and OP_RENAMEITEM legitimately exist in two modules with different text; each site imports the correct one and no module defines a name twice.) Two follow-up fixes in 240e456: (a) the import must land after the HEADER import block, not the last import in the file — features/bookmarks/operators.py carries a second block at line 222, so the constant was referenced at class-body evaluation before its import ran (NameError → whole feature failed to register → 8 cascading failures); a repair pass over all 109 files found it as the only case, and a regression test drives the shape. (b) The i18n guard correctly flagged 403 untracked strings: the collector harvests texts/ but not docstrings, so centralizing made these tooltips translatable for the first time — _pending.py regenerated 283 → 686.     14. 🟢 Native world assignment reconciles immediately and lands on the most specific governing tier. Inside the cascade, the WITNESS rule gates everything: scene.world counts as user intent only when it differs from the last cascade-applied value — un-witnessed states follow the tree (Alt-click tier clear removes the world; a take-switch winner change applies the new winner instead of adopting the stale one). A witnessed pick lands on the MOST SPECIFIC of (winning tier, adopt tier): a Take/VL/VLG override is updated in place (the drift-Accept write shape), otherwise the configured tier — so a Properties pick never silently reverts, and world drift rows with a non-None native world are suppressed in ADOPT (they all self-resolve).     26. 🟢 Batch delete: partial selections now ask instead of greying (field report: 'why is delete greyed when I select VLs with different parents'). Diagnosis: not about parents at all. draw_tree's multiselect branch computed an all-or-nothing can_remove — for VLs, every scene had to keep at least one across the WHOLE selection, so ticking the sole VL of one scene vetoed the batch; a scene ticked alongside a VL also failed multiselect_only_vls and disabled the button. Meanwhile TKS_OT_DeleteSelectedContextItems.execute ALREADY trimmed those cases (sel = sel[:-1], same for scenes) and would have deleted the remainder — i.e. the panel vetoed work the operator was happy to do, contradicting Constitution rule 6 (auto-filter, process the valid, report the skips). Fix: _build_plan(context) returns the exact lists (takes/vls/scenes/vlgs/sgs) plus human-readable skipped reasons; invoke builds it, reports and CANCELs when nothing is deletable, and otherwise opens an invoke_props_dialog whose draw lists both halves; execute consumes the SAME plan (a scripted call builds its own), so the summary agreed to is the work done. The dialog is forced whenever skipped is non-empty even if confirm_delete_take is off, because then the outcome differs from the request. Panel gate relaxed to remove_col.enabled = multiselect_any_selected. New user-facing strings routed through pgettext_iface/pgettext_rpt with 5 de_DE entries (both i18n guards initially failed: untracked strings + composed f-strings). 4 bpy tests. PROCESS NOTES: the first scripted insertion landed the whole block in TKS_OT_DeleteTake — an earlier class with a byte-identical invoke — and .replace(..., 1) took the first match; caught by the tests, extracted and re-inserted by line position. Test fixture also had to clear stale ticks (third time this session a dirty selection fixture skewed a result). Suite 1754. Commit c8f52f7.

    27. 🟢 All view layers ticked escalates to deleting the scene (revises Changed 26). Probe (bpy.context.scene.view_layers.remove(...), Blender 5.2) confirms the engine refuses: RuntimeError: View layer 'ViewLayer' could not be removed from scene 'PROBE'. So 26's "keep one back" was working around a hard constraint rather than a policy. _build_plan() in operators/context/ops_versions.py now collects such scenes into escalate and folds them into plan['scenes'], with plan['escalated'] driving a separate ERROR-icon box in draw() so the blast radius is stated before the OK. Backstop kept where Blender's own is: if nothing would survive, the last doomed scene is popped back and its view layers fall back to a plain VL delete minus one, both reasons pushed to plan['skipped']. Ordering matters — escalation runs before the last-scene check, and the scene section now runs even under a VL type filter, since escalation can produce scene deletions from a VL-only selection.

Wired into create_take, add_viewlayer (both exits), add_scene_to_group (both exits); the variant adds gain _select_new_row() (they already force-expanded); tag_add_new expands its group before selecting.

    31. 🟢 Group creation missed the reveal contract (field: "why is the adding new child not working the same way for rules and tags? This has to work the same way for all lists"). Re-audit: the Rule Library and Tag Library are ONE list in two modes, sharing tks.tag_add_new (contract added in Changed 30) and tks.tag_group_create, which still ended at sync_tag_tree() - no expand, no selection. Group creation now expands the new group and selects its header via a shared _select_tag_row() helper both creators use, so the paths cannot drift apart again.

    32. 🟢 State deletion now carries a blast-radius count (user ruling: "the deletion has to be confirmed and the popup should inform the user about the loose of assignments. The amount should be visible"). TKS_OT_VSW_TreeDelete.invoke used invoke_confirm, which renders bl_label and nothing else - it cannot carry a count line. The STATE branch now computes count_state_assignments() and, when non-zero, opens invoke_props_dialog with an alert count row plus a kind='status' wrapped_info_box (never gated, unlike kind='warning', so the number cannot be hidden by "Show Warning Details"). The count decision is made BEFORE the confirm_delete_variant short-circuit into execute() - that preference silences a routine confirm, not a data-loss count - pinned by test_delete_dialog_ignores_the_confirm_preference. execute() re-counts from live data rather than trusting the stashed number, so an EXEC_DEFAULT scripted call reports identically (Constitution rule 7); the count is reported as {'WARNING'}. Wording in texts/infoboxes.py (INFOBOX_VSW_STATE_DELETE_ASSIGNMENTS), re-keyed in de_DE in lockstep. Commit 8041ef13.

    33. 🟢 The reveal missed a second expansion storage (field: "No, not working for rules and tag library" after Changed 31). This tree keeps expansion in TWO places: a GROUP owns is_expanded, a CATEGORY expands through a window-manager flag tks_tree_expand_<type> (driven by tks.tagtree_toggle_expand). Setting only the group left a collapsed category shut and the new row hidden - in both Rule and Tag mode, one list. New _expand_tag_ancestors() opens both and is shared by tag_add_new and tag_group_create. +3 tests (incl. no-group and unknown-category safety).

    34. 🟢 Native .001 handling for duplicate tag / rule / group names (user ruling: "naming the tags the same is a problem... apply the native behavior here", "same goes for the rules" - one list, two modes). A tag is referenced BY NAME from scenes, VLs, takes and variant products, so duplicates made every reference ambiguous (the field log's rename chains). Reuses the house unique_group_name(); uniqueness is CATEGORY-wide (groups included - a group is not part of a reference); tag GROUP names get their own handler. Gated precisely (undo/redo + the flat-to-grouped migration) rather than by the broad addon_is_mutating, since this is data integrity. Collision detection COUNTS occurrences instead of comparing PropertyGroup wrappers - != on elements is unreliable after a collection reallocates (CRASH-08 hazard) and silently disabled the rule under churn; the two owner lookups use same-frame as_pointer() (# PTR-OK). +6 tests, wiring asserted against the source because the suite can hold two module objects for this file.

    35. 🟢 Native .001 naming in the Variant Switch (user ruling: "also the vsw should follow the native naming convention"). States, parts and material pools unique within their product; products across the file - a cascade token is literally <product_name>:<variant_index>, so duplicate products make every stored assignment ambiguous. The product rule existed but compared wrappers (p != self), unreliable after a reallocation - now counts occurrences like the tag rule. Owner lookup uses same-frame as_pointer() (# PTR-OK). +5 tests.

    36. 🟢 Five drawn controls had no wiki page (INFO-01 coverage + own_page + routing, 10 findings). tks.render_jobs_drag_resize and the four camera/world "needed" row chips (tks.camera_needed_pick / _new, tks.world_needed_pick / _new) were drawn in UI whose page documented neither. New features/cascade.md#needed-rows section covering both chips and the fact that they write to the tier the World handling / Camera handling preference nominates rather than a fixed one; a paragraph in features/batch_render.md#render-jobs for the corner grip (Blender popups cannot live-resize, so the drag is a modal preview and the width lands in the preferences). All five wired in doc/reports/data/wire_assignments.json + utils/manual_map.py, closing the routing dead-end on right-click → Online Manual.

      Failed approach. Regenerating manual_map.py with dev/scripts/apply_wire_assignments.py wired the five correctly and ALSO rewrote 28 unrelated entries from anchored to bare page URLs, because the stats snapshot it reads no longer resolves those anchors. Reverted; the five were placed by hand in alphabetical position and survive a future regeneration because wire_assignments.json carries them. Wiki commit b508dc2.

    37. 🟢 Retarget offered destinations that moved nothing, and hid the one that mattered. Two defects in one dropdown. It listed the group the tag was ALREADY in, so the obvious pick was a no-op; and "Ungrouped" was not a destination at all — a single id, "__UNGROUPED__", served as both the "Select a Group" placeholder AND the value execute() reads as "move it out of its group", which execute() then rejected as "No group selected". Moving a tag OUT of a group was unreachable from the dialog. The ids are now distinct (RETARGET_PLACEHOLDER / RETARGET_UNGROUPED), and _tag_group_helpers.retarget_destinations() computes what is reachable from the tags that would actually move (tags_to_retarget(): the multi-selection, else the active row). It drops any destination that would move nothing — the group they are all in, and "Ungrouped" when none of them is grouped. With a single group that yields exactly the user's rule: a grouped tag is offered Ungrouped, an ungrouped tag is offered the group. poll() reads the same function (and poll_message_sets when there is nowhere to go), so what is offered and what is accepted cannot diverge.

    38. 🟢 The Retarget dialog opened pre-aimed. invoke() preselected the only group when the category had one — which, for a tag already inside it, meant the dialog defaulted to the no-op above — and otherwise recalled _last_retarget_group[cat_type]. It now always opens on the placeholder. The per-category memory goes with it; the wiki sentence promising it is updated in the same push.

    39. 🟢 Solo-accordion toggle icons swapped for the sequencer pair. preferences/addon_prefs.py header draw: the accordion_solo_mode toggle drew SOLO_ON/SOLO_OFF (audio-solo glyphs, unrelated to what the toggle does). Now SEQ_SEQUENCER when solo is on and SEQ_STRIP_DUPLICATE when off. Draw-only literal swap — no logic, property, label or tooltip change; both literals are valid UILayout.prop(icon=…) enum members on 5.2.

    40. Panels lock while a restore is pending. Context, Inspector, Globals and Batch Render set layout.enabled = False; the navigation warning-badge cluster and every warning subpanel are suppressed outright (each carries a fix that would edit the flat rebuild), and the mode cluster greys out. Modes are deliberately NOT force-toggled: Rest and Still Mode "off" are real data operations. Locked rather than hidden so the user can still see what they had. Both messages draw once, in the navigation panel (panels/navigation/warnings/system_store_block.py); recovery_pending() lives in core/store_guardian.py so features/ can read it without importing panels/ (ARCH-01).
    41. 🟢 Assign-time camera dialog retired — picks dispatch directly (P1; in-app confirmed 2026-08-16; supersedes the July design recorded in Added 25 / Fixed 100). TKS_OT_LinkCameraAndAssign + _draw_confirm_menu/_open_confirm_menu removed from operators/cascade/ops_link_camera.py (registry entries in panels/context/_class_registry.py + context_popovers.py, tooltip const, manual-map row and 8 de_DE strings dropped in lockstep). The picker (menus_picker.py) loses the covered-scenes ERROR marks, "(missing in N scenes)" suffixes and the INVOKE_DEFAULT routing — every item calls tks.set_cascade_prop; the engine's silent skip of unlinked Global/SG winners (core/cascade.py:851-857, assignment preserved) is now the contract, surfaced by the tree flag + Camera Links warning. KEPT: tks.link_inherited_camera (now also the warning's repair; additionally bumps nav_warnings), _link_camera_into_scenes, _camera_home_collection, and the picker's "Link '' into this scene" entry. AI drivability win: the dialog's poll refused windowless callers; direct assign is headless-safe (pinned by test_camera_assign_direct.py, which replaces test_link_camera_confirm.py).
    42. 🟢 Tooltip + popover explain the inherit gap (P2). (In-app confirmed 2026-08-16.) tks.vl_camera_popover.description() gains the resolved-but-unlinked branch: "Can't inherit here: not linked into '' — this take is skipped" (Rule 71.253 dynamic tooltip). The VL popover body draws an INFO line ("Can't inherit '%s' — not linked into this scene") beside the existing Add→Fix swap; _warn_camera_not_in_all_scenes (_helpers.py, Global/SG popovers) reworded informational — "Won't inherit in: … (not linked)", INFO icon instead of ERROR. de_DE re-keyed in lockstep.
    43. 🟢 Prefs Cameras section: visual gap before the visibility family. preferences/draw_workflow.py: col.separator(factor=PREFS_TITLE_GAP) between camera_link_warning_mode (last of the native-handling split rows) and auto_camera_visibility — the dropdown trio and the visibility switch family read as two groups. Draw-only. Commit 7bae3cf8.
    44. 🟢 camera_link_warning_mode defaults to ACTIVE_SCENE (user ruling). Reverses Added 30's shipped default: the warning stays quiet until the user is standing in a scene the camera can't reach. The "(default)" marker moves to the ACTIVE_SCENE item, the tooltip leads with it, and de_DE is re-keyed for all three reworded strings (the i18n guard caught the two enum descriptions as orphans on the first suite run — rewording an item description silently kills its translation). Nothing becomes invisible: the tree's red flags are mode-independent. Commit 195410e6.
    45. 🟢 render_jobs_popup_position defaults to CURSOR. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) props_misc.py default TOP -> CURSOR, and batch_render/jobs_popover.py's getattr fallback (used when preferences cannot be resolved) follows, so the two can no longer disagree. Existing users keep their saved value - no migration was added. Commit 52f8c1ea.
    46. 🟢 Render Mode moves to the bottom of TKS_MT_RenderMenu, reworded. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) It is a setting, not a scope, so it sits below the rows that actually start a render. Labels now name the cost: "In Blender - you wait" / "In Background - keep working"; "Foreground"/"Background" said nothing about which keeps Blender usable. de_DE re-keyed in lockstep. Commit 52f8c1ea.
    47. 🟢 The idle render control uses OUTPUT in both modes. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) draw_render_control previously switched PLAY/RIGHTARROW_THIN by mode. One button, one icon; the mode is stated in words inside the menu it opens. Shared by the Batch Render sidebar and the Takes-tree sidebar, so one edit covers both. Commit 52f8c1ea.
    48. 🟢 Warning rows are built once, in warnings/_widgets.py. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) value_button_row now splits the row FIRST (DIFF_FACTOR, 0.4) and places the button cluster INSIDE the right half rather than beside it. That is what lets the split land at a fixed fraction of the row whatever it holds, so the arrow sits at the same x in every row, while the cluster still hugs the right edge and takes only what its own buttons need - a row with fewer buttons spends the difference on its AFTER chip alone. Two rejected shapes are recorded in the docstring: a cluster outside the split tied the split point to the button count (staggered arrows), and a fixed slot reserve left a slot-wide hole on every row that drew fewer buttons. Rows showing ONE value pass split=False. Commit 6370299c.
    49. 🟢 Value chips fill their column. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) value_box no longer sets alignment='CENTER' on the chip row: setting alignment makes a Blender layout SHRINK-WRAP, which both kept the chip a small pill in a wide cell and starved the row of the width its buttons needed to reach the right edge. The chip is drawn as a flat emboss=False operator, which fills its row AND centres its own text. Same trap hit arrow_cell, which now carries no fixed width at all, and the after half is no longer an aligned row (an aligned row packed the glyph flush against the right chip while the left side kept its spacing). Regression tests pin all of it. Commit 6370299c.
    50. 🟢 New tks.value_chip_info carries the untruncated value. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) A layout.label() has no tooltip, so a truncated chip was unreadable. Blender puts a truncated button's full text at the top of its tooltip for free; bl_description is a short static line ("Copy this value to the clipboard") and NOT the value - returning the value printed it twice - and must not be empty, which renders as "(undocumented operator)". execute() copies to the clipboard rather than returning a decorative FINISHED (Constitution rule 7). Commit 6370299c.
    51. 🟢 Nine warning panels route through ui.styles.wrapped_info_box. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) cascade_drift, cascade_broken_assignments, presets_missing, presets_incompatible, camera_links, variant_conflicts, system_cache, system_store_block, system_preview_renames hand-rolled box() + label(), which clips instead of wrapping, carries no header, and cannot be gated. Wording moved into texts/infoboxes.py with kind='warning' (Show Warning Details). system_cache and system_store_block had their message hand-broken into short lines to survive a narrow N-panel; the component wraps for real, so those are single sentences again. system_cache translates the TEMPLATE then formats the version in - wrapped_info_box looks the string up whole, and a version baked in would never match a catalogue entry. de_DE: 15 dead entries removed, 10 added, coverage held at 98.7%. Commit 6370299c.
    52. 🟢 Panel-level bulk actions moved into their panel's title row. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) Clear All, Empty all, Accept/Revert, Snap All to Rest, Rename All, Rescan, Rename All/Dismiss All. A row with alignment='RIGHT' shrink-wraps, so they now fit their icon + text instead of stretching across the panel. alert is explicitly cleared on the cluster - several panel headers are red and the buttons must not inherit it. The three prominent single recovery actions (Rebuild Cache, Cleanup Incompatible Presets, Preload All Layers) keep their scale_y=1.2 full-width shape. Commit 6370299c.
    53. 🟢 Alert red removed from the warning value chips. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) cascade_broken_assignments and variant_conflicts passed after_alert=True / alert=True. The panel header and the UNLINKED icon already say the row is broken; a red field read as "this field is wrong" rather than "this row needs a decision". Commit 6370299c.
    54. 🟢 The "no World" drift is gated on the new preference. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) See Added 32 for the gate and the cache-invalidation callback. Commit bfbccae6.
    55. 🟢 World-needed and camera-needed rows share one body. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) _draw_needed_row replaces _draw_world_needed_row + _draw_camera_needed_row. The world row was a one-off "World needed:" line with an inline prop_search, which read as a different kind of warning than it is. It now reads "Scene (SCENE_DATA) | -> None (WORLD)" - labelled by tier, before chip naming the scene (there is no cleared-world memory to show; the camera side has _last_cleared_camera), after chip carrying the icon of what is missing. 'scene_name' added to the world_needed payload. The inline Create button is gone (new_op is optional): the dropdown already offers Create New World. Commit bfbccae6.
    56. 🟢 Reapply Inherited World greys out when nothing is restorable. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) New core/cascade.py::reapplyable_world mirroring reapplyable_camera: returns the tracked world name only if that world still exists in bpy.data.worlds, so the row's enabled state is honest about what the button will do. Name-only and read-only, safe from draw; the menu gets the ANSWER rather than the tracker dict (ARCH-03). Commit bfbccae6.
    57. 🟢 Camera Link Gap rows adopt the standard warning shape. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) [Scene + icon 25%] | [scene] -> [camera] | [Link] via the shared row_label / value_button_row / diff_pair, replacing its own "name: value" list, and the per-camera title sits in the full-width centred band the broken-assignment and missing-preset panels already use. Also new: row_label() draws the label column as TEXT then ICON with a LABEL_ICON_GAP cell between them - Blender's label(text=, icon=) puts the icon first, which reads backwards in a right-aligned column, and an aligned row packs its children flush so the gap has to be a real cell. Commits 6370299c, bfbccae6.
    58. 🟢 The Variants in-use badge counts, and leads the stat cluster. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) _usage_cache stores counts instead of a name set, so product_usage_count() costs nothing extra - same single scan, same dirty flag, still never scanned from draw; assigned_product_names() / product_in_use() are built on top. A tier naming the same product twice counts once. The badge moves left of the states stat. _USE_COUNT_UNITS is paid for in the right cluster's fixed budget AND carried as a fixed cell width in BOTH branches - an empty label is not as wide as a digit, and either omission pushes every icon after it out of column. The stats reserve is trimmed 8.5 -> 7.2 at the same time: the cluster is right-aligned, so every over-reserved unit showed up as a hole between a truncated product name and the first badge. Commit d52870e5.

    59. 🟢 Non-live products wear a dimmed badge, not a button.

    60. 🟢 The Takes panel's poll no longer requires scene.sequence_editor. It hid the card on an ordinary shot scene — taking the auto-switch toggles, the "no strips" explanation and the Go To Timeline button with it. All three exist FOR that state. The panel lives in the sequencer space, so Blender only draws it when a sequencer is open; that is the whole condition.

    61. 🟢 engine.has_scene_strips requires actual SCENE strips. Blender creates a sequence_editor lazily and keeps it, so an ordinary project scene answered "yes I have one" forever — the follow followed a scene with nothing in it and called reset_applied() every tick. Measured in the field: the status printed usable as a timeline: 01-01 for the user's project scene while the real edit sat elsewhere.

    62. 🟢 core/vl_switch_scope.py — one contract for every view-layer switch. SEVEN callers of apply_vl_switch_unified each hand-rolled the announcement, and six were missing a DIFFERENT piece: the depsgraph handler never set is_applying at all (it only READ it as a re-entry guard, so a native switch ran the whole cascade while every listener believed the user had done it); the tree click never opened the quiet window; the sequencer follow never drained; rest mode announced nothing whatsoever; the preload FORCED the flag False instead of restoring it; both undo branches skipped the drain. Exit order IS the contract — drain while the addon still owns the scene, stamp jit_suppress_until BEFORE the flag drops (the updates it covers arrive on the following tick), then RESTORE rather than force, because switches nest. Out deliberately: the file-load gate (acquired in load_handler, released by a timer 200ms later — it spans two functions, so a context manager cannot express it; marked # LOCK-OK) and batch render (covered by is_batch_render_in_progress(), a genuinely different state). Now enforced by the auditor's CORR-18. Perf: +0.25ms per switch at first (60 objects, median 1.90→2.16ms), brought back to ~+0.1ms by draining only a non-empty queue, hoisting the receipt import out of the per-target loop, and using tuple receipt keys instead of f-strings.

    63. 🟢 Write receipts replace the timing guess. The quiet window is a guess — "motion arriving within a second of a switch was probably ours" — and guesses fail when a tick runs late. apply_vl_switch_unified now records which action it put on which target, and the fresh-action detector asks whether the action an object wears is the addon's own last write. One receipt per target, replaced on each write, NOT expiring: expiry by tick count would bury a second timing guess under the fix. Keyed by name, never as_pointer(). The quiet window stays one release as a backstop, then goes. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) The Live column offered an embossed icon button on every other row, so it read as "a badge and some buttons" - two kinds of thing - instead of one choice with one option lit. Same glyph, emboss=False + active=False; enabled stays true, so clicking still hands Live over. The word LIVE stays on the one row that is live, because the word IS the state. Commit d52870e5.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Rest-revert snap is now evidence-gated on witnessed key loss (trap-state enforcement + wrong-place snap). _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred (features/rest_state/revert_snap.py) snapped every user of a modified take action whose channels were unkeyed at the current frame — so an object left in the "action assigned, slot empty" state by Clear Keyframes / Alt+I was yanked to rest ~0.1 s after every subsequent autokey-off move (value-lock-like enforcement; the autokey-off early-exit path in mirror_logic.py queues the revert on ANY transform of an action-bearing object), and all 13 users of the shared take were swept as collateral (field log 2026-07-14 12:22). The snap could also land in the WRONG place: the hand-rolled slot matcher missed short-form/pipe slot names and silently fell back to the live rest cache — selection-time live snapshots, not rest values. Fix: per-target key-count baseline (_slot_key_counts, seeded seed-only from rest_cache._snapshot_id_block, cleared via clear_key_count_cache() in invalidate_and_rebuild() on undo/redo/file-load) — a target snaps only when its assigned slot's keyframe count DECREASED since last observation; rest values now resolve through the shared _resolve_rest_slot + _snap_one_target path (same source as the drift scanner and apply_rest_values, keyed-anywhere protection), and the rest-cache fallback is removed (uncovered targets skip with a logged warning). The original count-based drift detection (auto_snap_keyframe_clear.md) had been lost in the rest_state_snap_on_keyframe_delete.md rework. 9 regression tests in dev/tests/test_revert_snap_evidence.py; full suite 1294 passed. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/rest_revert_trap_state_snapping.md. Commit 69ba211.
    2. 🟢 auto_snap_on_clear preference wired up. Defined/drawn/search-indexed since its introduction but never consumed by the snap path. New _auto_snap_enabled() (default True, True when prefs unavailable) gates the snap portion of _revert_unkeyed_to_rest_deferred; the rest-cache invalidation on rest-action authoring (Fixed entry 1's sibling concern, guarded by test_gate_off_still_invalidates_rest_cache) deliberately runs regardless of the pref. Same commit 69ba211.

    3. 🟢 Datablock popover "New Slot" button no longer dies on a stale slots.new(for_id=) call. TKS_OT_DatablockAddSlot.execute (operators/inspector/ops_datablock_action.py) still used the pre-4.4 draft signature action.slots.new(for_id=target), which raises TypeError: ActionSlots.new(): required parameter "id_type" not specified on every Blender 5.x — the call was unguarded, so the button always failed with a Python error; every other slot-creation site had already been migrated to (id_type, name). Found during the 2026-07-16 autokey audit (fresh 0.7.11 install on a second PC) and confirmed by live probe on 5.1.2. Fix derives both parameters through the canonical helpers — core.anim_utils.resolve_id_type + core.path_utils.derive_slot_name_for_target — so the slot label follows the user's naming template instead of a raw datablock name (the animation_data_loss_fresh_install.md lesson). Regression test dev/tests/test_datablock_add_slot.py drives the operator end-to-end (RED: TypeError at the old call; GREEN after). Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/datablock_add_slot_stale_api.md. Commit 96ec131.

    4. 🟢 Autokey-guard operators had no MANUAL_MAP entry (right-click → Online Manual dead-ended at the wiki home). tks.autokey_guard_accept / tks.autokey_guard_decline (operators/ui/ops_misc_ui.py:68,93) are drawn from the Toggle-Autokey consent popup and the Autokey Is Being Blocked nav warning (panels/navigation/warnings/system_autokey_blocked.py), but carried no explicit map row, so only the catch-all wildcard matched and the manual link resolved to (wiki home). Surfaced by the auditor's INFO-01 manual_map_audit as two routing findings once the operators became documented (wiki eee4c37 added the Autokey Is Being Blocked section to interface/navigation_panel.md — itself the fix for the two coverage_audit findings). Fix: two manual overrides in doc/reports/data/wire_assignments.json → interface/navigation_panel/#autokey-is-being-blocked, then dev/scripts/apply_wire_assignments.py regenerated the AUTO-WIRED block (971 → 973 rows; diff is exactly the two new rows — the generator was fed a fresh codebase_stats.json copied from the auditor, since a stale/absent input would rewrite the whole block). Resolution verified against Blender's matcher semantics (lowercase id → case-sensitive fnmatchcase → first match wins) and the all-patterns-lowercase invariant; -k manual_map subset 28 passed on Blender 5.2. Note: codebase_stats.json is a 1.7 MB transient pipeline input and is deliberately NOT committed. Commit 644dc7d.

    5. 🟢 TKS_OT_AutokeyGuardAccept / TKS_OT_AutokeyGuardDecline had no poll() (CORR-07 missing: 2). Both shipped with the 2026-07-16 autokey-guard work without a precondition, so the buttons stayed clickable when context.preferences.addons.get(ADDON_MODULE) could not resolve — execute() then returned {'CANCELLED'} with no report, i.e. a dead click. The auditor classified them as REAL rather than by-design (its harmless: 304 bucket already excuses the INTERNAL-by-design set). Fix: both now poll() on exactly what execute() needs — reachable addon preferences, since accept writes autokey_manage_insert_available / autokey_manage_consented and decline clears them. The duplicated lookup is extracted to a module-level _guard_prefs(context) and ADDON_MODULE hoisted to a module-level import (core.constants is a leaf re-export; poll runs on every redraw of the autokey-blocked warning panel, so it must not sit behind a deferred import — ARCH-04 / draw-path cost). Deliberately NOT a UI-state poll: the system_autokey_blocked panel draws the buttons unconditionally, and that panel only exists while the addon is registered, so the preferences always resolve there and the buttons never grey out in practice. Registered in the existing CORR-07 registry dev/tests/test_corr07_polls.py (AST-based, mirrors the auditor's own parse). Suite 1341 → 1343 passed on Blender 5.2; re-scan CORR-07 missing 2 → 0, quality 9.9 → 10.0. Commit 86d117e.

    6. 🟢 Word-list entries are mirrored into Blender's operator translation context. Button labels stayed English while panel headers translated: Blender resolves layout.operator(text=…) labels in contexts.operator_default ("Operator"), but bl_label / panel headers use the default '*' context, so entries authored only under '*' never reached any button (the Context / Inspector tabs were the visible case; translation misses never error, so it read as "i18n is broken"). Root-caused by a GUI probe in Blender 5.2 — registering the same sources under the operator context made the tabs render marker text, the '*' entry alone never did. texts/i18n.py::build_dict() now mirrors each default-context entry into the operator context (translators still author one line per string); a hand-authored operator-context entry wins over the mirror. 2 tests in dev/tests/test_i18n_plumbing.py; troubleshooting doc/troubleshooting/i18n_operator_context_buttons.md. Commit ff39176.

    7. 🟢 The custom-token preset row now mirrors styles.preset_row — native search popup + [+][✏][X] cluster. The picker (features/smart_syntax/presets.py) was a bpy.types.Menu (TKS_MT_custom_token_presets) drawing one row(align=True) per preset with an inline X; a Menu lays children in an implicit single column, so a row() per entry made Blender reflow into a second column — the delete buttons and the trailing "Save current tokens as…" broke away from the list (reported from a German-UI screenshot). First rebuilt as an INSTANCED popover panel (2a38b4e); that fixed the reflow but still didn't match the Properties preset rows, which use styles.preset_row (ui/preset_rows.py) — a native invoke_search_popup selector plus a [tier][badge][name][+ create][✏ edit][X] cluster. Parity pass (c3bad58): the popover panel is replaced by TKS_OT_SearchCustomTokenPreset, mirroring TKS_OT_SearchRenderPreset — bl_property = "preset_name", a dynamic enum built from list_presets(tier) and retained through utils.enum_cache.retain (a runtime os.listdir-derived enum dangles otherwise, per [[feedback_dynamic_enum_retain]]), invoke_search_popup in invoke, apply in execute. The row's ✏ is a new TKS_OT_EditCustomTokenPreset (rename + move-tier invoke_props_dialog, mirroring TKS_OT_EditRenderPreset; the tokens themselves are edited in the grid, so a preset needs an identity edit) — save-new/delete-old, and the selection follows the rename when it was active. Kept the single-tier listing (deliberate divergence from the render picker's all-tiers popover, per the user's earlier "filtered tier" call), so the tier dropdown stays meaningful. The dirty-driven +→✓ save / ✏→↩ revert toggles that preset_row also carries need token change-tracking that doesn't exist yet — deferred to the token-preset-ownership work (doc/roadmap/ideas/token-preset-ownership.md).     8. 🟢 Info-box bodies stayed English in a translated UI — wrapped before translated. ui/styles.py::draw_wrapped_paragraph split the source into per-line fragments and drew each via col.label(); Blender only translates a label equal to a COMPLETE registered msgid, so a wrapped fragment matched nothing and the registered German was never applied (reported on the Custom Tokens info box). Fix: one bpy.app.translations.pgettext_iface(text) on the whole string before wrapping (the template-first rule texts/i18n.py documents), hoisted above the wrap loop (perf rule); fragments drawn with translate=False. The box header was already fine (whole-string label). Single wrap path ⇒ fixes every info box. Behaviorally verified: pgettext_iface on the real Custom Tokens string returns 'Eigene Token aus Szenendaten definieren …' under de_DE. 3 source-contract tests; test_info_box fake layout updated to accept the translate kwarg. Suite 1376 passed. Commit beb1a09.
    9. 🟢 FG batch render start crashed Blender 5.2 with EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION — the render_stats registration is now version-gated. Blender 5.2 added BKE_callback_exec_string(G_MAIN, rs->infostr, BKE_CB_EVT_RENDER_STATS) to the UI render job's image_renderinfo_cb (render_internal.cc) WITHOUT the rs->infostr == nullptr early-return the background path (stats_update, pipeline.cc) has; at the first stats draw of do_render_full_pipeline infostr is still NULL, and with ANY Python handler in bpy.app.handlers.render_stats the bridge crashes in PyC_UnicodeFromBytes → strlen(NULL) on the render thread BEFORE Python runs (fingerprint: strlen ← PyC_UnicodeFromBytes ← bpy_app_generic_callback ← BKE_callback_exec_string ← image_renderinfo_cb ← do_render_full_pipeline). The handler's defensive *args signature never helped — the C bridge only early-outs when the handler LIST is empty, which is also why vanilla Blender doesn't crash. Source-verified: 5.1-release has no exec call there; upstream main still unguarded (report draft: dev/temp/blender_bugreport_render_stats_null.md). Fix: render_hooks.fg_render_stats_supported() (False on ≥ 5.2.0 until the upstream guard lands) gates the FG append AND its register_process("FG Render Stats Handler") row in operators.py invoke; cleanup stays unconditional (idempotent removal, unregister_process no-ops on unknown names). FG per-VL progress falls back to the elapsed-based estimate — the effective 5.x behavior anyway (FG render_stats only ever delivered the final Time: line, per doc/roadmap/_dev/render-eta-precision.md). The headless BG worker (cli_worker.py) keeps its handler — the BG stats path NULL-guards. Tests: dev/tests/test_render_stats_52_gate.py (4 — version matrix, live-version default, registration-site-gated source guard); full suite 1321 passed on Blender 5.2. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/render_stats_null_infostr_crash_52.md. Commit 4295c3e.

    23. 🟢 Six latent NameError sites across presets, cascade, nav warnings and prefs (CORR-11 haul). core/cascade.py:817,841,1009,1569 called logger.debug with no module-level logger — two sites sit INSIDE except handlers, so the NameError replaced the exception being handled (commit e22c4ee). serialization/resolve.py used os (:285,:287) and seven capture_* helpers (:229-249) without importing them, crashing detect_orphaned_properties / remove_preset_properties on first call; capture imports are function-local because capture.py:3 imports this module at import time (cycle). ops_manage_crud.py:455 named json.JSONDecodeError in an except clause while importing json as _json — a NameError at exception time (commit 3da172a). warnings/presets_incompatible.py:19 and warnings/system_cache.py:23 used pgettext_iface without the ....texts.i18n import their five siblings carry, so drawing either warning crashed the panel; preferences/ops_preference_config.py:258 called _scan_project_prefs_files, a name that exists nowhere — the canonical helper _scan_config_files is already imported at :18 and used at :195 (commit 6549d7c).
    24. 🟢 Draw caches retained RNA collection elements (CRASH-08). That is the documented 0xC0000005 shape (IDP_GetPropertyFromGroup) that find_take_set defends against with indices + identity re-check, and CHANGELOG entry [0.5.x] already records _vlg_cache in an undo-crash fix. Its single consumer (tree_list.py:223, tag-filter dim) only ever read tks_assigned_tag, so the cache now stores that STRING: _vlg_tag_cache[(scene_name, group_name)] -> str. Strings-only now matches draw_layers.py's documented policy. TKS_UL_InspectorObjects._targets_cache (ui_list_objects.py) is a different lifecycle — it holds real ID datablocks (object, data, shape keys, materials, node trees) from iter_anim_targets, and Blender raises ReferenceError on a freed ID rather than dangling. Converting to names would require heterogeneous re-resolution across bpy.data collections on every draw for no safety gain, so it keeps the datablocks behind a new _entry_is_live() probe: as_pointer() on each target (cheapest probe that raises, no string allocation) plus an identity check on the first entry (which iter_anim_targets guarantees is the object itself, catching an entry inherited via rename), rebuilding on failure.     26. 🟢 Group reorder was a dead click once Ungrouped left collection index 0 (audit defect D8 — listed by the fix pack, then missed). _move_scene_group guarded with if group_idx <= 1: CANCELLED on UP and if group_idx == 0 ... on DOWN, and _move_vl_group derived main_group_idx as the FIRST group for the scene. Both encode 'the default group is at collection index 0'. But tree_sync SORTS Ungrouped to the front for display and hides its header, so collection position is not display position — and group/ungroup churn moves Ungrouped off index 0. Repro (dev/temp, since removed): with the collection at ['G1','G2','Ungrouped'], G2-UP and G1-DOWN both returned CANCELLED while can_move (display-order) reported the arrows enabled — lit buttons, no effect. Fix: new _named_sibling_target(groups, group_idx, direction, same_scene=None) picks the swap target from the NAMED siblings (optionally scoped to one scene for VL groups), identifying the default by name (UNGROUPED) rather than by position; Ungrouped itself returns None in both directions, and the ends of a named run refuse to move outward. Both move paths now use it, so the operator and the sidebar's can_move agree. 3 bpy regression tests in dev/tests/test_group_move_guard.py, including the Ungrouped-off-index-0 ordering. Suite 1686. Commit 6ac79c2.
    27. 🟢 Group/ungroup left multi-select on, disabling the move arrows (field report). draw_tree.py:346,350 draw the arrows enabled = can_move and not is_multiselect, and grouping/ungrouping are PERFORMED in multi-select — but GroupScenes, GroupVLs, UngroupScenes and UngroupVLs all returned FINISHED without clearing tks_multiselect_list. So the arrows went dead immediately after the action, with no on-screen reason. The batch-delete ops already exited the mode; the group family never did (flagged in the consolidation audit's multiselect dimension as 'group/ungroup ops don't exit at all'). New exit_multiselect(wm) in operators/_tree_ops_core.py clears the mode, the type filter (which otherwise survived and silently narrowed the next multi-select) and the per-item tks_selected ticks; wired into all four operators. NOTE: a first attempt used from .._tree_ops_core from operators/context/groups/ — one dot short, caught by the new tests. 3 bpy tests. Suite 1689. Commit 4df3be2.

    28. 🟢 Move refusals were silent (two dozen bare return {'CANCELLED'}). A refusal and a broken button were indistinguishable from outside, which is how the D8 guard survived and why the log could not explain 'nothing happens' — especially with every debug topic off, as in the reporting session. _refuse() + _refuse_report() in ops_crud_reorder.py now log to UI:SYNC and self.report({'INFO'}), so the reason reaches the status bar with no debug topic enabled. Reasons cover: scene gone, VL in no group, member list missing the entry, already first/last in its group, no named sibling group to swap with. The most valuable one in practice: ungrouped VLs live in the implicit Ungrouped group whose header is hidden, so a plain VL and a grouped VL can look adjacent under a scene while sitting in different containers — the move is refused with 'already last in its group' instead of appearing broken. Commit 8f1f62b.

    29. 🟢 A renamed scene split its view layers across two 'Ungrouped' groups (field report + log). VL groups store the scene TWICE: scene (PointerProperty, follows renames) and scene_name (String, does not). When rename propagation misses one — ambiguous batch rename, or a rename made while the tree wasn't watching — the group still resolves through the pointer while its string names a dead scene. reconcile_topology's per-scene pass filters groups with (g.scene or bpy.data.scenes.get(g.scene_name)) == scene, i.e. POINTER-first, so it saw the scene covered; then the name-keyed lookups found nothing and it created a SECOND Ungrouped for the same scene. The scene's VLs then live in two containers, render as one flat run (Ungrouped's header is hidden) and cannot move past each other — _move_vl reorders within vlg.members. Diagnosis came straight from the user's log once the topics were on: adjacent rows 11/12 logged move refused: already last in its group vl='09-01_advantages' group='Ungrouped' and already first in its group vl='REST' group='Ungrouped', and reconcile_topology: DONE listed both 'Ungrouped'@'00-00_MAIN'(10 members) and 'Ungrouped'@'00-00'(1 members) while the SG membership showed the only live scene as 00-00 — i.e. the scene had been renamed 00-00_MAIN → 00-00. Fix, both in reconcile_topology: (1) heal a stale g.scene_name from g.scene when the string names no live scene (removes the CAUSE); (2) _merge_duplicates() folds same-(scene,name) VL groups and same-name scene groups into the first, preserving member order and identity (repairs files ALREADY split). Groups sharing a name across DIFFERENT scenes are untouched (legitimate). The scene-group axis carries the same pointer/string pair on its members and now heals identically — it hides better there because most SG code reads the pointer first, but string-only readers (e.g. _first_scene_in_sg, the split view's jump) silently find nothing. New report keys scene_names_healed / member_names_healed / groups_merged. 5 bpy regression tests. Suite 1719. Commit bd037e4.

    30. 🟢 Multi-select mode integrity (revises Fixed 27). 27 made group/ungroup call exit_multiselect() so the arrows — drawn enabled = can_move and not is_multiselect — came back. The user pushed back that auto-flipping a mode they set is its own UX smell, and it forces re-entry between batches. Correct diagnosis: the arrows were only gated on multi-select because a move handles ONE row, not a selection; expressing that limitation as a dead control was the mistake. draw_tree.py now drops and not is_multiselect from both arrow columns — they act on tks_all_viewlayers_index (the highlighted row), which is well-defined regardless of ticks. exit_multiselect() → consume_multiselect(): clears the per-item tks_selected ticks and tks_multiselect_type_filter (which otherwise survives and narrows the next selection) but NOT tks_multiselect_list. Tooltip OP_MOVEALLVIEWLAYERITEM rewritten to say it moves the highlighted item and that multi-select does not change that; de_DE re-keyed in lockstep (INFO-09). Tests from 27 inverted to assert the mode SURVIVES. Follow-up captured as doc/roadmap/ideas/move-multi-selection.md with the user's ruled constraint: a block move is offered ONLY when every ticked row is on the same level, since a selection spanning tiers has no single correct reading. Open questions recorded there (same level but different parents; non-contiguous selections; highlighted row outside the selection). Suite 1719. Commit 21dcddb.

    31. 🟢 Tree highlight was dragged back by the sync timer (field report: 'the highlight is jumping back to original place'). _sync_timer (panels/context/handlers.py:410) RE-ASSERTED tks_all_viewlayers_index onto the active VL every time its body ran — and the body runs whenever _context_sync_dirty/_sync_dirty is set, which any tree mutation does. So a deliberate highlight (row click, _on_row_ticked, the block move's leading-edge index) survived only until the next dirty tick; _move_guard_until (0.5 s, armed by notify_move_completed AND by the timer's own sync branches) merely postponed it. Now change-driven: module-level _last_active_vl holds the last observed (scene.name, vl.name) and the snap runs only when it differs — preserving the useful half (switch VL elsewhere → bar follows) without overruling a choice made in the tree. Reset to None in _handle_undo_redo_sync and _handle_load_post_sync so undo/File▸Open re-follow. 2 bpy tests in dev/tests/test_tree_index_snap.py. NOTE on the test harness: the timer arms its OWN guard inside the sync branches, so both tests explicitly zero _move_guard_until — without that the no-drag test passes vacuously (guard active → snap skipped → highlight 'preserved' for the wrong reason), which is exactly how this class of bug hides. Suite 1747. Commit 759e374.

    32. 🟢 Arrows lit for a selection the operator would refuse. block_can_move() answers only whether rows have ROOM, so a selection spanning two VL groups (plenty of room, zero shared container) enabled the arrows and the Shift+Click then hit the same-parent refusal. New selection_is_movable(items, selected_idx) in operators/_tree_ops_core.py answers whether it is a block at all: at least 2 rows, one item_type, not group/GLOBAL rows, exactly one parent_key(). draw_tree gates the OR-in on it, so an invalid selection leaves the arrows reflecting the highlighted row alone and a plain click still works. _parent_key was promoted from ops_crud_reorder into the shared shell as parent_key(), so the operator refuses by the same definition the panel greys by, closing the drift the sidebar and the move operator had for move legality before they were unified. 3 bpy tests. Suite 1750. Commit 8a0717c.

    33. 🟢 Empty delete plan cancelled silently (field report: "delete button is active but does nothing, no prompt, no info"). invoke() early-returned {'CANCELLED'} with only self.report({'INFO'}, ...) when _plan_counts() came back empty — a status-bar line under a modal-less click, i.e. invisible. The draw() branch for that case already existed and was unreachable. invoke() now opens the dialog when not counts as well as when skipped is non-empty; only a fully deletable selection may skip the ask. execute() gained the matching guard so scripted callers get {'CANCELLED'} plus a named reason instead of running a no-op body. Regression test drives execute() through a SimpleNamespace shim with a pre-built empty plan, since poll() correctly greys the button for the only fixture-reachable protected case (default group).

    34. 🟢 Undo took the one sync branch that skipped the repair (field report: "undo redo is not refreshing instantly. Tree shows item disappear and reappearing"). _sync_timer repairs the group store before rebuilding on the fingerprint branch only. Undo restores the World store to an earlier snapshot WITHOUT changing a name, so the fingerprint matches and just _sync_dirty is set - the elif branch rebuilt from unrepaired membership and dropped the row, which returned when a later unrelated edit happened to take the repairing branch. reconcile_topology() now runs on both branches. Reproduced first with dev/temp/probe_treesync.py. Latency half of the report addressed separately: mark_sync_dirty() schedules one early catch-up tick at 50 ms (guarded by _catchup_pending, so a burst of marks cannot pile up timers) instead of waiting up to a full 250 ms period. It is a safe_register timer rather than a direct call because undo_post is one of the emitters and repairing the store inside a handler would mutate persisted data behind Blender's undo stack (Constitution rule 2).

    35. 🟢 Global tier followed the alphabet, not its data (field report: renaming a scene moved the Global world onto that scene; a second rename brought Global back while the stray record stayed). Two defects, reproduced by dev/temp/probe_master_flap.py. (a) The master scene - carrier of every tks_global_* record - was bpy.data.scenes[0] at ~110 sites, and bpy.data collections are C-level alphabetically sorted, so a rename changed WHICH scene was master while the records stayed behind: Global read empty. (b) The witness ledgers (_last_cascade_world et al.) are scene-NAME-keyed; after a rename the lookup missed, _witnessed_external fired falsely, and the no-winner ADOPT branch cemented the cascade's own applied world onto the renamed scene's tier. Fixes: utils/master_scene.get_master_scene() resolves the master by DATA (first scene carrying a Global record; cached via session_uid, which survives renames and holds no RNA), swept over every master site incl. still/rest features; cascade.rename_scene_in_ledgers() re-keys all seven name-keyed ledgers from the rename propagation. Standalone caveats: cli_worker.py reaches the resolver via sys.modules (launched as a bare --python script), still_mode/engine.py imports it lazily (spec-loaded context-free by its tests). Suspected to also explain Fixed- reported rename icon flashing: each keystroke could flip the master, flapping the Global assignment for every row. 5 regression tests in test_master_scene_anchor.py.

    36. 🟢 Split carriers made the world stop switching (regression from Fixed 35, field report same day). Historic files wrote each global prop to whatever scene sorted first AT THAT MOMENT, so tks_rest_mode can sit on one scene and tks_global_world on another. The resolver weighed all markers equally; a rest-only scene won the master title and the Global world became unreachable (probe: resolve_cascade(WORLD) -> (None, None)). _PRIMARY_MARKERS (the eight tks_global_* records) now always outrank _SECONDARY_MARKERS (rest flags); most-records-wins among primaries, ties by collection order, uid cache restricted to primary carriers. consolidate_global_records() heals the split once per load (deferred via safe_register from load_handler - handlers never write), master values winning over stray flap artifacts. +2 tests.

    37. 🟢 Undo of a rename reshuffled the tree (field report: "undoing the rename is resorting the whole tree. Should never happen."). Undo restores live names while the group store keeps the timer-patched strings (the rename propagation writes from a timer, outside the operator's undo step) - or vice versa. reconcile_topology() answered the stale member with prune + re-adopt: the live VL landed at the END of Ungrouped, named-group membership and manual order gone. The unambiguous 1:1 case (one stale member + one unclaimed VL in the same scene) is now healed IN PLACE before adopt/prune runs, reusing propagate_renames' set-difference rule; the take set is re-pointed in the same pass; 2:2+ still falls through to the classic repair. New vl_names_healed counter in the report dict.

    38. 🟢 find_take_set missed for the whole stale window (the remaining icon flash after Fixed 35). _vs_cache's token is count-based, so a rename never rebuilt it: draws queried the scene's CURRENT name (resolved via the row's PointerProperty) against keys holding the OLD one - miss - take tier dropped out of _get_vl_cascade_status icons until the sync timer patched the strings, once per keystroke. A miss now falls back to a pointer scan (vs.scene == bpy.data.scenes.get(scene_name)), serves the hit and patches the cache key, so in-window draws resolve identically to out-of-window draws. O(N) only on the miss frame itself.

    39. 🟢 Scene axis reshuffled where the VL axis was already healed (caught in the user's log: scenes_adopted:1, scenes_pruned:1, SG member order flipped). Undo reverted the SG member STRING to the pre-rename scene name with a DEAD pointer (member predates PointerProperty), so the existing pointer heal could not fire and prune+adopt moved the scene to the end of Ungrouped. Same 1:1 in-place heal as Fixed 37, scene axis: one stale member

      • one unclaimed live scene = rename, rewritten in place (string AND pointer restored). test_orphaned_scene_is_adopted_not_lost updated: heal now preempts prune+adopt in the unambiguous case; intent unchanged.

    40. 🟢 Retarget dispatcher raised on a failed nested poll (field traceback: retarget_scene.poll() failed, context is incorrect via ops_global_shortcuts.py:370 -> ops_edit_item.py:246). The typed retarget polls demand a second group to move TO; a failed poll on a nested bpy.ops call surfaces as RuntimeError, not a refusal. All four dispatch targets in TKS_OT_RetargetTreeItem (retarget_scene/viewlayer, merge_scene_group, retarget_vl_group) now route through _dispatch(), which pre-checks op.poll() and reports the reason on both the multiselect and single-select paths. 4 de_DE entries. Regression test drives the multiselect branch through a shim (the single-select path resolves panel focus state headless runs lack).

    41. 🟢 Settle gate for inline renames (field report: "name still flashing with the icons. Why?" - after the take-set rescue). Inline renames commit per keystroke; each commit wiped _vl_cascade_cache, propagated the half-typed name and rebuilt the tree while other string-keyed lookups held the previous keystroke's name. VL names have no pointer to rescue through (ViewLayer is not an ID), so per-lookup rescues are whack-a-mole. The sync tick now HOLDS while a name-only fingerprint keeps changing (re-arms at 100 ms, touches nothing - rows read datablocks directly so on-screen names stay live) and processes once after _RENAME_SETTLE_SECONDS (0.35 s) of quiet, mapping pre-burst -> final name in one set-difference step. Structural fingerprint changes and the _sync_dirty undo path are never held. The cache invalidate moved below the settle gate so held ticks no longer wipe icons. 3 tests in test_rename_settle.py.

    42. 🟢 Row identity fallback painted the ACTIVE layer onto the renamed row (field report: "In this flash I always see the first vl flashing" - the settle gate lengthened the mistaken-identity window, which is what made it visible). draw_vl's miss fallback was context.view_layer; replaced by _resolve_row_vl() - set difference over the scene's live VLs vs the tree rows, so the ONE unmatched layer is the row's own; ambiguity returns None rather than guessing. _get_vl_cascade_status() gains held_key: on a primary miss it serves the row's pre-burst cache entry verbatim, so icons do not change during the hold (recomputing mid-burst derived state from the half-stale store - that WAS the flash). Settled sync wipes the cache, bounding the hold. 3 tests in test_row_vl_identity.py.

    43. 🟢 The Added-16 camera-undo safeguard could not act on an already-wiped snapshot (field report: "assigning a camera natively is the issue here, when doing undo"). Sequence: native pick (undo step) -> witness ADOPTs onto the tier from a TIMER (outside the undo step) -> Ctrl+Z restores scene.camera=None AND the pre-adoption record. skip_camera_clear=True only stops the cascade's own clear; the PRESERVE branch then kept the wiped state and overwrote _last_cascade_camera with None - destroying the only memory of the pick. The undo path now re-instates the witnessed camera from the ledger when (skip flag, ADOPT mode, no winner, scene.camera None, ledger non-empty): a scene.camera write ONLY - never a tree write, so undo replay sees no phantom tree state - and the next normal pass re-adopts the record itself via the standard witness. Explicit tier clears and no-memory undos unchanged. 3 tests in test_camera_undo_reinstate.py. NOTE: the world PRESERVE branch has the same shape but ALSO a deliberate "native removal is respected" contract - left untouched on purpose; revisit only if a field report asks for it.

    44. 🟢 Native datablock renames broke tier records (field report: "As soon I rename [the world natively] the connection is lost... icon shows red"). Records store names (PointerProperty ban); the pencil ops repair them (Fixed 15) - native renames never did. core/datablock_rename_heal.py remembers as_pointer() ints for every datablock a record resolves; a broken record whose remembered pointer now carries a different name is a rename -> every record with the old name is rewritten across all six owners (Scene/VL/SG/VLG/take + globals) for worlds, camera objects, compositor groups and actions, witness ledgers included. Plain-int pointer memory (no RNA), reset on load, collection scan only on broken-record ticks; deletions stay broken. Wired into _sync_timer's processing path. 4 tests.

    45. 🟢 Fast typing still lost every icon on the row (follow-up to Fixed 41/42). The settle gate held the SYNC's wipe, but depsgraph-driven topic invalidations wiped _vl_cascade_cache per keystroke anyway, and the mid-burst recompute against the half-stale store came out all-False. invalidate_vl_cascade_cache() now defers non-forced wipes while hold_cascade_cache() shields the burst (settle window + 0.2 s); the settled sync wipes with force=True, bounding the hold. ARCH-04 kept flat by hoisting the new load-path imports in vl_lifecycle. 1 test.

    46. 🟢 Shadow store + session_uid (field: "still happening if I'm extremly fast" and the pointer-reuse callout). The burst shield arms only when _sync_timer notices the rename - up to 250 ms after the first keystroke - so extreme typing landed wipes plus wrong recomputes in the gap, and the poisoned entries were then held. _vl_status_shadow in draw_layers is wipe-IMMUNE, written only on coherent draws (held row key == live key) and served unconditionally on incoherent ones; incoherent computes can never poison it. And datablock_rename_heal matches by session_uid instead of as_pointer() - freed pointers get reused, uids never. +1 test.

    47. 🟢 The take/group store was still worlds[0] (field log during the super-fast rename test: "Group store moved from world 'SOLO' to 'SOLOsdgsdgsdg'" - the tree rebuilt from the wrong store, reordered, and dropped icons). The long-parked world-storage-anchor card, forced by a live hit. _groups_shared.get_world() now resolves the carrier by DATA (non-empty store collections), uid-cached like the master scene (Fixed 35/36); worlds[0] only when nothing carries. Cache reset on load; card moved to done/. 3 tests.

    48. 🟢 One settle window can hold MANY renames (field log: five rows -> vls_adopted:5, vls_pruned:5, order scrambled, icons gone). The 1:1 set-difference refused a 5:5 diff, the store went stale five-wide, and prune+adopt rebuilt the group in view_layers order. Bridge: probed that scene.view_layers is NOT name-sorted - renames never reorder it - so with an unchanged count, position i old IS position i new. propagate_renames pairs the whole window positionally for VLs (scenes stay set-difference: bpy.data.scenes IS sorted); _resolve_row_vl pairs multiple missing rows the same way, guarded by an order-consistency check so a custom row order can never bind an edit field to the wrong datablock. test_two_unmatched_rows_refuse_to_guess updated to the evolved contract. +4 tests total.

    49. 🟢 Positional pairing could still mispair among the MISSING rows (field: the active-VL dot rode with the renamed row, snapped back at settle). The Fixed-48 order-consistency check validates RESOLVED rows only; a custom row order swapped among the missing rows let mid-burst pairing hand the typed row a neighbour's identity - including the active layer's. Airtight bridge: vl_index on the mirror row, captured at COHERENT sync (scene.view_layers.find), value-guarded via _TREE_FIELDS. Renames never reorder scene.view_layers, so view_layers[item.vl_index] is exact through any burst regardless of row order; guarded by a taken-name check, with the orphan/positional logic kept as fallback. +1 regression test (custom order + two simultaneous renames incl. the active layer).

    50. 🟢 Scene-axis 2:2 refusal cascaded into VL prune+adopt (field log: scenes ['01-01','uzu'] -> ['ui','uib'] ambiguous, then vls 3:3, named groups emptied into Ungrouped). The scene axis kept 1:1 set-difference (bpy.data.scenes re-sorts; position cannot pair it), and with scene_renames empty the per-scene VL pairing looked scenes up by their OLD names, found nothing, and skipped them. The fingerprint now records (session_uid, name, layers) per scene and propagate pairs scenes uid-to-uid - exact for any batch size; VL positional pairing rides through because the old->new scene map is always present. Legacy-format guard for the one pre-reload fingerprint. Remaining narrow window: VL-GROUP renames stay 1:1 (PropertyGroups have no uid). +1 test.

    51. 🟢 Group tiers completed the burst-proof identity contract (field: crossing the scene and renaming the VLG dropped icons). (a) Propagation: SG and VLG axes kept 1:1 set-difference over entries that EMBED the scene name and member lists, so a same-window scene rename or member change made even a single group rename ambiguous. CollectionProperty rows never reorder on rename -> both axes pair positionally at stable count, 1:1 fallback otherwise. (b) Draw: group header rows resolved their PG by NAME (store commits per keystroke, row held -> miss -> checkbox/colour/icons gone). New group_index captured at coherent sync, _resolve_row_group() falls back to it - same contract as vl_index. Tier status: scenes = session_uid, VLs = position + vl_index, SG/VLG = position + group_index, takes = take_index (index-addressed already). +2 tests.

    52. 🟢 Mid-burst rebuilds dropped rows (field: "paritially the items themselve" vanish; "after the rebuild of the tree the active vl is on another place"). A rebuild bypassing the settle hold (undo-flag path) resolved members by LIVE name and continued on a miss - renamed rows and their takes vanished until the settle, breaking the highlight's identity anchor. The builder now keeps a missing row under its member name (heals at the next coherent pass; deleted layers still pruned by the reconciler) and matches take sets STORE-to-store (vs.vl_name vs the member name) so both sides stale in lockstep. End-to-end regression drives the rebuild without propagation. NOTE: the two prior field reports ran a session started 12:15 - before Fixed 50 (12:19) and 51 (12:30) were merged.

    53. 🟢 SG row draw crashed on a blind deref; reconcile gained the positional multi-heal (fresh-session log + live traceback). (a) draw_scene_group's render-toggle loop did bpy.data.scenes.get(m.scene_name).view_layers - None mid-burst -> AttributeError on every redraw until settle (= "vl groups loosing their icons until rebuild"). Pointer-first + guard. (b) vls_adopted:5/ vls_pruned:5 on fresh code: when propagation yields nothing (undo- restored strings, mid-burst-stamped baseline), the 1:1 heal was the only defense.
