Reconcile now pairs N stale members with N orphan layers positionally (resolved-order-consistency guard, take sets re-pointed); ambiguous order still falls back to adopt/prune. test_ambiguous_staleness_still_falls_back_to_adopt renamed/updated to the evolved contract. +1 test.

    54. 🟢 The sync timer could die silently (field: a session with ZERO sync log lines while renames were happening - every symptom "still happening" at once). bpy.app.timers unregisters a callback that raises; one exception anywhere in the tick froze the tree for the session, invisible except in the console. _sync_timer is now a never-die wrapper around _sync_timer_payload(): crashes log at ERROR with traceback into the addon log and the timer re-arms at 0.25 s. Diagnostic contract: a silent tree now always leaves a named culprit in the log.

    55. 🟢 Vacuous-consistency cross-group swaps closed (field log 14:24: all five members stale after undo, positional multi-heal paired concatenated group order vs view_layers order with nothing left to verify against). TKS_VLGroupMember.vl_index - refreshed for every resolved member at every coherent reconcile, SAVED WITH the store so undo restores name+index together. Stale members heal to view_layers[vl_index] when that layer is unaccounted - exact per member/group, take sets ride along; positional multi-heal and 1:1 remain as fallbacks for unstamped members. de_DE for the new prop strings (i18n guard). +1 cross-group exactness test.

    56. 🟢 The last guessing path closed (user screenshot + recipe: non-stop double-click renames; the active dot reappeared on the wrong row after each mid-storm rebuild). Rows rebuilt from still-stale members carried vl_index=-1 (name unfindable), so the draw fell back to the positional matcher - vacuous consistency in a storm - and could bind a row to the ACTIVE layer. The builder now passes the member's SAVED index through on a name miss; all member writes (adopt, both heals) stamp the index with the name. Identity now flows through one persisted coordinate at every layer: member (store, undo-consistent) -> row (mirror) -> draw. +1 storm-row test.

    57. 🟢 VLG strip's SECOND lookup bridged; duplicate-index double dot refused. draw_vl_group resolves its group twice; the icon-strip lookup still matched raw g.scene_name == scene.name (fails mid-burst after a scene rename) - now through _resolve_row_group. And an undo across a structural change can duplicate a saved index across two members: both rows resolved to one layer for a frame (the momentary second active dot). _resolve_row_vl detects a duplicate index among name-missing rows and binds neither - blank beats double; the settle resolves exactly.

    58. 🟢 Pointerless VLG records blanked the switched-to scene's icons for ~2 s (field: burst "canceled" by the VL switch - by design, now exact - then blank VLG strips). Legacy groups without a scene POINTER whose scene_name went stale mid-burst were unreachable by name AND refused by the index fallback's scene check. Reconcile now stamps the missing pointer whenever the stored name still resolves; the index fallback accepts a pointerless record whose stored scene name is provably dead (a dead name cannot contradict a coherently captured index). +1 test.

    59. 🟢 The switch detector was name-keyed (field correction: "the scene only switches, if I switch the layer and not renaming the scene tier"). vl_key = scene.name::view_layer.name - renaming the active scene/layer changed the key and ran the ENTIRE switch pipeline mid-rename (cascade re-apply, phantom VL-undo pushes, jit suppression, settle-gate bypass = "my rename burst got canceled"). Identity check first: same scene.session_uid + same layer position = a rename, absorbed by refreshing the stored names. All last_* trackers keep uid+index coherent; the undo-path tracker leaves them stale by design (degrades to classic switch treatment).

    60. 🟢 VLG render toggle flapped mid-burst (field: "flashes all the rendericons in all tiers"). The group row's render state resolves member layers by NAME; a stale member name mid-burst missed and the icon flipped to RESTRICT_RENDER_ON. Member resolution now falls back to the remembered vl_index - the standard identity contract.

    61. 🟢 Ungroup left the blue bar at the old index (field report). Both TKS_OT_UngroupScenes and TKS_OT_UngroupVLs now move tks_all_viewlayers_index to the FIRST ungrouped item's row after the sync and call notify_move_completed() so the snap guard is armed - the highlight never sits on whatever row slid into the freed slot.

    62. 🟢 The vanishing tree, closed at the root (field log: reconciled 1 item(s) (+0 -9) - the build emptied). Pointerless legacy SG members with a mid-burst-stale scene_name resolved nothing and the builder dropped every scene row. TKS_SceneGroupMember.scene_uid (stamped at reconcile/adopt/heal) + builder resolution pointer -> name -> uid; reconcile also stamps missing SG member pointers (Fixed 58's treatment, one tier up). Draw armor: filter_items degrades to show-everything and row draws to a name label, both logging tracebacks throttled into the addon log (a raising filter/draw was console-only - the sync timer's old blindness). GRID branch preserved. de_DE for new prop strings. +1 vanishing-tree regression test.

    63. 🟢 Witness ledgers keyed by scene session_uid (field: scene-tier camera record stayed empty after rename+undo; probed - the self-heal works whenever the ledger resolves). Name keys + rename re-key + undo restoring the OLD name = both rescue paths missed the entry under the NEW key. All seven ledgers now uid-keyed (survives rename AND undo); rename_scene_in_ledgers is a documented no-op; reapplyable_camera resolves name->uid and gains its bpy import (module-level bpy is TYPE_CHECKING-only in cascade.py - the accessor silently returned '' through the menu's fail-open except); native-sync + drift consumers and test fixtures swept; +1 rename+undo record-survival regression.

    64. 🟢 Undo pass restores the wiped record on the spot (field log with uid ledgers live: rename survived, then the deferred undo pass flipped exp_name to None permanently). The snapshot wipes the tier RECORD while the applied camera survives; the PRESERVE branch then overwrote the ledger with None, and apply_overrides only runs on triggers - the witness re-adoption never fired. New branch ahead of the Fixed-43 re-instate: surviving native == ledger memory + winner gone -> restore the record where the memory says it lived (Scene/ViewLayer tier), ledger untouched. One pass, trigger-independent. +1 regression.

    65. 🟢 Variant + Tag tree draw armor (pre-verification hardening for the phase-9 remainder). Both filter_items degrade to show-everything and both draw_items to a name label on exception, with throttled traceback logging - the Fixed-62 guarantee extended to all three trees. Audit note: both trees came out of the shared-engine adoption structurally clean (no name-keyed store lookups in the variant tree; the tag list's six name comparisons are same-frame live compares, permitted by the identity doctrine).

    66. 🟢 Shift-chevron collapsed every level in the variant/tag trees (user ruling: shift acts on the clicked level). Their pre-engine toggles drove ALL rows / all categories; now only rows of the clicked item_type (variant tree) and only the clicked category's groups (tag library) - the takes tree's contract everywhere.

    67. 🟢 Variant STATE rows were immovable and moves lost the highlight. TKS_OT_VSW_TreeMove.poll admitted only PART/MATERIAL; STATE moves now supported with the index-tracked product.active_index remapped so a move never silently changes the active state. After any move the operator finds the entity's new row in the rebuilt mirror and hands the blue bar over - the takes tree's handover contract.

    68. 🟢 Ctrl+Click children-walk worked only from PRODUCT rows. The variant toggle now walks descendants from ANY row via the shared _VSW_DEPTH map (mirror order until depth returns), same as the takes tree - headers with depth-2/3 children previously did nothing.

    69. 🟢 Preset unlink (✕) cleared a fixed tier, not the owning one. ui/preset_rows.py → preset_row() never set override_tier on either ✕ button, so TKS_OT_SelectPreset fell back to its property default "SCENE". The rows draw the applied config, which sync_preset_cascade() resolves over TAKE > VL > VLG > SCENE > SG > GLOBAL, so a preset owned by a more specific tier won again immediately and the name never changed

      • a no-op for every non-Scene assignment. Only the untiered material / bookmark types cleared, because write_tier_preset routes them straight to the applied config (absent from PRESET_FIELDS). Distinct from the older all-tiers-empty defect in the same symptom family, whose fix is present and correct. Unrelated to World/Camera auto-adopt, which writes the tks_world / tks_camera pointers, not tks_*_preset. New resolve_clear_tier() in features/render_presets/ops_select.py reruns get_cascade_winner() and returns (tier, None) / (None, tier) / (None, None); the rows pass sentinel override_tier="WINNER", resolved in execute() before the write. Clearing a VL winner uncovers the Scene tier rather than wiping the chain (one undo step per click); SG / GLOBAL are shared defaults, so a scene-local unlink reports the owning tier and returns CANCELLED instead of destroying them - the same Scene-rank clear cap the camera cascade applies. Tier list read from _TIER_PRESET_FIELDS (the constant that registers the tier props) to avoid the list-drift class that produced the world_preset registration bug. preset_selector_row() popovers keep exact per-tier revert semantics; apply_only prepends keep "NONE". Regression test dev/tests/test_preset_clear_winning_tier.py (5 tests, one pinning the defective mechanism itself); full suite 1828 passed. Commit ba894ecf. See doc/troubleshooting/preset_clear_sync_cascade.md (Root Cause 2).
    70. 🟢 Product rename orphaned every stored assignment (field: "changing the vsw product name is loosing the assignment on the takes tree"). Cascade tokens are "ProductName:variant_index" - product half name-keyed. SIX holder kinds store a tks_vsw_cascade string: World / Scene / ViewLayer (registered onto the ID type in features/variant_switch/properties.py), plus TKS_Take (properties/groups_takes.py), TKS_SceneGroup (groups_scenes.py) and TKS_VLGroup (groups_vl_layers.py). The repair lived in TKS_OT_VSW_RenameItem.execute and walked only the first three, so the Take-level assignment - the one the takes tree renders - was never repaired. It was also unreachable from the primary path: ui_row_renderers._draw_product draws left.prop(product, "name", emboss=False), a direct RNA write that hits no operator, and name had no update=. New features/variant_switch/ref_repair.py owns all six holders and is driven by _on_product_name_changed, so inline field and rename dialog share one path; name_prev (seeded in _ensure_product_defaults) carries the old name because RNA callbacks fire post-write. Assignments were orphaned, never destroyed - renaming back restored them.
    71. 🟢 Inline product names could clash or be emptied. The tree's name field bypassed the uniqueness guard _unique_product_name gives the duplicate operator; two products sharing a name make every token ambiguous, and an empty name yields an unparseable token. The rename callback now routes through properties.groups.unique_group_name (.001 house convention) and restores the previous name on empty.
    72. 🟢 State move left stored indices behind. move_state (features/variant_switch/operators.py) remapped product.active_index only; stored tokens are index-keyed too, so a move silently repointed every assignment onto the swapped neighbour. repair_state_move() trades the two affected indices - variants.move() on adjacent indices is a swap, the only form the tree's Up/Down produces.

    73. 🟢 State delete shifted assignments onto their neighbours. A bare variants.remove(vi) left tokens below the hole one index high and tokens on the hole aiming at nothing. repair_state_delete() drops the entries on the removed state and decrements those below, so they keep resolving to the same state (pinned by test_delete_preserves_identity_of_the_shifted_assignment, which compares get_variant_display() before and after). A zero-states defensive branch drops the product's entries entirely; the operator's poll enforces a one-state minimum, so only a scripted caller reaches it.

    74. 🟢 Tag rows lost their colour swatch mid-rename (field report). The row demanded candidate.name == item.name BEFORE trusting its stored index, so while the live name ran ahead of the mirror nothing resolved (tag = None) and the swatch - drawn only if tag - vanished. New _resolve_row_tag() takes the INDEX as identity (collections never reorder on rename) and keeps the name lookup only for genuinely stale cases (out of range / undo-shifted). Same contract as vl_index in the takes tree. +1 test.

    75. 🟢 The tag/rule row write-back was broken two ways (field: "I still can name rules and tags the same name", "There is no suffix being added"). The tree edits the MIRROR ROW, and _on_tree_item_name_changed (a) wrote a GROUPED tag to category.tags[tag_index] - the FLAT list - though the index addresses group.tags, hitting an unrelated tag or nothing; and (b) never read the store's answer back, so a uniqueness suffix never reached the row and looked like it had not happened. The callback now resolves the owning collection and mirrors the final stored name back behind a re-entry guard; group headers propagate their suffixed name to members' group_name too.

    76. 🟢 Rules and tags now share ONE namespace (field: "rules and tag list still can have the same names"). Not cosmetic: _on_tag_renamed rewrites scene.tks_output_rule (a RULE reference) and scene.tks_assigned_tag (a TAG reference) alike when the stored value matches the old name - so a rule and a tag sharing a name means renaming either silently repoints the other's assignments file-wide. Uniqueness therefore spans the whole library rather than one category (_library_of_tag / _iter_library_tags), which is also what the user sees: the Rule and Tag libraries are two modes of one list. Group names likewise. +1 test.

    77. 🟢 The rebuild wrote rows back into the store (field: "the names reset back to before", "still can get the same name") - and this is why the uniqueness rule appeared absent in the app while passing every test. reconcile() patches row.name, firing the row write-back callback, which pushed the row's pre-rebuild (stale) name into the store - undoing the rename that triggered the sync and any .001 just applied. Rows are a projection; only user edits travel upward, so sync_tag_tree holds the guard across reconcile(). Second half: the guard variable was never defined at module level (an earlier insertion landed inside a class body), so re-entry protection had been dead entirely. Probed end-to-end in a live Blender: duplicate -> Alpha.001 in store + row, surviving the rebuild; a TAG taking a RULE's name -> Hero.001.

    78. 🟢 Rules and tags are SEPARATE namespaces (field + screenshots: "why are rules and tags still sharing the same name space?" - tags were pushed to a.002/a.003 by rule names; I had read the earlier ruling backwards). Split exactly along TAG_CATEGORY_TYPES (Rule Library: Output/Camera/ World/Material) vs TAG_DATATYPE_CATEGORIES (Tag Library), groups included. The coupling that made one namespace look necessary is fixed at its root instead: _on_tag_renamed rewrote tks_output_rule (RULE) and tks_assigned_tag (TAG) alike, so renaming a tag could repoint a same-named rule's assignments; the repair now runs only over its own kind (unknown owner still repairs both - safe default). Probed live: a tag taking a rule's name stays as typed; two tags still yield a / a.001.

      Write discipline (entries 70-73). Repairs use RNA setattr, never an idprop subscript: on the ID-level holders the property is registered onto the TYPE, so holder["tks_vsw_cascade"] = x creates a SEPARATE custom property the RNA read never sees (a repair that changes nothing); on the PropertyGroup holders it lands but skips _on_vsw_cascade_changed, i.e. the invalidate("vl_cascade") that rebuilds the takes tree read-model, leaving stale rows until the ~200 ms context sync timer (Constitution rule 4). finalize() invalidates unconditionally because those callbacks early-return while the mutation flag is held. Holders in the World's IDProperty storage are re-resolved by index per access (_take_resolver / _group_resolver), never held - tks_vsw_products edits churn that same storage and the backing array can move without a count change (0xC0000005 in IDP_GetPropertyFromGroup; Constitution rule 1). All three rules are pinned by source-level tests.

      Failed approach. The rename callback first copied the house guard from _on_take_name_update and gated on addon_is_mutating. That folds in is_applying, held during cascade applies and after file load - and a rename orphans assignments just as thoroughly in that window. The headless harness sits with is_applying=True post-load and all four rename tests failed with the repair never running. It now gates on is_undoing / is_redoing only; addon_is_mutating gates the tree rebuild instead. 16 regression tests in dev/tests/test_vsw_ref_repair.py; full suite 1844 passed. Commit 8041ef13. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/vsw_stored_assignment_repair.md.

    79. 🟢 The VSW product store and the Tag Library were still worlds[0] (CORR-14, ~20 sites across six modules). The take/group store was cured in Fixed 47; these two carried the identical defect. bpy.data collections are name-sorted at the C level, so a rename — or a world that sorts earlier — leaves the records where they are and points every reader somewhere else. New utils/store_world.py: a WorldStore resolving a store by the DATA it carries, carrier cached by session_uid (survives renames, plain int, no RNA retained), falling back to worlds[0] only when nothing carries yet — that is where the FIRST write lands. GROUP_STORE / VSW_STORE / TAG_STORE; _groups_shared.get_world() delegates, so all three share one implementation, and vl_lifecycle invalidates all three on load. Converted: core/variant_queries.py, features/variant_switch/{logic,ops_crud,panel,pool_resolve,properties}.py, features/smart_syntax/resolvers.py, operators/tags/ops_library.py, properties/tag_library.py. features/batch_render/cli_worker.py and features/still_mode/engine.py keep their scenes[0] fallbacks with an # ANCHOR-OK reason — both are standalone/spec-loaded paths with no package to reach a resolver through.

      Failed approach. Broadening GROUP_STORE to every world-hosted collection (adding tks_vl_version_sets) let a world carrying only a peripheral collection outrank the one holding the takes, and tripped test_no_internal_vlv_identifiers. Reverted to exactly the three collections the carrier resolved by before. 6 tests in dev/tests/test_store_world_carriers.py.

    80. 🟢 The Inspector's node-tree owner lookup could never hit (real bug, surfaced by CORR-15). sync_viewport.py walks iter_anim_targets(obj) where obj = update.id from depsgraph.updates — the EVALUATED copy. Probed on 5.2: update.id.session_uid == 0, .original.session_uid == 258, and the addresses differ. The two sub-target lookups keyed on _sub_target.as_pointer() into _nt_owner_cache, which is built from bpy.data.materials / worlds / lights — originals. Every lookup missed, so the "Blender names auto-actions after the OWNER, not the NodeTree" fallback silently never ran. The two sites three functions away already spelled _id.original, which is why half the feature worked and the bug stayed invisible. Both now resolve .original before keying.

    81. 🟢 Address-keyed memory that outlives its tick (CORR-15, 20 sites). as_pointer() is a raw address and Blender hands a freed one to the next datablock it allocates, so such a memory does not go empty when its subject dies — it answers for a stranger. Converted to session_uid: core/slot_split.py (_known_ptrs → _known_uids, the deferred duplicate worker's re-fetch, and both ledgers re-keyed from scene.name to scene.session_uid — INFO-12), core/vl_switch.py (_prev_names_by_id, _prev_mod_names), panels/inspector/cache.py (_nt_owner_cache) plus its four consumers in sync_jit / sync_viewport, and features/render_version/properties.py. Two kinds carry no session_uid: a Modifier is not an ID (keyed by Blender's own Modifier.persistent_uid, probed present on 5.2) and neither is a ViewLayer (keyed by (owning scene's session_uid, layer name)). Same-frame as_pointer() comparisons are left alone — that is the correct use.

    82. 🟢 Cascade camera lookups were file-wide (CRASH-01 K6). core/cascade.py and core/cascade_drift.py resolved a camera name through bpy.data.objects.get(), where the rest of the cascade already uses scene.objects.get() (and refuses a camera whose name is not in scene.objects). Three sites scoped to the scene, per Constitution rule 5.

    83. 🟢 Render-version major/minor semantics were ungated (CRASH-01 K4). _on_render_version_update had no undo guard, so a replayed write could zero a sub-version the undo step was about to restore.

      Failed approach. The house guard (addon_is_mutating or is_undoing) broke it: that flag is open for any addon write anywhere — a cascade on a timer — so a genuine user bump landing in such a window stopped resetting the minor, and test_{scene,viewlayer}_rev_bump_resets_subrev caught it. Narrowed to is_undoing / is_redoing, the same conclusion Fixed 78 reached for the VSW rename callback.

    84. 🟢 Two persistent handlers were invisible to the Process Monitor (REG-06). The load_post msgbus re-arms in core/{camera,world}_native_sync.py now register_process(...) / unregister_process(...) like every other handler the addon owns. Coverage 94.7% → 100%.

    85. 🟢 Four operators ran without a poll() (CORR-07), and 14 broad excepts carried no reason (CORR-05). TKS_OT_RenderJobsRescan, TKS_OT_RenderJobsDragResize, TKS_OT_VSW_ConflictsRescan and TKS_OT_VSW_RevealPool got real preconditions — the POLL_NOT_NEEDED marker on ConflictsRescan sat INSIDE the class body, where the check does not look, and was replaced with an actual poll rather than moved. The 14 never-die guards around UIList draw/filter bodies and the sync timer now carry # CORR-05-OK with the reason they must stay broad: a draw that raises kills the panel, and a timer that raises is silently unregistered for the session.

      Auditor side: CORR-15 produced one false positive — a helper nested inside a sweep, filling a dict the sweep created (vl_switch_fast.py's _rest_bind_counts). Fixed at the check (scope-tree inheritance + reach-through-accessor locality, with an escaping helper inheriting nothing), 4 regression tests, and blender-addon-auditor/doc/troubleshooting/corr15_nested_helper_false_positive.md. Scan after the pack: Code Quality 4.7 → 10.0 / 10.0, deduction 5.34 → 0.00, all audits clean. Full suite 1979 passed. Commit 57e103d9. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/auditor_fixpack_pointer_and_anchor.md.

    86. 🟢 83 operators reported SUCCESS to a scripted caller and did nothing (AI-01). Constitution rule 7: an MCP bridge runs bpy.ops.tks.<op>() from a bpy.app.timers callback, so Blender runs execute(), not invoke(). 67 popover launchers plus a props-dialog, a panel launcher, a menu launcher and 13 modifier-driven operators had the work in invoke() and return {'FINISHED'} in execute() — the single most misleading shape an addon can offer an assistant. 76 are now invocation-aware: invoke() sets self._tks_invoked, execute() branches on it and otherwise calls the new utils/click_only.refuse_scripted(), which names the operator and CANCELs. The other 7 (TKS_OT_Legend*, TKS_OT_SoundInfo, TKS_OT_RQStatTooltip, TKS_OT_RenderQueueInfoIcon) are tooltip carriers with no work for ANY caller and carry # AI-01-OK instead — {'FINISHED'} is honest there.

      Failed approach. A bare return refuse_scripted(self) as the whole body. The awareness test reads which self.<attr> names execute() touches, so a helper call reads as unaware — and, worse, Blender routes a popup's Return-key confirm back through execute(), so it would have raised an error toast on every ordinary click. The marker read has to be in execute() itself, which is why was_invoked() was dropped again (MAINT-01 caught it as dead).

    87. 🟢 18 operators were unusable from a timer (AI-02). Seven that reach call_panel / invoke_props_dialog / call_menu_pie / INVOKE_DEFAULT from execute() now refuse in poll() (context.window is not None) instead of raising from inside. Eleven dereferenced a windowless member: the context.screen.areas loops in ops_utils, ops_camera_levels, ops_viewlayer_camera and render_scope_ops are getattr-guarded so the camera is still created and only the "align it to the 3D view" half is skipped; context.window.view_layer / .scene in ops_utils, ops_output_rules and ops_manage fall back to the context's own; and tks.add_viewlayer reports why a non-active target scene needs a window rather than tracebacking.

      Auditor side: AI-02 produced three false positives — context.area.type if context.area else None is a guard, but _guarded_names never harvested ast.IfExp tests. Fixed at the check with 2 regression tests and blender-addon-auditor/doc/troubleshooting/ai02_ternary_guard_blind.md.

    88. 🟢 151 deferred imports for 12 (file, module) pairs (ARCH-04.2). panels/context/properties.py deferred core.cascade 20×, operators/cascade/_helpers.py deferred properties.groups 16×, three files deferred utils.tks_log 10× each. All downward, leaf-ward targets with no import-time back-edge, so each collapses to one module-level import in the header block; surrounding try/except blocks stay, since they guard the logging CALL. Also take added to the §4.2 property-infix allow-list in lockstep with the auditor's _PROP_INFIX_ALLOW (INFO-05), and the last three uncentralized texts moved into texts/ with German (INFO-09 + INFO-10).

    89. 🟢 Remove had two gates that computed different answers. panels/tag_library_ui/draw.py greyed the button from the ACTIVE ROW alone (is_tag or is_group_header) and ignored multiselect; TKS_OT_DeleteTagItem.poll switched to the TICKED ROWS whenever wm.tks_multiselect_list == "TAGS". With multiselect on, no state satisfied both at once — ticking a checkbox left the panel gate False, moving the active row left the poll False — so Remove was greyed in every reachable state, Rule mode and Tag mode alike. Both now read sync.removable_tag_row(wm), which returns the row Remove would act on or None. It takes wm, not context, deliberately: the panel must not inherit the poll's in_sidebar guard (it is already drawing in the sidebar; a context miss there would grey the button for an unrelated reason), so the poll applies that guard on top for single-item deletes. dev/tests/test_tag_remove_gate.py (6 tests) pins each answer — including the previously unreachable ticked-row-plus-category-header state — and asserts structurally that neither call site hand-rolls the gate again; verified RED on the old panel line, GREEN on the shared one. Commit cf1fca2d.

      First attempt (05cd65d6, below) fixed the same class of defect in draw_tag_tree_view, which no panel calls — dead code, so it changed nothing in the field. Kept, with its guard, since that function is still exported. Diagnostic lesson: confirm the drawer under investigation is actually reachable from a registered panel before reading anything into what it does.

      Superseded detail — the dead-code attempt. panels/tag_library_ui/draw.py::draw_tag_tree_view draws tks.delete_tag_item (and the add/group operators) but never set window_manager.tks_active_list_context = "TAGS". Every tag operator's poll goes through _resolve_active_tag_item, which reads that flag, so all of them evaluated False and drew greyed — in both Rule and Tag mode. The sibling panel draw_tag_library_mode has set it since it was written (line 166), which is why the same operators work there and the defect looked mode-specific. Pre-existing, not a regression from the tree-reliability campaign (git log shows the file untouched by it); surfaced now that the tree view is the primary surface. One-line claim added after the docstring. Guarded structurally by dev/tests/test_tag_panel_list_context.py (2 tests): it walks the panel module's AST and fails any draw_* function that mentions a tag operator without assigning tks_active_list_context. Verified RED on the unfixed file and GREEN on the fix — the polls themselves are not exercisable headlessly (they additionally require a sidebar region), but the invariant that actually drifted is exactly the one asserted. Commit 05cd65d6.

      Scan after the pass: Maturity 9.38 → 9.74, AI Readiness 7.12 → 8.75 (silent 83 → 0, unsafe 21 → 0), Wiki Health 9.35 → 9.75, Architecture 9.84 → 9.96, Quality 10.0, Reliability 10.0. AI-03 (181 capabilities a script cannot reach) stays open by decision — it is the remaining ai-ready roadmap phases, not a defect. Full suite 1979 passed. Commits 8a929d7d, f74bd8a5. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/ai_drivability_and_import_piles.md. 90. 🟢 Cascade Drift could show alongside another warning panel.

    90. 🟢 A view-layer switch is no longer mistaken for the user animating. A switch MOVES objects, and Blender delivers those depsgraph updates on the tick AFTER is_applying drops — so sync_viewport's fresh-action detection read the switch's own motion as authoring, and _process_fresh_actions manufactured an empty {scene}_{viewlayer} action per click (fcurves=0, fake_user=True, one per view layer). Found with a stack-trace tripwire (dev/experiments/trap_action_creation.py) after four rounds of name-watching found nothing: a timer-based watcher always arrives after the frame that did the work and can never name the caller. See doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_manufactured_empty_actions.md.

    91. 🟢 Object.tks_action is a fallback, not a veto. Both apply_action_to_watched AND apply_vl_switch_unified skipped any object carrying it — two enforcement sites, so fixing one changed nothing the user could see. That made the field an absolute, silent, permanent veto, while the addon's own auto-assign WRITES into it with a generated name. Ruling (user): the cascade wins; is_pinned() is the only hands-off, and it must be asked with scene=, because pins are keyed scene::viewlayer and the helper falls back to the ACTIVE scene — which a sequencer follow never is.

    92. 🟢 An action with no populated slots clears nothing. apply_action_to_watched unassigns whatever the cascade action does not cover — right for a real action, catastrophic for an empty one. Logged in the field as apply_action_to_watched: action='01-01_red', 84 objects, populated_slots=[].

    93. 🟢 Returning applies the take instead of only moving the window. Mechanism in Added 37.

    94. 🟢 Every trigger reaches the timeline. Nine causes, all recorded in doc/troubleshooting/sequencer_scene_autoswitch_triggers.md: keymap placement (three separate routes), a MOUSEMOVE registered with 'PRESS' (registers cleanly, matches never — now caught statically by the auditor's CORR-17), bpy.ops from a timer with the RuntimeError swallowed, reset_applied() wiping the scrub baseline on every tick, is_animation_playing being TRUE during a scrub (_real_playback exists for exactly that and says so ten lines above the guard that ignored it), and the timer reading bpy.context.window rather than every window.

    95. 🟢 The Frames LEFTMOUSE binding is gone. A window-level click says nothing about where it landed, so with only Playhead switched on, clicking a strip switched the scene. A test fails if it ever reappears on that map.

    96. 🟢 needs_cascade creation follows auto_assign. The branch created the action FIRST and consulted the preference only for the tier write — and the only log line on that path sits inside the auto_assign block, so with Auto-Assign off the addon still created, silently. Field report: "auto assign option off is not creating or assigning anymore" while empty actions kept appearing.

    97. 🟢 The VL-switch detector is scoped to the window's scene. Blender delivers depsgraph events for other scenes — a VSE scene strip being evaluated, a background view-layer preload — and the key paired the handler's scene ARGUMENT with the WINDOW's view layer, building a mismatched key that could never equal last_key. The detector then declared a switch and ran the whole pipeline against a view layer that was not even a member of that scene, which surfaced as take state flipping to a foreign take while scrubbing a sequencer timeline. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-19.) The warning subpanels are one-at-a-time via _make_warning_callback, which walks a tuple of sibling props and clears them. tks_show_cascade_drift was registered WITH that callback but was missing from the tuple, making the relationship one-way: opening Cascade Drift closed everything else, but opening anything else never closed Cascade Drift, so it stacked on top of whatever was already showing. It was the only toggle in that state. Fixed at the source rather than by adding the name - the set was typed out by hand in two modules (panels/navigation/__init__.py and logic.py::_ensure_exclusive_warning, whose stale copy held only the original five), which is what let the live list drift unnoticed. WARNING_TOGGLE_PROPS now lives once in navigation/logic.py and both read it. dev/tests/test_warning_toggle_exclusivity.py parses both modules (no bpy) and asserts in BOTH directions that the props registered with the callback are exactly the props in the tuple. Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/warning_subpanel_exclusivity_drift.md. Commit 8a01790b.

    98. 🟢 The autokey mirror's suppression window is two windows. (In-app confirmed 2026-08-20. User Fixed 123.) core/cascade_actions armed one wall-clock window before its snap pass so the addon's own rest-value writes were not read back as user edits. But the cascade handler runs in the SAME depsgraph tick as the mirror and one slot EARLIER (depsgraph_update_post slot 10 vs 11), so keying an object the cascade adopts armed the window and then muted the mirror on the very tick carrying the key. Split by the writer it mutes: HARD (VL/take switch) still stops the handler dead; SOFT marks an addon-own-write window and guards only the non-keyed branch, because a property write never carries a keyframe. Windows extend with max() so re-arming cannot shorten one. Both gates are old (throttle 2026-04-03, arming seam 2026-07-12); the 2026-08-19 switch contract made the cascade run where it used to stand back, which turned a latent race into a certainty.

    99. 🟢 The 50 ms throttle no longer drops the tick carrying the keyframes. (User Fixed 124.) A drag fires a tick every ~10 ms and autokey lands its keys on mouse-release, at the end of that burst, so the keyed tick met a hot throttle. A dropped tick is gone: the next survivor no longer advertises the Action, so has_action_update is False and the handler waits for a keyframe already past. has_action_update is resolved BEFORE the throttle now and exempts a tick that carries an Action. Not an extra scan - the decision phase needed that value anyway, so it is computed once and reused.

    100. 🟢 No bpy.data writes inside depsgraph evaluation. (User Fixed 125.) _handle_autokey_mirror drained the mutation queue synchronously in its finally (27d65e6a, 2026-05-09, to fold writes into the user's own undo step) and called _redirect_orphan_action inline. Both write during scene_graph_update_tagged: insert_rest_keyframe calls animation_data_create(), reassigns ad.action and inserts a keyframe; the redirect called bpy.data.actions.remove() on a material's auto-created action. Two EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATIONs in deg_update_eval_copy_datablock, plus an instant crash on I over a material value field. The queue timer owns the writes; the redirect is queued as _apply_orphan_redirect; test_handler_body_contains_no_bpy_data_writes guards the handler body at source level, since a depsgraph-evaluation crash has no headless repro.

    101. 🟢 The SOFT window no longer starves the revert witness. (User Fixed 126.) revert_snap only snaps a target that WITNESSED a key-count drop, and that baseline is seeded by the incremental re-snapshot - inside the same non-keyed branch the SOFT window guards. Alt+I on a freshly touched target therefore read keys 0->0, no witnessed loss and did nothing. _seed_revert_witness runs even while the window is open: a key COUNT cannot carry our own writes into the rest cache the way a value re-snapshot can.

    102. 🟢 RNA types on both sides of a rest value. (User Fixed 126, 129.) A rest value comes out of an FCurve, so it is always a float, and Blender refuses a float on an INT, BOOLEAN or ENUM property - the write threw and the property never got a baseline. core/path_utils.coerce_rna_value casts on the way in (INT rounds, BOOLEAN casts, ENUM maps the number back to its identifier; flag enums and unknown values pass through untouched). rna_value_as_number reads a dropdown's identifier back out as a number. is_array_value stops a string counting as an array - an enum identifier answers both __len__ and __getitem__, then dies on "'str' object does not support item assignment". Separately _snap_one_target wrote scalars with setattr(target, data_path, val), which works for location and throws "'ShaderNodeTree' object has no attribute" for anything nested - the material editor failing while the 3D viewport worked.

    103. 🟢 The revert snaps only the channels that lost a key. (User Fixed 127. User ruling 2026-08-20.) The witness was one total count per target - it could answer "did this target lose a key?" and never "which channel?", so a single Alt+I dragged every unkeyed property on the datablock back to rest, checkboxes included once the RNA fix finally gave them baselines. _slot_keyed_channels returns a frozenset of (data_path, array_index); the scan passes prev - cur into _snap_one_target(..., only_paths=...). only_paths=None still snaps everything, which the cascade-clear path wants. Unrelated drift is the drift warning's job.

    104. 🟢 The revert asks for a redraw. (User Fixed 128.) It runs on a timer, so nothing else repaints for it: the values were reverted and the viewport kept painting the old ones until the next event. It calls signal_redraw() after a revert that changed something (house rule 3).

    105. 🟢 One undo step per gesture, not one per queue drain. (User Fixed 130.) The queue pushed "Takes Auto-Merge" at the end of every drain with work, and one keyframe makes three (orphan redirect, the mirror write its own writes trigger, the revert). The push is armed on a settle timer, re-armed by every further drain AND by every enqueue so it tracks the reaction chain rather than the drain cadence - 0.35 s split a Properties-editor gesture in half, 0.8 s holds it - and it closes the gesture after firing. Two presses is the floor: one would mean folding the writes into the operator's undo step, i.e. writing during evaluation again. _undo_push() is a named seam because bpy.ops.ed is rebuilt on every attribute access, so patching it patches a throwaway wrapper.

    106. 🟢 Live apply borrows autokey instead of keeping it. (User Fixed 131. User ruling 2026-08-20.) Arming switched autokey off and left it off, on the reasoning that turning it back on is the user's deliberate act. The lived result was the opposite of that intent: one preview and autokey was gone for the session with nothing saying why. remember_autokey_kill / restore_autokey_if_killed return it on every disarm door - the operator toggle and live_apply.disarm (watchdog, context-left, render start). Autokey already off before arming is left alone, and the borrow never crosses a file load. The restore runs after the scene is put right and after the watchdog has seen the disarm, so it cannot re-fire.

    107. 🟢 The addon deletes no Action, ever. (User Fixed 132.) The orphan cleanup called bpy.data.actions.remove() on a zero-user orphan, contradicting its own docstring and the standing fake_user policy - and the depsgraph can still hold a relation to the freed ID, so the next DEG_graph_relations_update walked a dead pointer (BKE_animdata_from_id inside build_driver_relations). Clearing fake_user hands it to Blender's GC, which frees it at a moment when nothing points at it.

    108. 🟢 Viewport tool sync pays the tolls every depsgraph handler owes. (User Fixed 133.) features/sync/handlers_viewport._on_depsgraph_update writes tool settings into every other scene and had neither an addon_is_mutating gate nor a Process Monitor entry. The log for 2026-08-20 15:40:10 shows 28 cross-scene propagations inside the second an undo was unwinding, and that second ended in an access violation inside bpy_app_generic_callback. Gated now, and registered as "Viewport Tool Sync" so it can be switched off - it was the only handler on that event that could not be ruled in or out while bisecting. NOT claimed as the fix for that crash: it is intermittent and has not reproduced on demand.

    109. 🟢 A refusal that cannot explain itself. Remove sat behind a panel-side layout.enabled in front of TKS_OT_DeleteTagItem.poll. A panel gate cannot state a reason, and it suppresses the poll's message, so all four refusal conditions rendered as the same dead button — which is why two rounds of this report (entry 89, and the dead-code attempt below) were diagnosed from source rather than from the screen, and both missed. The panel gate is removed: the poll is the only gate, and every return False sets poll_message_set naming the condition (empty list / multi-select with nothing ticked / active row is a category header / cursor outside the sidebar / another list holds tks_active_list_context, named). Verified in a GUI Blender probe rather than headlessly: every gate on this path reads context.area/.region, which do not exist under --background, so the headless suite cannot exercise the poll at all — the probe confirmed poll=True for a focused tag row, False for each refusal, and that a real delete succeeds in the sidebar context. Three structural tests: the panel may not re-add a gate, the poll keeps sharing removable_tag_row, and no refusal in the poll may be silent. Commit 8339f238.

      Also ruled out by evidence, recorded so they are not re-derived: the tks_active_list_context draw-order race (TKS_PT_Context order 2 claims CONTEXT, TKS_PT_Globals order 4 claims TAGS) cannot bite here because the three claimants are mutually exclusive branches of the same panel's mode; and the confirm-dialog re-poll theory fails because TKS_OT_DeleteTreeItem has the identical structure and works in the field.

    110. 🟢 Delete reported {'FINISHED'} for tags it never removed. Both delete paths skipped an index they could not match and returned success regardless, so a stale tag_index (the row moved between the click and the confirm) or a category that no longer matched was indistinguishable from a real delete — a usable button that leaves the tag on screen, which is the same disease as entry 90 one layer down. Removal is now verdict-based: _remove_single_tag() returns whether a tag actually went, the batch branch counts what it removed, and every exit in invoke/execute reports — nothing selected, multi-select with nothing ticked, empty list, no library, "the tag list changed underneath". German strings in lockstep. Six tests over the helper plus a structural one: no CANCELLED in either method may return without a self.report within the preceding lines. Commit 8a5fb4c8.

    111. 🟢 A vanished group deleted an unrelated tag. Found by the entry-91 tests, and older than this thread. In both delete paths target was initialised to cat.tags and only reassigned when info['group_name'] matched a live group. When the group had been renamed or deleted, target stayed on the UNGROUPED list while tag_index still meant "inside the group" — so the delete removed whatever unrelated ungrouped tag happened to sit at that position. Both paths now refuse (single returns False, batch continues) rather than fall back: a wrong delete is worse than a refused one. Pinned by test_a_missing_group_does_not_delete_from_the_ungrouped_list, which failed on the pre-fix code with ['beta'] != ['alpha', 'beta'].

    112. 🟢 A poll that depended on the region it was asked in. THE fix for the field report. _resolve_active_tag_item opened with in_sidebar(context), so every tag operator's poll answered differently depending on WHERE Blender evaluated it. Blender polls a button in more contexts than the panel draw — building the tooltip is one — and in those the region is not the sidebar, so Remove disabled itself and then explained the refusal with a condition the screenshot disproved: tooltip "Move the mouse over the Takes sidebar" with the cursor over the Takes sidebar. Entries 89–92 each fixed a real defect on this path but none was the cause; this one is.

      The guard was redundant. It exists to stop DEL/X acting on tags out in the viewport, and that rule already lives at the keyboard entry points: no tag operator is bound to a key at all (only tks.global_* are), and all ten dispatchers poll _in_sidebar before routing. Removed from the resolver and from TKS_OT_DeleteTagItem.poll; keyboard behaviour is unchanged. What remains is the focus flag, a WindowManager property that reads identically in every context — which is what a poll needs.

      dev/tests/test_tag_poll_is_region_free.py (4 tests). Two of them could not have existed before the fix: headless Blender has no area or region, so the old resolver returned None there for exactly the reason the field hit — which is also why five rounds of headless reasoning could not see it. Verified RED on the pre-fix code. The other two pin that focus is still required and that all ten dispatchers still own the sidebar rule. Commit 17167985.

      Rule for this codebase: a poll may only read state that is the same in every context Blender might ask it in. WindowManager and scene properties qualify; context.area/.region do not. Region rules belong at the keyboard entry point, which is polled once, where the cursor is.

    113. 🟢 Moving a tag renamed the tag it moved. A move adds the tag to its destination BEFORE removing the source, so for one instant the name existed twice in the namespace and the uniqueness rule renamed the ARRIVAL: retargeting "blue" produced "blue.001", and TKS_OT_TagGroupCreate did the same to every tag it gathered into a new group. Both now run inside properties.tag_library.migrating_tags(), a re-entrant context manager around the existing _migrating_tags flag (re-entrant so it composes with _copy_tag_into_group, which sets the same flag). A genuine duplicate is still caught — the source is gone by the time the guard lifts. Also on this path: the move stamped the tag's group_name with the enum SENTINEL, so a tag sent to Ungrouped claimed membership of a group called "__UNGROUPED__"; it is "" now. dev/tests/test_tag_retarget_destinations.py (10 tests) covers both, RED before the fix with ['loose.001'] != ['loose']. Commit 99c86047.

    114. 🟢 pgettext_rpt used without importing it. operators/ops_global_shortcuts.py:446 — the Alt+D branch that explains a product copy is always unlinked called pgettext_rpt(...) in a module that never imported it, so the line raised NameError instead of reporting. Added from bpy.app.translations import pgettext_rpt, the same import every other reporting module uses. Found by the auditor's CORR-11 (its only finding on the addon).

    115. 🟢 Debug-log switches and log calls had drifted apart in BOTH directions. utils/logger.py resolves its gate by NAME with a permissive default (getattr(prefs, f"log_topic_{topic.lower()}", True)), so nothing joins the two sides and neither kind of drift fails loudly. Ungated (CORR-16, 17 gates / 72 lines). A topic or subtopic with no property logged unconditionally, invisible in Developer › Topics and impossible to switch off — UI:HOTKEYS alone was 27 lines, and topic="OPERATORS" was a typo for OPS whose whole topic never existed. Eight gates were SYNONYMS of a live switch and were retargeted onto it rather than given a new one: OPERATORS:CLEANUP→OPS:ANIM, OPS:MISC→OPS:GENERAL, UI:RENAME→OPS:RENAME, BATCH:STATS + BATCH:ETA→BATCH:PROGRESS, CORE:reload→CORE:INIT, CORE:VARIANT→FEATURES:VSW, CORE:world_popover→UI:POPOVERS. Nine genuinely new concepts got a switch: core_rename, core_ai, core_event_bus, core_providers, core_cache, ui_hotkeys, features_preview, batch_progress, preset_colormanagement. Orphaned (MAINT-08, 16 switches / 12 findings). Dead checkboxes, including the entire RENDER group (topic + 4 subtopics) left behind when batch logging moved to the BATCH topic. Deleted, plus expand_log_topic_render. Wiring. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 545 → 537 (−17 +9). The removed keys drain from saved configs via _LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS in persistence_io.py — they controlled nothing, so nothing migrates. draw_debug.py topic lists and the addon_prefs_constants.py expand tuple updated in lockstep (the list lives in FOUR places and only the count fails loudly — see the troubleshooting doc). texts/locales/de_DE.py: 12 orphaned entries removed, 8 new labels translated (Color Management already existed). Enforcement. Both directions are now checked on every scan by the auditor's CORR-16 and MAINT-08, both at 0 after this change. doc/troubleshooting/log_switches_out_of_sync.md. This is Stage 1 of doc/roadmap/ideas/debug-log-taxonomy.md; the topic RENAME is Stage 2 and is untouched here.

    116. 🟢 Two store-recovery operators and one keymap teardown carried no auditor marker. TKS_OT_DismissStoreNotice / TKS_OT_RestoreStoreSnapshot (CORR-07) are INTERNAL and drawn only inside a row that already tested the same condition; a poll() would duplicate that predicate where disagreeing with it greys out the user's only way back to their panels, and for the restore the only real precondition is a DISK read that would then run on every redraw. Both carry # POLL_NOT_NEEDED with that reasoning. features/variant_switch/ops_crud.py:819 (CORR-01) is addon-keyconfig teardown removing by identity — the same shape already sentinel'd in ops_global_shortcuts.py — and now carries # CORR-01-OK. Also removed utils/store_snapshot.py::baseline_accepted, a public getter with no callers (MAINT-01); the module reads _baseline_accepted directly.

    117. 🟢 Six subsystems wrote no log line at all. INFO-13 reported five dark packages plus the take-data safety copy, which wrote ONE line filed under "List Sync". Instrumented at the DECISION seams rather than sprinkled: core/store_guardian.attempt_recovery() had six silent early returns, so "why did it not restore my data" had six possible answers and no trace of which; utils/store_snapshot.write() froze the copy on a detected regression without saying so; still_mode/engine.apply_still_for_vl() is the single seam every take switch and both toggles pass through; bookmarks import skipped malformed and duplicate entries with a bare continue, so "Imported 3" out of twelve was unexplainable; render_version detect reports "nothing on disk" identically whether the scan found nothing or the version token never resolved. Not dark, differently plumbed. features/smart_syntax/engine.py was logging through Python's stdlib logging, which reaches Blender's console but NOT the addon log file and has no switch in Topics — including the unresolved-token warning, the one a silently-wrong render path depends on. Its four calls now route through tks_log under FEATURES:NAMING. The same parallel channel exists in ~10 other modules (core/cascade.py, features/batch_render/*) and is left for a follow-up. Level discipline, learnt from the keymap tick. Anything on a heartbeat is DEBUG or silent: the snapshot write (2s tick), the viewport-sync propagate (every tool-settings change), the bookmark duplicate-skip. INFO and above is reserved for a decision the user would ask about. Switches. +6 (core_store, features_still, features_naming, features_sync, features_bookmarks, features_version); EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 537 → 543. log_sub_features_naming was dropped as an orphan in entry 96 and comes back with call sites, so it is also removed from _LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS — a key in the drain AND in the props would be stripped from disk on every save. de_DE re-keyed (+6). Result. INFO-13 dark 5 → 0, 27 → 32 packages logging; CORR-16 and MAINT-08 stay at 0.

    118. 🟢 The keymap audit wrote to disk every two seconds to say nothing happened. utils/keymap_audit.diff_snapshots() logged [AUDIT-DIFF] <label>: no changes at INFO and called _flush_now() on that branch — a synchronous write, on a periodic tick, in a logger whose whole design is to batch I/O from 100+/sec down to 1/sec (see utils/logger._flush_log_buffer). ~24 lines and 24 flushes a minute for the lifetime of a session. Now DEBUG and unflushed; the change-detected branch still flushes immediately, which is the case actually worth having on disk before a crash. Found by reading a user's live log after the UI:HOTKEYS switch made those lines visible for the first time.

    119. 🔴 The camera link confirm dialog's OK button looped forever. tks.link_camera_and_assign opened its three-choice confirm via wm.invoke_props_dialog, whose own OK re-enters execute() on the dialog instance — mode still 'PROMPT' there, and that branch (the EXEC-context fallback for picker-menu dispatch) reopened the dialog. The footer also duplicated Cancel. Replaced with a wm.popup_menu (self-closing, footer-free, ESC/click-outside cancels): module-level _draw_confirm_menu(layout, p) / _open_confirm_menu(context, p) over a plain props dict (the op instance is freed before the menu draws); both entry paths return {'INTERFACE'}. Explicit Cancel entry dropped; CANCEL mode kept. Regression-pinned by dev/tests/test_link_camera_confirm.py (4 tests, recording-layout pattern). Root-cause record: doc/troubleshooting/camera_link_confirm_loop.md. Suite 2186/0.

    120. 🟢 Log topics renamed after the SYMPTOM, not the folder. Stage 2 of doc/roadmap/ideas/debug-log-taxonomy.md. The old set was half symptom (CASCADE, REST as subtopics) and half package (CORE, UI, OPS, DATA, FEATURES), and a package-named topic has no natural boundary - which is exactly why CORE had grown to hold half of every log line in the addon across 14 subtopics while DATA held one. The new set is 12 topics named for what a user would REPORT: SWITCH, ANIM, REST, VARIANT, RENDER, PRESET, NAMING, TAGS, STORE, UI, OPS, SYSTEM, with 51 subtopics. STORE exists because the take-data safety copy previously filed its lines under "List Sync", which is the case that started this whole thread. OPS is reframed from a second junk drawer ("User Actions") into the operator TRACE channel - what ran, with what, and what it returned. The migration is a committed script, dev/scripts/log_taxonomy_migrate.py, whose MAPPING table IS the decision: 53 reviewable lines instead of 489 diff hunks, re-runnable after main moves, and idempotent (a pair already in target form is skipped). It rewrites the positional tks_log_active(topic, sub) form as well as the keyword one - the omission that let BATCH:ETA survive Stage 1's first pass. Result. 489 call sites in 102 files. 12 topics + 51 subtopics + 12 accordion flags replace 8 + 52 + 8; EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 553 → 560. All 43 dead keys drain via _LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS rather than migrating - a switch called log_sub_core_rest gated lines that now answer to log_sub_rest_state, so its saved value is stale by construction, and a logging preference is one tick to set again. de_DE: +16, −6 orphans. Verified with the auditor against the branch: CORR-16 0 ungated, MAINT-08 0 orphaned, INFO-13 0 dark, 52 gates in use across 63 switches (51 subtopic pairs + one topic-only RENDER).

    121. 🟢 False red "missing camera" flag judged against the ACTIVE scene (in-app confirmed 2026-08-16) (user screenshot 2026-08-16: switch to an empty camera-less scene → other scenes' takes flag red; user-facing log: Fixed 57; camera-cross-scene-linking P0). core/cascade_validation.py::is_missing_camera(name) read bpy.context.scene.objects — every tier row was checked against whatever scene was active, and the (scene, vl)-keyed status cache (_vl_cascade_cache) served the wrong answer regardless of later switches while the 200 ms recompute re-derived it. The false positive also suppressed the genuine inherited-unlinked branch behind the not _missing_camera gate. Fix: required scene parameter, no context fallback — VL/Scene/VLG/Take rows pass the row's scene, SG/Global pass None (existence + CAMERA type only; membership is per-scene there) — threaded through all 14 call sites (draw_layers, draw_scenes, draw_collections, draw_tree_nodes, lists_context, lists_split). Second leak closed: draw_vl's scene = context.scene rename-staleness fallback now draws the row inert for that tick instead of binding it — and its cache entry, under a foreign key — to the active scene. Architectural rule: a per-row status is computed from the row's own data, never from bpy.context. Tests: dev/tests/test_missing_camera_scene.py (3). Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/false_red_camera_flag_active_scene.md. Commit b7667605.

    122. 🟢 Cascade drift fired on the engine's own unlinked-winner skip (field report minutes after the feature shipped; user-facing log: Fixed 58). Switching into a scene whose camera inherits from Global/SG without being linked there showed "Assignment changed outside Takes tree: Camera → None" — but the mismatch was engine-made: the skip branch (core/cascade.py, unlinked-winner validation) withholds the apply AND, via the elif not _cam_unlinked_winner: guard, writes nothing to the drift ledger, so get_cascade_drifts compared a stale expectation against scene.camera=None. The "camera needed" nag fired in the same state although the tree does assign a camera (it just can't reach the scene). Fix: new engine tracker _last_cam_unlinked_winner (session_uid → winner name; popped at the start of every camera pass, set on the skip branch), and the detector's camera block stands down entirely while it is set (DEBUG log names the suppression) — the red flags + Camera Links warning own that state. Genuine native clears of a linked, applied camera still raise their row (control test). Known deliberate leftover, documented: native picks in a skipped scene aren't adopted while the skip stands (the same guard bypasses adoption) — follow-up candidate. Tests: dev/tests/test_cascade_drift_unlinked_skip.py (3). Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/cascade_drift_unlinked_camera_skip.md. Commit b3317002.

    123. 🟢 Warning-row tier labels say "ViewLayer", not "VL" (user screenshot; user-facing log: Fixed 59). The display group_type built by core/assignment_health.py (broken-assignment rows, incl. the variant branch) and features/render_presets/preset_health.py (missing-preset rows) abbreviated the view-layer tier to "VL" while every other surface — cascade source labels, popover headers — and the de_DE catalog use "ViewLayer" (the catalog even mapped the stray 'VL' to 'Ansichtsebene', so the abbreviation showed only in English). Machine tier identifiers (tier='VL', operator props) untouched. Tests: dev/tests/test_warning_row_tier_labels.py (2). Commit 20a06b08.

    124. 🟢 Replace was dead on Variant broken-assignment rows (user screenshot; user-facing log: Fixed 60). TKS_OT_ReplaceBrokenAssignment built its target as f"{tier}_{type}_popover" with _TYPE_SUFFIX covering only the four pointer types, so VARIANT — added to the health scan later — fell through to a Unknown tier/type: VL/VARIANT warning that reads like a data problem but is a missing mapping. The obvious one-line 'VARIANT': 'variant' would have failed one layer later: the variant popovers are feature-owned (tks.vsw_<tier>_variant_popover) and declare a NARROWER prop set — the TAKE one acts on the active take with no take_index, and an undeclared kwarg is a TypeError inside bpy.ops. Extracted popover_idname() / popover_kwargs() as the one mapping (all six tiers for VARIANT; row coordinates sg_group_name / vlg_group_name renamed to the popovers' own group_name). Tests walk every tier, assert the id is registered in bpy.ops.tks and that the kwargs are a subset of the operator's RNA properties, plus a control that a product which EXISTS is never reported broken — confirming the row itself is no false positive (the tree can look healthy beside it because assignment_resolves lights the icon when ANY product in a multi-product token still resolves, by design). Tests: dev/tests/test_broken_variant_replace.py (3). Troubleshooting: doc/troubleshooting/broken_variant_replace_dispatch.md. Commit fdfe4fca. Superseded the same day — see Fixed 90: with the dispatch wired, picking still changed nothing, and the right answer was to drop Replace for VARIANT entirely.

    125. 🟢 Variant rows offer Clear only; warning chips stretch to their buttons (user ruling; user-facing log: Fixed 60 + 61). Two findings from one report. (a) Replace is meaningless for VARIANT. A pointer tier holds ONE value so its picker overwrites it and the row clears; the variant tier holds a SET and tks.vsw_*_variant_popover MERGES a pick, leaving the dead entry — the click read as dead. And nothing is ever LOST: properties._on_product_name_changed → repair_product_rename follows renames (including the tree's inline field, a direct RNA write reaching no operator) and repair_product_delete drops assignments on delete, so a dangling product name only arrives from OUTSIDE those flows (appended scene/layer, lost carrier World, script write) where Clear is the only honest fix. supports_replace() now lives in core/assignment_health.py beside _DATA_TYPES — core sits below both callers, so the drawing panel and the dispatch share one rule without a panels → operators import; popover_idname() returns '' for VARIANT and the row omits the button. (b) Chip stretch is now a shared rule. Every warning row is [chips] [buttons] and each panel carried its own factor (0.72 / 0.8 / 0.82); a proportional split reserves button space unconditionally, so a row with fewer buttons shows dead space that WIDENS with the panel (the gap the user marked). New _widgets.value_button_row(parent, buttons) sizes the cluster at buttons * BUTTON_UNIT (1.15 ui-units each) and gives the value area the remainder — applied to all eight row sites (broken assignments, cascade drift, camera-needed, rest drift, slot + action mismatch, preset changes, missing presets, variant conflicts) and the pattern for any future row. Tests: test_broken_variant_replace.py (4, incl. a recording-layout draw test asserting VARIANT draws Clear-only while a pointer type still draws Replace). Suite 2105 passed. Commit 82fb2702.

    126. 🟢 The before chip is width-stable in every warning row (user ruling; user-facing log: Fixed 62). Follow-up to Fixed 106: with the button cluster fixed, the before/after pair was still a proportional split(factor=…), so the LEFT chip's width moved with the row's button count and the panel width and the chip column read ragged. _widgets.diff_pair now gives the before area a fixed BEFORE_UNITS (6.0) and leaves the after area elastic — it absorbs whatever the buttons take and shrinks first, which is the ruling ("only the after can shrink"). The factor parameter is gone; the four callers that passed their own (broken assignments, variant conflicts, both preview-rename rows) drop it. Tests: dev/tests/test_warning_row_widgets.py (5) — PURE, loading the bpy-free _widgets by file path (house pattern from test_camera_link.py) with a recording FakeLayout: identical before width across rows with an after chip, without one and with long text; no fixed width on the after or value areas; cluster width tracks the button count. Suite 2115 passed (rebased onto the concurrent variant-switch session's cac7510d / 68be6a49, which independently fixed the store-resolution side of the same report). Commit 1cdefa39.

    127. 🟢 Native VL switches never applied the variant cascade (guard collision; user-facing log: Fixed 104). _on_vl_switched (features/variant_switch/__init__.py), the VL_SWITCH_POST_CASCADE subscriber behind every native switch, set the package-global _applying_cascade before calling apply_variant_cascade — whose _guarded() re-entrancy check reads THE SAME attribute and silently returned. Only the addon's own switch operator (direct engine call) worked, which masked the bug. Ownership rule now documented on the flag: only cascade_engine._guarded writes it; every other site reads. Also added VARIANT:switch tks_log coverage to the engine (guard skip, no products, no value, winner, per-product apply) — the total failure was invisible precisely because the engine only logged to the python console. Found via the VSE compatibility fixture (dev/experiments/build_vse_take_test.py). Regression test dev/tests/test_vsw_native_switch_guard.py; analysis in doc/troubleshooting/vsw_native_switch_guard_collision.md. Commits 96e71574, 02a9734a, 57bd0015. Confirmed in-app 2026-08-19.

    128. 🟢 Object.tks_action sync was dead — UnboundLocalError on bpy (user-facing log: Fixed 105). The update callback (core/vl_handlers.py::_on_obj_tks_action_update) carried an import bpy inside its clearing branch; a function-local import makes bpy local to the WHOLE nested function, so the earlier bpy.data.actions.get(...) raised on EVERY invocation. RNA swallows update-callback exceptions, so the marker string still stored (the cascade-clear exemption kept working) while the sync to animation_data.action/action_slot never ran — UI edits and scripted writes alike. Dropped the local import; the module-level bpy covers the function. Regression test dev/tests/test_obj_tks_action_manual_sync.py (hardened against suite-state pollution in ad8e9cb4); analysis in doc/troubleshooting/tks_action_unboundlocal_bpy_shadow.md. Commits bde9b1f1, ad8e9cb4. Confirmed in-app 2026-08-19.

    [0.7.11] - 2026-07-12¶

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Automatic View-Layer Preload can open the progress panel for you. New pref preload_auto_open_panel (BoolProperty, default False) in TKS_AutomationsPropsMixin (preferences/props/props_automations.py); EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 495→496. Drawn in preferences/draw_workflow.py as an indented sub-flag, shown only when preload_viewlayers_mode == 'AUTO'. Hook in core/vl_lifecycle.py (_deferred_load_apply, the AUTO start_preload() site): after start_preload(), if the pref is set AND is_preloading() (a preload actually started — start_preload no-ops when all layers are preloaded), set wm.tks_show_preload_panel = True. Mutual exclusivity (below) closes any other open warning panel.

    2. 🟢 The public wiki now mirrors the changelog, alongside the roadmap. The wiki CI (Takes-for-Blender-Wiki/.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml) gained a "Mirror changelogs from addon source" step that copies the cloned .addon-src/CHANGELOG.md → docs/changelog/index.md and CHANGELOG_DEV.md → docs/changelog/dev.md. Published 1:1, markers + legend intact — the wiki is the documented exception to the strip-markers rule, which still governs the shipped ZIP changelog + release-notes (see memory feedback-release-logs-no-verification-markers). Surfaced via a new What's New nav group in mkdocs.yml (Changelog · Changelog (Dev) · Roadmap), replacing the lone top-level Roadmap tab. Two follow-up fixes were needed to make mkdocs build --strict (fails on any unresolved link) pass on the mirrored dev page: (a) the copy step sed-rewrites the intro's sibling changelog link to the user page (index.md, same dir) and de-links any source-file (.py) reference to inline code; (b) dev/build/verify_wiki.py now skips any docs/changelog/ path in its string-drift scan, since a changelog names historical / renamed / removed identifiers by design. Same mirror pattern as the roadmap board: pure wiki-side adaptation, a push to the addon repo republishes both. 🟢 verified live — Changelog, Changelog (Dev), and Roadmap render under the What's New landing page, with correct breadcrumbs and version-only nav confirmed on the deployed wiki.

    3. 🟢 A token/value toggle in the Build Syntax popover switches the grid between token names and their live values. New WindowManager.tks_token_show_values (BoolProperty, SKIP_SAVE), toggle drawn left of the search box in token_builder.draw_builder_strip (icon flips SYNTAX_ON ↔ HIDE_OFF). panel._draw_builder_columns resolves token_example once per cell (reused for the existing dim cue) and, when the toggle is on, passes it as a display label override to _emit_token — falling back to the token name when a token has no value. The appended token is unchanged: clicking still inserts {token}, not the resolved value. Separators / path literals are excluded (they already show their value beside them). Test test_token_toggle_icons_are_valid (icon-enum validity). Commit b47373b.

    4. 🟢 Quick-insert tokens + Clear Last / Clear All in every token field's ▾ popover. Each field's ▾ popover (the naming-template rows and the Smart Output Directory / File Name rows) gained an "Insert Token" list of its top essential tokens — one click appends the bracketed token at the very end of the field — plus "Clear Last Token" (drops the last whole token via the shared parse_segments/remove_segment, never a single character) and "Clear All" (empties the field). The list is the field's valid tokens only, so a click can never produce an invalid-token status: naming rows rank essential_tokens_for_field(field) (preferences/naming.py, intersected with TOKENS_PER_TEMPLATE, date/time excluded, cap 5); output rows rank essential_tokens_for_filter('CONTEXT','RENDER_PATH') against the new shared ESSENTIAL_TOKEN_PRIORITY (features/smart_syntax/builder.py). Wired through one pair of target-aware operators in builder.py — tks.field_append_token (reads target, appends format_token_for(mode, token)) and tks.field_clear (action CLEAR_LAST / CLEAR_ALL) — both keyed by the same (target_kind, target_data, bracket_mode) param set the Build Syntax launcher already uses, so prefs/CURLY (naming) and scene/SMART (output) share the code; this replaced two short-lived naming-only operators (tks.append_naming_token / tks.edit_naming_field) authored earlier the same session, avoiding duplicate operators. _draw_field_actions (naming) and the new _draw_quickpick_and_clear helper (features/batch_render/panel.py) draw the rows; Reset to Default was regrouped to sit just above the two clear rows so all "undo my edits" actions are together. Tests: test_output_popover_quickpick.py (new, Dir/File popover wiring), essential_tokens_for_filter cases in test_token_builder.py, the quick-pick/clear cases in test_naming_validation.py, and updated sequence/divider expectations in test_row_action_menu.py. Full suite 634 passed, 1 skipped. Lives in the new features/smart_syntax/ package (see Changed entry 7). ✅ in-app verified.

    5. 🟢 A search bar above the Preferences tabs dims non-matching settings (Naming tab pilot). Blender's native settings search is C-level and never reaches an AddonPreferences.draw() body — there is no API to read the native filter text and it won't dim custom rows — so the dim-non-matches / keep-matches-highlighted behaviour is reimplemented in Python. New prefs_search StringProperty on TKS_MiscPropsMixin (preferences/props/props_misc.py) with options={'TEXTEDIT_UPDATE','SKIP_SAVE'} and no update= callback (live redraw per keystroke; typing never triggers autosave); added to persistence_io.UI_STATE_KEYS so the JSON persistence never serializes it; EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 481→482. Drawn above the tab-nav row in preferences/addon_prefs.py (prop(self,"prefs_search",icon='VIEWZOOM') + a conditional ✕ that runs the new tks.clear_pref_search INTERNAL op in preferences/ops_misc.py). Two pure decision functions (unit-tested in isolation): pref_matches(query, *texts) in preferences/addon_prefs_helpers.py (case-insensitive substring; empty query → True; None-safe) and naming_search_flags(query, title, fields, label_fn=naming_field_label) in preferences/draw_naming.py (returns (section_match, {field: active}); a title hit lights the whole section; empty query is neutral so manual expand state is respected). Wiring: draw_naming_template_row gained active=True (sets row.active), draw_collapsible_section gained force_expand=False/active=True (search reveals a matching section without disturbing the stored expand flag and dims a no-match header), _draw_naming_categories/draw_naming_tab thread the query from prefs.prefs_search. Scope: Naming tab only (the data-driven NAMING_TEMPLATE_CATEGORIES pilot); the bar is global but other tabs are inline draws that opt in later (roadmap phase 4), and cross-tab auto-jump is deliberately out of scope. Tests: dev/tests/test_prefs_search.py (9, all pure); adjacent persistence/naming/panel/UI/accordion groups 116 passed. Roadmap doc/roadmap/active/prefs-search.md. ✅ in-app verified.

    6. 🟢 A "Show Tip Boxes" switch hides the add-on's explanatory tip boxes addon-wide. New show_tip_boxes BoolProperty (default True, update=_autosave_preferences) on TKS_MiscPropsMixin (preferences/props/props_misc.py); EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 480→481. Persists like any pref — in none of the persistence_io exclude sets. Surfaced in the "Info Boxes" accordion under Preferences → Interface → Confirmations (draw_interface.py; expand flag expand_confirm_infoboxes in props_logging.py → +1 to EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT, see entry 8; added to the Interface>Confirmations ACCORDION_GROUPS tuple and the prefs_search.SEARCH_INDEX['UI']['CONFIRMATIONS'] section list). (Earlier draft lived under a dedicated Interface→Misc subtab; that subtab was removed and the toggles relocated into Confirmations.) Gating lives in the shared component: ui/styles.py::tip_boxes_enabled() does a defensive bpy.context.preferences.addons[ADDON_MODULE].preferences read needing only ADDON_MODULE, so ui.styles stays free of any preferences-package import (no circular dependency) and returns True when prefs are unreachable. wrapped_info_box(..., kind='tip') returns None and draws nothing when off. Tests: dev/tests/test_info_box.py. ✅ in-app verified.

    7. 🟢 A "Show Warning Details" switch hides the read-once explanation inside warning panels. New show_warning_details BoolProperty (default True, update=_autosave_preferences) on TKS_MiscPropsMixin; EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 482→483 (after prefs_search's 481→482). The component's old is_tip boolean became a kind string — 'tip' (gated by tip_boxes_enabled), 'warning' (gated by the new warning_details_enabled(), parallel defensive read), 'status' / 'info' (never gated). The N-panel naming-template consequence note (panels/navigation/warnings/naming_changes.py) moved to kind='warning' + the centralized INFOBOX_NAMING_TOKENS_WARNING (texts/infoboxes.py), so it hides while the warning headline + Fix buttons (drawn separately) stay. Drawn in the same Info Boxes accordion next to Show Tip Boxes.

    8. 🟢 An ✕ on each tip / warning box hides that whole category, after a confirmation; and every box now carries a mandatory header. Header row in wrapped_info_box (ui/styles.py) gained a ✕ for kind in ('tip','warning') → tks.dismiss_info_boxes (preferences/ops_misc.py, INTERNAL, kind StringProperty). Its invoke() uses the plain wm.invoke_confirm(self, event) so the popup appears at the mouse pointer like the add-on's other confirmations (the rich title=/message= variant renders a centered dialog); execute() flips show_tip_boxes / show_warning_details off (the prop update= autosaves) + signal_redraw(). status/info boxes draw no ✕ (no pref to gate to). No new property. Separately, every box now has a header (no headerless path): default word per kind (_DEFAULT_HEADERS = Tip/Warning/Status/Info), title= overrides, title="" falls back to the default. The Info Boxes accordion's expand_confirm_infoboxes flag (props_logging.py, default True) accounts for EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 483→484. Tests: dev/tests/test_info_box.py (15 — kind gating × mandatory header × dismiss-button-present-per-kind).

    9. 🟢 The Build Syntax sheet offers Blender's own filepath tokens on render-path fields. Blender 5.1 resolves its own filepath template tokens in render-output + File Output paths, so the token grid now includes all 13: {scene} {camera} {fps} {resolution_x} {resolution_y} {blend_name} {blend_dir} {blend_name_lib} {blend_dir_lib} {node_name} plus #### (frame) and // / ../ (path). New engine data BLENDER_NATIVE_TOKENS + blender_native_by_category; WM toggle tks_token_show_blender_defaults (default True). Natives scatter into their matching categories, each trailed by the Blender logo (a native {scene} 🔵 sits beside its add-on twin [scene]), inserted LITERALLY in Blender's {…}/####/// syntax, never the add-on bracket style. Shown only on the render-path surface (not naming templates). Bracket-sync now reserves curly {…} — convert_to_current_style never rewrites a {token}, so inserting a native on a SQUARE-style field no longer triggers the red Sync-Brackets correction. {blend_name_lib}/{blend_dir_lib} became real registry tokens (resolve like blend_name/blend_dir, no linked-library context in a render path), leaving BLENDER_NATIVE_TOKENS = just the three frame/path literals. Category sort counts only add-on/separator cells, so toggling natives changes a category's height but never its position; the marker trails the token and the dimmed per-native explanation label was dropped (duplicated the hover tooltip). Commits 8d56686, 6b0e11e, 8af3790, be56a7a, a5b1846, a99885b, 5df302e.
