Sub-tab labels later reworked by a parallel session in commit da2189e (Settings→"Logging", Misc→"Utilities"); enum ids stayed 'GENERAL'/'MISC'. Commits 6fcece7, da2189e.

    50. 🟢 While a take is Still, the timeline scrub bar can't move the playhead — the native playhead lock rides the Still clamp. _apply_playhead_lock (features/still_mode/engine.py) forces scene.lock_frame_selection_to_range = True only for a single-frame clamp (start == end); a defined Animate range and restore_scene hand back the user's own value, snapshotted into the new Scene.tks_still_saved_lock_frame (properties.py) alongside the frame range, so in-place re-clamps (Still ↔ custom Animate range) track it too. Defense-in-depth for Fixed 26 — with the playhead unable to leave [0,0], a scrub on the Still scene can't even start the crash sequence — and it delivers the "inert scrubber" UX (a real gray-out of the native scrub bar has no addon hook). Tests: 4 pure lock-lifecycle tests in dev/tests/test_still_mode.py. Commit 87297e5.

    51. 🟢 The category icon picker opens on the tab of the icon the category currently uses, and its "Current" row carries a one-click copy of the icon's identifier. New pure icon_group_of(ids, icon, min_group=3) in features/smart_syntax/custom_tokens.py maps an icon to its categorize_icons header — headers double as the sheet's active_group enum identifiers, so TKS_OT_PickCategoryIcon.invoke (features/smart_syntax/registry.py) presets active_group from the category's current icon, falling back to _first_icon_group for unknown/stale ids (the unset default PLUGIN correctly deep-links to "Others", where it lives). The copy button reuses the existing tks.copy_icon_name (icon COPYDOWN, emboss=False) on _draw_icon_sheet_body's Current row, so a header copy also feeds the Recent tab exactly like a click in the browse-only sheet. The browse sheet (tks.view_icon_sheet) keeps its Recent-first open. Tests: 5 pure icon_group_of tests in dev/tests/test_custom_tokens.py. Roadmap: active/token-icon-sheet-ux.md. Commit 98a0248.

    52. 🟢 Internal: architecture-debt ratchet added to the test suite, with pure/bpy/slow pytest markers — no behavior change. Phase 0 of the decoupling plan (GitHub/.claude/plans/takes-decoupling.md). New dev/tests/test_architecture.py bootstraps the sibling blender-addon-auditor's ARCH-01..05 classifiers over the addon package (locates the auditor by walking up from the test file so worktree runs resolve; skips cleanly when the checkout is absent), applies the frozen grandfather baseline arch_baselines/takes_for_blender.json, and fails on ANY new non-baselined violation. A guard-the-guard test proves the classifiers actually run over the tree (the whole debt surfaces when no baseline is applied), so a green gate means "no new debt", never "the check silently no-oped". pytest markers pure/bpy/slow registered in pytest.ini; the autouse fresh_scene reset is scoped OFF for @pytest.mark.pure tests — opt-out on pure rather than opt-in on bpy, so every existing unmarked bpy test keeps its read_homefile reset — letting plain-Python checks run under bare pytest (pytest -m pure) with no Blender in the interpreter. Commit 8fceea2.

    53. 🟢 Internal: the take-switching core no longer imports panels or features — it announces events and queries the provider registry — no behavior change, fast sweep unregressed. Phase 1 of the decoupling plan, three tranches. (1) Nav-warning + inspector cache flushes became NAV_WARNINGS_INVALIDATE / INSPECTOR_CACHE_INVALIDATE emissions on core/event_bus.py; panels/navigation / panels/inspector self-subscribe invalidate_nav_warnings / mark_inspector_dirty at register time (12 upward core→panels imports removed, all fire-and-forget — commit d7bd6db). (2) The sweep-only post-undo profiler payload is emitted as PROFILER_FEED (navigation subscribes and owns its SWEEP_ONLY_PHASES constant); new core/providers.py — register_provider / get_provider / query / clear, the pull-side inversion companion to event_bus, torn down alongside it — lets the inspector register its _pending_fresh_actions queue as the inspector_fresh_actions capability instead of core importing panel privates (killed an ARCH-01 and an ARCH-03 edge — commit a75650f). (3) The last ~23 core→feature return-value sites inverted onto the registry, each feature registering at enable time: rest_state (get_rest_action, rest_mode_action_name, is_rest_mode, get_rest_drifts, find_slot_collisions, the slot-snap trio, an arm_suppress mirror-suppress setter replacing external pokes at _suppress_until, invalidate_cascade_action_cache, rest-cache ensure/build/invalidate), render_presets (last_applied_preset, is_preset_dirty, find_missing_presets), still_mode (apply_still / apply_switch_snap / reconcile_sync bundle), navigation (get_slot_mismatches, formerly a private cross-package import — commit b5fcd8d). Hot paths (vl_switch_fast, the cascade-clear loop) hoist provider refs into locals once at setup — no query() in any inner loop; every site keeps its original try/except and a matching default so a torn-down / not-yet-loaded feature degrades exactly as the old ImportError skip did. Fast sweep UNREGRESSED: apply_vl_switch_unified clear-all warm p50 2.68 ms / cold p50 5.38 ms (main baseline 2.90 / 5.75; gate 8.98 ms). Seam tests: dev/tests/test_arch_events.py (event constants pure; emit-reproduces-side-effect + provider seam, bpy). Suite 1241 passed / 1 pre-existing skip. ARCH baseline re-frozen 207 → 193 keys (auditor commit 1f3a847) — the ratchet now holds the shrunk debt. ✅ in-app verified (VL switching, cascade, undo/redo, rest & still switches, preset warnings).

    54. 🟢 Internal: cache invalidation routed through a leaf registry — writers stop importing panel draw caches upward — no behavior change. Phase 2 of the decoupling plan. New utils/cache_registry.py (register_cache / unregister_cache / invalidate / invalidate_all / clear): each cache owner registers its invalidator under a topic at register time — navigation "nav_warnings" (invalidate_nav_warnings), inspector "inspector" (mark_inspector_dirty), context panel "vl_cascade" (invalidate_vl_cascade_cache), rest_state "rest_state" (cache.invalidate_all) — and 29 writer sites across 17 files (render_presets ×5 files, rest_state, bookmarks, variant_switch, operators/inspector ×8, operators/cascade ×3, operators/ui ×2, ops_slots_rename, ops_rule_logic, properties/_groups_shared, properties/tag_library, panels/context/properties, panels/inspector ×2) call invalidate("<topic>") on the leaf utils module instead of importing the owning panel upward. Registry semantics: idempotent registration, per-invalidator crash isolation (a broken cache never sinks the writer that announced a change), unknown topic = silent no-op (owner not yet registered → stale-cache degradation, matching the old except ImportError: pass behavior); clear() torn down in core/vl_handlers.py beside event_bus.clear() / providers.clear(). Division of labour vs the bus: event_bus = push notification with semantics, cache_registry = dumb pull-side invalidation fan-out — a writer uses one per concern. Tests: 9 pure registry tests + 4 bpy topic-wiring seam tests + a textual guard that the upward imports never regrow (dev/tests/test_cache_registry.py). Suite from main 1255 passed / 1 pre-existing skip. ARCH baseline re-frozen 193 → 185 keys, 0 new violations (auditor 9f113e2). Freeze gotcha for the record: --arch-freeze-baseline without AUDITOR_SCAN_ROOT scans zero files and writes an EMPTY baseline — always point it at the addon repo. Commit fe40bd4. ✅ in-app verified.

    55. 🟢 Internal: three large code files reorganized into smaller focused modules — no behavior change. File-split refactor of the size-audit top three (worktree branch refactor/file-splits, commit 2c92709, pure moves — no logic edits): (a) features/smart_syntax/builder.py 1142→697 — pure pattern logic (parse/join/move/remove/append/filter/format, naming_valid_tokens, tokens_for_filter, ESSENTIAL_TOKEN_PRIORITY) moved to new segments.py and re-exported from builder (explicit # noqa: F401 block), so every caller and headless test keeps its builder. import path; the 8 Token Builder sub-operators + 2 field ▾ operators moved into the feature's existing operators.py (one classes tuple — REG-01 literal-loop friendly); builder keeps TOKEN_CATEGORY_MODEL/categorized_tokens, target IO (_read_target/_write_target/_resolve_target_default/_tag_redraw_all — still imported by tests and batch_render/path_mode.py) and draw_builder_strip; builder.register() removed (no classes left), smart_syntax __init__ and the root reload list updated (features.smart_syntax.segments added before builder). (b) features/smart_syntax/registry.py 906→628 — the searchable icon sheet became new icon_picker.py: _icon_enum_items cache, retained _icon_group_enum_items (+ RECENT_GROUP_ID, recent-tab helpers), _draw_icon_grid/_draw_icon_subgroups/_draw_icon_sheet_body, TKS_OT_PickCategoryIcon/TKS_OT_CopyIconName/TKS_OT_ViewIconSheet, and the unassigned icon-sheet hotkey keymap (identity-only teardown preserved); _prefs moved with it so the dependency stays one-way (registry → icon_picker, no cycle — registry re-imports _prefs/_icon_enum_items); TKS_OT_SetCategoryIcon stays in registry with the custom-token data it mutates; icon_picker.register() runs before registry.register(); preferences/draw_debug.py comment + test_corr07_polls.py path + test_icon_sheet_hotkey.py import repointed. (c) ui/styles.py 914→579 — preset_row + preset_selector_row (the ~350-line render-preset widget family) moved to new ui/preset_rows.py and re-exported from styles, so all ~30 styles.preset_row(...) call sites (render_presets panels, cascade level popovers, inspector, globals, channels) are untouched; ui/__init__ imports the new module. Also utils/manual_map.py now opens with a GENERATED DATA — DO NOT SPLIT/MOVE header (the MANUAL_MAP table is auto-written by dev/scripts/apply_wire_assignments.py, one row per wired control; it must stay in the shipped package because register() hooks bpy.utils.register_manual_map). Tests: test_field_ops_registered_in_builder → test_field_ops_registered_in_operators and test_builder_reset_op_registered now assert against operators.classes (the only 2 failures the split caused). Suite from main: 1279 passed / 0 failed (worktree run used the documented --ignore for the 4 auditor-engine tests; the full set ran green post-merge). Also in this window (test-infra, no shipped code): test_node_target_round_trip_directory (dev/tests/test_token_builder.py) stopped skipping — Blender 5.1's explicit-assignment compositor leaves a fresh headless scene with no compositing_node_group and use_nodes no longer auto-creates a legacy node_tree, so the test now creates + assigns its own CompositorNodeTree group (cleaning it up after) and only skips where neither API can produce a tree; suite skip count 1→0. Commit 9503136.

    56. 🟢 Camera Visibility Automation caches the per-scene camera list instead of scanning scene.objects every switch. apply_camera_visibility (core/cascade.py) scanned all of scene.objects on every VL switch to find cameras, so switches slowed as a file accumulated cameras/objects — only with the automation on. New per-scene cache _camera_vis_cache = {scene_name: (object_count, (camera_name, …))}; the O(objects) scan reruns only when len(scene.objects) changed or a cached name no longer resolves to an in-scene camera (add / remove / rename / unlink — a same-count swap is still caught by the name check), otherwise the cached list is reused (O(cameras)). Invalidation policy is a pure, RED-first unit-tested core core/camera_vis_cache.py::camera_cache_valid (5 tests, dev/tests/test_camera_vis_cache.py). The cache lives behind the auto_camera_visibility early-return so the feature-off path stays zero-cost; names only, never object refs (stale-pointer ban). Also surfaced in the switch profiler (Added 26) so the fired/skip state + time are observable. Confirmed working in-app with the automation on. Troubleshooting doc/troubleshooting/camera_visibility_switch_slowdown.md. Commit 1047563.

    Fixed¶

    1. 🟢 Clearing all keyframes at the current frame now affects only the scene you're working in. PERF-03 review of the 12 bpy.data.objects for-loops surfaced one genuine over-reach: the keyframe-clear operator's use_all_targets branch (operators/inspector/ops_keyframes.py) built its global targets from context.scene (scene + scene.world + node trees) but then iterated bpy.data.objects for the per-object targets — so a "remove all keys at current frame" wiped keys on objects in every scene, inconsistent with its own scene-scoped Scene/World targets. Scoped the object walk to scene.objects. Strictly narrows the blast radius (can only clear ≤ what it did before); aligns the object scope with the already-scene-scoped global targets.

    2. 🟢 The View-Layer Preload panel no longer gets stuck open after a preload finishes. The nav-bar toggle renders only while _preload_show = is_preloading() or cold_count() > 0 (panels/navigation/panel.py), but the panel BODY drew on tks_show_preload_panel alone — so when a run completed (not preloading, 0 cold) the toggle vanished while the body kept drawing, stranding it open. Two-part fix: (a) the body draw is now gated on the same is_preloading() or cold_count() > 0 condition, so it auto-hides when there's nothing to show; (b) at natural queue-drain completion in core/vl_preload.py::_preload_tick, if cold_count() == 0, reset wm.tks_show_preload_panel = False so next time a layer goes cold the (red) badge re-appears closed rather than the panel silently re-opening. The toggle's update callback no-ops on a False write (and tks_show_preload_panel isn't self-mutually-exclusive on turn-off). See doc/troubleshooting/preload_panel_stuck_open.md.

    3. 🟢 A view layer visited by an interactive switch reverted to COLD in the preload panel. _preloaded_this_session had only two writers — reset_preload_state() and _preload_tick — and the tick excludes the active layer (pair == active_pair → continue). So nothing recorded a layer preloaded by switching, and the layer switched away from fell through ACTIVE→PRELOADED→PENDING to COLD despite its depsgraph still being cached. Fix: new vl_preload.mark_preloaded(scene, vl) (idempotent), called from core/vl_switch_fast.py::apply_vl_switch_unified — the single sweep every path funnels through (interactive / load-apply / batch / preloader), always for the layer being built. Deferred import (vl_preload imports vl_switch_fast → top-level would be circular). The load-apply records the initial active layer; each switch records the to-layer; the active-first check keeps the current layer showing ACTIVE. Tests: test_mark_preloaded_* in dev/tests/test_vl_preload.py. See doc/troubleshooting/preload_visited_layer_shows_cold.md.

    4. 🟢 The public roadmap is now a live board that keeps itself up to date, with a clearer layout. Source of truth stays in doc/roadmap/{ideas,active,done} (status = folder; _dev/ private). dev/scripts/build_wiki_roadmap.py rewritten: emits three Markdown tables (Feature · Meta · What) + per-feature pages; parse_meta now also reads the required **Size:** token; board_table collapses Theme/Area/Size into one Meta column of Material icons with { title= } tooltips, the feature title is the page link (no Link column), the size dot is :material-circle:{ .sz-* }; wrap_phases wraps ## Phases in a .phases div so CSS marks non-task <li> with an ⓘ glyph; board_blurb trims summaries; intro admonitions dropped; new --addon-root so the wiki CI runs it against the cloned .addon-src. .github/workflows/notify-wiki.yml now also triggers on doc/roadmap/** + the generator. doc/ROADMAP.md demoted to a pointer; every feature file gained a **Size:** token; doc/roadmap/README.md, the roadmap skill, and the global Auto-Push rule updated to the one-push flow (chose Option A — generate-in-CI — over moving the human source into the wiki).

    5. 🟢 VL-switch rest-snap silently skipped objects whose rest slots changed since the cache was built. apply_vl_switch_unified STEP 3 read get_cached_rest_values() behind only a lazy if _rest_cache is None guard; invalidate_rest_cache() is called only on rest-keyframe write/revert, so when the Rest Action's slot set changed any other way (e.g. snapshotting newly-selected objects) the cache stayed incomplete and those objects fell out of ref_by_slot → SNAP=0. A full Blender restart rebuilt the cache and masked it (diagnosis: pre-restart sweeps all SNAP=0; post-restart KEY_HITS=94, SNAP 2–28). Fix in features/rest_state/cache.py: new ensure_rest_cache_fresh() + pure _rest_cache_needs_rebuild(cache_present, live_names, cached_names) rebuild when the live Rest Action slot-name set diverges from _rest_slot_targets (add/remove/rename), not only when None; shared _slot_cache_name() helper (hoisted _ID_PREFIXES). core/vl_switch_fast.py calls it in place of the lazy build. See doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_same_action_keyed_snap.md.

    6. 🟢 Same-action VL switch reset animated objects (notably Empties) to their Rest values. STEP 3's keyed-path exclusion matched the Rest action slot name against a keyed_paths set keyed by the cascade action slot name. Those names diverge for Empties — the Rest slot is {object} (ctrl_drawer_S_03) but STEP 2 renames the cascade slot to the template label {object}_EMPTY (ctrl_drawer_S_03_EMPTY) — so the keyed location path was not excluded and got snapped to rest; on a same-action switch the depsgraph never re-evaluates, so the bad snap stuck (laser trace: chosen_key='ctrl_drawer_S_03', name_in_ref=True label_in_ref=False, location[2] live=0.38379931 ref=0.37821015 willsnap=True, then stuck at the rest value). The manual path (get_rest_drifts/snap_single_to_rest) was always correct because it reads keyed paths from the target's actual assigned slot fcurves (identity). Fix in core/vl_switch_fast.py: build keyed_by_handle = {slot_handle: {(data_path, array_index)}} from the cascade action during the slot pre-scan; new pure helper keyed_paths_for_assigned_slot(keyed_by_handle, ad, target_action) matches by slot handle (rename/template-proof); STEP 3 skips those paths. Duplicate-slot theory ruled out (chosen_key and ref values were correct/stable). Tests: dev/tests/test_vl_switch_rest_snap.py (11 — handle exclusion incl. the Empty name-mismatch case + cache-freshness add/remove/rename); 152 adjacent rest/VL/slot tests still pass. See doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_same_action_keyed_snap.md.

    7. 🟢 Naming-template rows in Preferences showed a doubled dropdown chevron. Each row's ▾ actions popover (draw_naming_template_row in preferences/draw_naming.py) is layout.popover(panel_id, text="", icon='DOWNARROW_HLT'). In the Preferences/Add-ons editor Blender draws a popover button's own native disclosure chevron whenever the button has spare width, so the explicit DOWNARROW_HLT icon (dim, left) and the native chevron (bright, right) both rendered — width-gated (it vanished as the window shrank and the button lost slack). The Properties editor (Smart Output popovers) doesn't add the extra chevron, so the byte-identical call is single there: an editor-surface behaviour, not the popover call/panel/layout. Ruled out (all confirmed not the cause): the compact scale_y on Slots-Object-Data, removing the icon (→ bare wide chevron), dropping align=True from the label/field split, changing the generated panels' bl_space_type/bl_region_type to 'PROPERTIES'/'HEADER' (user: "no change"), and restructuring to the Smart-Output flat-row layout (still doubled). Fix: pin the ▾ to a fixed icon-width cell so the editor can't give it spare width — pop = input_row.row(align=True); pop.ui_units_x = 0.8; pop.popover(...) — single clean ▾ at any window width. Diagnosed with a throwaway GUI-Blender screenshot probe (open real prefs → maximize → screenshot → zoom the button column), since the bug is invisible to headless tests. See doc/troubleshooting/naming_template_popover_double_chevron.md.

    8. 🟢 The File Name preview now resolves even when the Directory is invalid; a bad directory no longer collapses the Output panel. Root cause: the directory preview's else branch (taken only when the directory is valid) did a LOCAL from ..smart_syntax.engine import SmartSyntaxEngine, which makes the name local to the whole draw_output_panel_prepend function. When the directory was invalid that else was skipped, the local was never assigned, and the File Name preview's later use of SmartSyntaxEngine raised UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'SmartSyntaxEngine' → its try/except fell back to the raw, unresolved pattern ([view_layer]_####.[file_format]). Invisible headless (the bug is in panel-draw scope, not the resolver). Fix: drop the shadowing local imports (it's already imported at module scope). Found only via a diagnostic that surfaced the caught exception text in the preview. Several real but non-causal defensive fixes were made along the way (each made the failure degrade more gently, which is why the symptom kept moving): resolve_token/resolve_path now except Exception per-token (a cluster raising a non-(RuntimeError, AttributeError, KeyError) type no longer bubbles out and blanks the whole path — degrades just that token to [token]); the #### frame pass prefers the PASSED scene over bpy.context.scene and is guarded separately so a frame error can't discard token resolution; .alert moved from the directory preview box() to an inner row() (setting alert on a box() corrupted draw state and silently dropped the next box — the File Name preview); and the Output override wraps the prepend in try/except so a bad path can't drop the native Saving/image-settings section. Commits 07e66ea (the fix), ef32b48, dda7952, e99ddcf, 785bd5c. See doc/troubleshooting/smart_output_invalid_dir_filename_unbound.md. ✅ in-app verified.

    9. 🟢 Reset / Clear actions in the Build Syntax popover repaint the field, chips and preview immediately. Clicking Reset / Clear Last / Clear All changed wm.tks_token_builder but the keep-open popup only updated after a mouse move — Blender doesn't auto-redraw a floating keep-open popup when a child popover closes. The Clear and Reset operators now tag every editor for redraw so the popup repaints instantly (the final real Menu form also closes cleanly, repainting on close). Commit 8c43622. ✅ in-app verified.

    11. 🟢 The Take Name naming template kept reverting to an invalid value on fresh starts after a headless test-suite run (prefs autosave leak). Tests in dev/tests/test_token_builder.py pointed the Token Builder's WM target at the REAL naming_take_template pref; the live write-through (features/smart_syntax/properties.py::_builder_to_target) pushed fixtures (junk{scene} → [sep][hostname] → [scene][sep][take], last write wins) into AddonPreferences, and update=_autosave_preferences full-dumped the config over the developer's real user_preferences.json.     12. 🟢 Calibrating render times no longer produces multi-minute estimates for takes that actually render in seconds. User-reported: 2 of 7 takes (~10s real render) showed ~22-minute estimates after Calibrate; the header ETA summed to ~24m. Three stacked root causes: (1) structural — the old probe extrapolated on pixels × nominal samples, which is ~100× wrong under Cycles adaptive sampling (see Changed 17 for the resolution-only probe redesign); (2) guard blindness — the probe sanity check read sibling reality from the session-only SKIP_SAVE tks_last_render_time, which is empty right after every restart, so stored garbage probes passed unchecked into the per-row labels AND the frozen batch snapshot (fixed by history-backed _vl_reality_seconds + the mid-batch reguard_estimate rescue, Changed 16); (3) verification blocked — a full day of in-app checks silently ran stale code because the Blender 5.1 extension junction pointed at the paused custom-tokens worktree (%APPDATA%…\extensions\user_default\takes_for_blender → .worktrees\Takes-for-Blender-custom-tokens); repointed to the main checkout — always verify the junction target before an in-app session. See doc/troubleshooting/render_eta_probe_blowup.md. Commits cd9935d, 29daade. ✅ in-app verified.

    13. 🟢 A background preload no longer overwrites camera, world, or action choices you made by hand. The restore leg re-applied the active layer's cascade resolution (_apply_preload_cascade(saved…)), not the actual prior state — manual deviations were stomped once per tick, and a layer resolving no camera CLEARED scene.camera (core/cascade.py None-branch, ~:548) / scene.world under auto-clear (~:635). core/vl_preload.py now captures a names-only raw snapshot per touched scene on first touch (_capture_scene_snapshot: camera/world/compositing_node_group/use_nodes + per-target (action.name, slot.identifier) keyed (obj.name, label) via iter_anim_targets) and the restore leg writes it back verbatim with guarded writes (pure restore_writes — equal values write nothing ⇒ nothing dirtied ⇒ restore-leg evaluated_depsgraph_get() dropped; target-leg eval kept — it IS the preload). Active snapshot recaptures when the user switches pairs mid-run (snapshot_needs_recapture). Names-only invariant enforced by non_name_values (no ID refs — PointerProperty-ban analog). start_preload also swapped the stale _rest_cache is None guard for ensure_rest_cache_fresh() (from 2ed1c31) so preload can't bake an incomplete rest cache. 7 TDD pure-helper tests in dev/tests/test_vl_preload.py. See doc/roadmap/_dev/preload-viewport-integrity.md. Commit e30b9d9.
    14. 🟢 Scenes shown in a second window are no longer switched around by a background preload. Only the user's scene+layer was restored; other scenes kept the last-preloaded VL's camera/world/compositor/actions. Every touched scene is now snapshot-captured on first touch and guarded-restored every tick (_restore_scene_snapshot(target_scene) first, then the active scene so shared objects end on the active layer's assignments); cancel / process-disable / batch-interrupt / addon-disable paths run _restore_all_snapshots(). Commit e30b9d9.
    15. 🟢 The VL Switch Profiler now repaints fully on an undo/redo re-fire (was single-writer + stale header + blank skipped groups). The profiler tree (wm.tks_profiler_items) had exactly one writer — the switch operator's deferred cascade in operators/context/ops_crud_switch.py — so the post-undo re-fire (core/vl_lifecycle.py::_maybe_refire_cascade_snap), which runs apply_vl_switch_unified directly and discarded its (_perf, _stat), left the panel showing the previous operator switch. Three stacked fixes: (1) extracted the ~90-line inline tree build into panels/navigation/profiler_feed.py::rebuild_profiler_tree(wm, perf, sweep_perf, sweep_stat, target_action_name, rest_action_name, ran) — ran (OPERATOR_PHASES vs SWEEP_ONLY_PHASES) marks phases the caller didn't execute as SKIPPED; the operator calls it with full groups (byte-parity), the re-fire with sweep-only (WM props aren't undo-tracked, so the deferred-timer write can't desync the undo stack — same pattern as the tks_cascade_step_* icons the sweep already sets there). (2) The header reads full_ms = tks_cascade_time_total + tks_cascade_time_eval, but tks_cascade_time_eval was written only by the operator, so a sweep-only rebuild left the prior switch's (dominant) eval time frozen; the helper now owns that prop (from perf['blender_eval'], 0.0 when absent) and the re-fire measures + times view_layer.update() when the profiler/cascade-steps panel is open (opt-in, safe in the deferred timer — the warm-up timer evals there too). Redraw switched to signal_redraw_deferred() because the profiler is a template_list and a synchronous tag_redraw from a timer skips the list's layout re-eval until a mouse move. (3) A SKIPPED group header rendered its timing cell blank (_draw_group only printed a time for exec_ms >= 0), reading as "not calculated"; extracted panels/navigation/monitors_profiler.py::group_timing_display(exec_ms, status) → dimmed "skipped" label + greyed header. Re-running overrides/finalize on undo is intentionally NOT done — apply_overrides() mutates materials/objects and fights Blender's native undo restore — so skipped is the correct state, now legible. Tests: dev/tests/test_profiler_feed.py (8), dev/tests/test_profiler_display.py (3), all red-first. Commits 821f266, 2b6569b, 0d92ea5. See doc/troubleshooting/profiler_stale_on_undo.md. ✅ in-app verified.
    16. 🟢 The public wiki deploys again on every push — two independent pipeline failures fixed. Added an id-shape fallback (operator_shaped_idname: a literal dotted-lowercase bl_idname is unambiguously an operator) + same-file bl_label/bl_description inheritance mirroring Blender's runtime; pinned by dev/tests/test_manifest_extractor.py. (2) dev/scripts/build_wiki_roadmap.py mirrored card prose verbatim, so the preload-viewport-integrity card's ../done/vl-preload.md + ../_dev/preload-viewport-integrity.md links 404'd on the flat published board and failed mkdocs build --strict. New neutralize_relative_links() rewrites cross-card links to the published flat sibling when the slug is on the board and demotes the rest (typically _dev/ companions, excluded before the slug check to avoid self-links) to inline code — same guard the changelog mirror applies to .py links.     17. 🟢 Same-action VL switch left a nudged keyed object at the nudge. Root cause (user-pinpointed via the Watchlist pipeline: "the snap is not firing between the same actions"): the fast sweep's STEP 2 writes ad.action = target_action only when the action CHANGES; that assignment write is what tags the target for animation re-evaluation, so a same-action switch performed no write, no re-eval happened, and a user-nudged keyed channel kept its nudge (different-action switches restore as a side effect of the write). STEP 3's rest snap can't cover it: it excludes every path the cascade action animates — and when the cascade action IS the rest action, that excludes everything. Fix: in the sweep's no-write branch, target.update_tag(refresh={'TIME'}) forces the same re-evaluation an action change causes; sweep summary log gains RETAG=N. Mechanism verified headless; confirmed in-app 2026-07-08. Works with the Value Lock off too. core/vl_switch_fast.py, commit ccac6d1. See doc/troubleshooting/vl_switch_same_action_no_reeval.md.

Fix: symmetric kill-switches on both channels (preferences/persistence_io.py load_saved_preferences, core/vl_lifecycle.py deferred call site), mirroring the _autosave_preferences guard; direct monkeypatched load_project_preferences() calls in test_prefs_persistence.py stay live. Regression guard dev/tests/test_prefs_load_isolation.py (red-first: sentinel → ''). Suite 919 passed / 0 failed. See doc/troubleshooting/order_dependent_preset_test_failures.md. Commit 8332bff.
    19. 🟢 Deleting/unlinking the Rest State action while the mode is on now AUTO-EXITS cleanly (mode off, autokey + Value Lock restored, button grays); exiting the mode always restores both. Two-part follow-up to Added 21, with a UX revision superseding an interim red click-to-exit button (commit fd93fc3) via user-chosen auto-exit. (1) Auto-exit reconciler. No crash was ever possible — get_rest_action() is bpy.data.actions.get(name) (None on delete) and every rest read is None-guarded — but the mode went "zombie": flag on, autokey paused, resolver falling through to the real tree action. A deletion is first observed in draw / property-update contexts (mutation ban), so the fix is a one-shot timer: schedule_orphan_reconcile() (idempotent, gated on rest_mode_broken()) registers _reconcile_orphaned_rest_mode, which runs in a safe context and calls the shared deactivate_rest_mode(context, restore_lock=True) — set_rest_mode(False) + restore_autokey + _reapply_active_vl (reassigns the real tree actions) + Value-Lock restore. The reconciler defers (returns 0.15) while TKS_VL_STATE.addon_is_mutating/is_undoing/is_redoing, never throws into the timer loop, and is unregistered on addon unregister. Scheduled from two sites: the toggle's poll (per-redraw) on a mode-on orphan, and _on_rest_action_update (properties.py) for popover unlink/change. TKS_OT_RestModeToggle.poll now grays whenever not has_rest_action() (mode on OR off) — the prior "keep enabled to exit when broken" is obsolete since the reconciler auto-exits; the interim red alert= row and dynamic description() broken branch were removed. deactivate_rest_mode writes state DIRECTLY (not via the now-grayed toggle) so the auto-exit can't be blocked by its own poll. (2) Symmetric Value-Lock restore (unchanged from fd93fc3): entering sets Scene.tks_rest_mode_lock_was_on before releasing the lock; exit re-enables it after restore_autokey + reapply; recursion avoided via restore_lock: BoolProperty(default=True, SKIP_SAVE) (the Value-Lock reverse exclusion passes restore_lock=False). Ordering: restore_autokey (→ ON) then re-enable lock (→ re-pauses) reproduces the pre-mode state. Tests: test_rest_mode.py (pure — poll grays-always truth table, orphan-poll schedules reconcile, schedule idempotency + orphan-only, deactivate/schedule wiring, restore_lock+memory, reverse restore_lock=False) and test_rest_mode_sweep.py (registered end-to-end, @_needs_followup now also gates on deactivate_rest_mode: auto-exit-on-delete via the shared helper + lock round-trip). Junction serves MAIN → registered tests validate post-merge. Design record doc/roadmap/_dev/rest-state-mode.md. Worktree full suite 1027 passed / 0 failed; post-merge registered gate 3/3. Commits fd93fc3, f59a319.

    21. 🟢 While a preload run is live, working in the viewport no longer stutters between layer builds, and a stray action can no longer land on your current take mid-run.     26. 🟢 Dragging the timeline playhead while a Still take was active hard-crashed Blender (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION @0x28). Root cause (source-confirmed in the 5.1 release branch): Screen.is_animation_playing is a GLOBAL getter over ED_screen_animation_playing, which counts screen->scrubbing — so a Timeline drag reads as "playback" with NO animtimer. The Still auto-stop then ran screen.animation_cancel, and 5.1's stop_playback() (screen_ops.cc) reads screen->animtimer->customdata — wmTimer.customdata sits at struct offset 0x28, the exact faulting address — with no null guard, so the op segfaulted even under the probe-proven temp_override(window, screen) (guarded upstream after 5.1). Three production crashes: 2026-07-10 19:43 (Eloise), 2026-07-12 00:10 + 08:38 (Basketballkorb). This CORRECTS the 2026-07-10 red-herring verdict — the playhead drag was never incidental; scrubbing is an independent, sufficient trigger. Fix (features/still_mode/handlers.py): _scrub_somewhere() (per-screen is_scrubbing across ALL windows — the C-side acts on the FIRST playing-or-scrubbing screen) consulted by the frame_change scheduler AND re-checked inside _stop_still_playback (a scrub can begin between scheduling and firing); _scrub_end_watch (0.1 s poll) snaps Still playheads home with plain frame_current writes once the scrub ends; both timers cleaned up in unregister_handlers. TDD: 2 predicate tests + a source-contract regression lock in dev/tests/test_still_mode.py; RED observed pre-implementation; suite 1212/0 post-merge. See doc/troubleshooting/still_mode_playback_cancel_crash.md (updated with the scrub mechanism). Commit 87297e5.

Two independent dim concerns wrote the same trow.active flag in panel.py::_draw_builder_columns: the search dim, then (after it) the "nothing to resolve here" hint — which only ever set False, so a token matching the search but holding no current value (empty {stamp_note}, node tokens with no File Output node, camera tokens with no camera) could never light up; in value mode its N/A compounded the "doesn't work" impression. Headless diagnostic (dev/experiments/diag_stamp_note_resolve.py) proved resolution itself was always correct (stamp_note → the Note text when set, '' when empty; only genuine absence → None). New pure token_row_active(search, matched, example=True) (features/smart_syntax/builder.py) decides the row once: an active search's MATCH owns the brightness; the resolvability hint applies only to the idle grid; separator/native rows omit example. Both dim sites in panel.py wired through it. TDD: 5 pure decision tests in dev/tests/test_token_builder.py (RED via missing import, GREEN 18 passed). Suite 1096/0 in the worktree, junction-repointed. See doc/troubleshooting/token_builder_search_dim_collision.md. Commit c658a76.

    28. 🟢 The Preferences Data tab crashed on every draw — the serialization package stopped re-exporting a publicized name. The ARCH-03 publicize sweep rewrote the call site serialization._get_project_presets_dir() → get_project_presets_dir(), but the features/render_presets/serialization/__init__.py package re-exports an EXPLICIT name list that still carried only the private spellings. Package-attribute access follows that list literally, unlike module-attribute access which follows renames automatically — so AttributeError: module 'serialization' has no attribute 'get_project_presets_dir' fired on every Preferences → Data draw tick. Neither py_compile nor the headless suite saw it (attribute resolution is lazy; the prefs Data draw is not test-exercised). The storage import block now re-exports the four public dir resolvers (get_addon_presets_dir, get_shared_presets_dir, get_local_presets_dir, get_project_presets_dir) beside the legacy private aliases. Regression test_serialization_package_exports_public_dir_api (dev/tests/test_feature_divorce.py) pins the export list; troubleshooting doc/troubleshooting/serialization_package_export_drift.md records the lesson (a name consumed as a PACKAGE attribute must be added to every __init__ export list on the path). This is the bug that motivated the auditor's REG-08 check. Commit ae5771c.
    29. 🟢 The cascade-overflow popover's VARIANT column raised AttributeError — six module attributes had moved. operators/misc/ops_cascade_overflow.py resolved global/sg/scene/vlg/vl/vl_version _has_variant off features/variant_switch/operators, which defines none of them — the re-export vanished in an earlier refactor, and lazy attribute resolution meant no import error, no compile error, and no headless coverage of that popover branch, so every VARIANT overflow query raised at runtime. Found by the new auditor check REG-08 (Module-Attribute Existence) on its first real-tree run. The import now binds core/variant_queries (the helpers' real home, downward-legal). Troubleshooting doc/troubleshooting/overflow_has_variant_attrs.md. Commit d202236.
    30. 🟢 Selecting a cascade camera raised AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'select_set' for any non-Scene tier. The Select button (tks.select_scene_camera) called cam.select_set(True) on whatever resolve_cascade returned — but every non-Scene camera tier (ViewLayer / VL-group / scene-group tks_camera, tks_global_camera) stores a NAME string, so any tks camera override made the button raise, and the surrounding except RuntimeError never caught it. features/render_presets/ops_select.py now normalizes name → bpy.data.objects.get() before use; a dangling name falls into the existing "No camera assigned in cascade" cancel. Every other CAMERA-resolve consumer already normalized — this op was the one that skipped it. Found by the auditor's HARN-09 operator exec-smoke. Regression dev/tests/test_select_scene_camera.py (3); troubleshooting doc/troubleshooting/select_camera_string_tier.md. Commit 16dcf2b.

    2. 🟢 The naming-template unlock gate removed — every template is editable directly. Removed the naming_templates_unlocked BoolProperty (props/props_naming.py; its bpy.props import slimmed to StringProperty only, since BoolProperty/EnumProperty were now unused) and the entire lock card + unlock toggle in preferences/draw_naming.py::draw_naming_tab. The temporary LOCKED/FREE category split (added the same session) was collapsed back into the single NAMING_TEMPLATE_CATEGORIES list (original order), which the tab now draws unconditionally; the orphaned 'naming_templates_unlocked' key was dropped from the draw_data_inspector session-state key filter. EXPECTED_PROP_COUNT 481→480. Rationale (verified at the source): naming templates are generators, not matchers — bindings are identity-based, so changing a template only affects newly created names and can never break an existing connection: cascade datablocks (actions/cameras/compositors, Rest Action) are tracked by name + UUID self-heal (bpy.data.<coll>.get(name) + tks_*_uuid repair), and action slots are paired to their targets by a UUID token (core/slot_tokens.py ensure_token/get_token, stored on the target and on the owning Action keyed by slot handle). detect_slot_renames compares a slot's name_display to the template's expected label only to offer a cosmetic rename — never to bind. So the unlock gate guarded nothing. ✅ in-app verified.

    Added¶

    1. 🟢 Absolute/relative path mode for the Smart Output directory — one-shot convert + A/R field badge. New features/batch_render/path_mode.py (pure logic + thin operator, mirrors token_builder.py). Pure: path_mode(s) (RELATIVE/ABSOLUTE/NEITHER by leading prefix only), is_absolute, to_absolute(s, blend_dir), to_relative(s, blend_dir). Whole-string conversion — tokens ([scene], ####) are inert path text and survive because only the ///drive prefix is rewritten, so no path↔token splitting is needed. to_relative normalizes os.path.relpath returning '.' (the .blend's own folder) to '', so blend-dir → // not //.; returns None on a Windows cross-drive ValueError. Operator tks.toggle_render_path_mode (REGISTER/UNDO/INTERNAL): reads scene.tks_render_directory, flips it via the pure fns using dirname(bpy.data.filepath), signal_redraw(); reports {'WARNING'} (clear wording) on unsaved file or cross-drive; state-aware description(). Registered after token_builder in batch_render/__init__. UI in panel.py: draw_output_panel_prepend badges the Directory field with EVENT_A (absolute) / EVENT_R (relative) glyphs set as the field's own prop(..., icon=…) — the house pattern from preferences/draw_data_storage.py::_draw_storage (plain prop when empty); TKS_PT_DirPatternActions adds a contextual Make Absolute/Relative item with the same letters. Tests: dev/tests/test_path_mode.py (14 — classification, conversion, cross-drive None, token survival, //↔abs round-trip incl. the //. regression, icon-enum validity, operator registered) + test_row_action_menu.py updated for the new contextual item. Repro-driven debugging (the real trigger was an unsaved .blend; // can't resolve without a save anchor) documented in doc/troubleshooting/path_mode_toggle_double_slash.md. A follow-up fix added path_mode._canonical() (applied in path_mode/to_absolute/to_relative) so a single leading \\ is read as the Blender-relative // — mirroring the renderer's exact rule in properties._get_expected_filepath — instead of as an absolute UNC path, which had made the badge disagree with what actually rendered. Full suite 475 passed headless. Follow-up: TKS_OT_ToggleRenderPathMode gained a poll() returning False when not bpy.data.filepath with cls.poll_message_set("Save the .blend first — '//' relative paths anchor to its location"), so the popover's Make Absolute/Relative item is grayed (with a reason) on an unsaved file instead of relying on the execute-time {'WARNING'} cancel.

Operators tks.preload_viewlayers / tks.cancel_preload_viewlayers / tks.preload_toggle_section (ops_crud_switch.py). The residual delay was diagnosed with a temporary ctx.view_layer.update() probe in _deferred_cascade → it's Blender depsgraph eval (cold ~1600 ms → preloaded ~110 ms → revisit ~50 ms), inherent to single-valued shared action assignment (preload holds every VL's topology but only the active VL's animated state). Full history in doc/roadmap/_dev/vl-preload.md. Suite 548 passed.

Auditor contract (blender-addon-auditor): info_05_naming._FEATURE_REGISTRY key reference→rest + home features/rest_state/, _PROP_INFIX_ALLOW reference→rest; info_04_manual_map DIR_TO_WIKI/AREA_LABELS keys → features/rest_state/"Rest State". naming_conventions.md §6 row updated; the now-inverted §7.4/§11 "rest_state typo" notes removed.

Docs/wiki: 10 doc files renamed (rest_state_persistence.md, set_rest_default.md, 8 troubleshooting); wiki ~12 label spots + the feature page "(formerly Reference State)" note. ~90 addon .py files, ~931 + phrase/final lines. 419/419 headless tests pass (3 runs); /stats health 9.9 (sole deduction a pre-existing render_presets/preset_health.py nesting finding, unrelated to this change).

    22. 🟢 Smart Output pattern-row action buttons collapsed into per-field popover panels — no behavior change. In features/batch_render/panel.py, the Directory row (Build / Browse / Sync / Reset = 4 buttons) and File Name row (Build / Sync / Reset = 3) each now end in a single row.popover("TKS_PT_<dir|file>_pattern_actions", text="", icon='DOWNARROW_HLT'). Two new INSTANCED popover panels (TKS_PT_DirPatternActions / TKS_PT_FilePatternActions, bl_space_type='PROPERTIES', bl_region_type='HEADER') hold the actions — same mechanism as the render-preset popovers (TKS_PT_render_presets_popover), chosen over layout.menu so the look matches the rest of the addon. Each item is drawn via a shared _popover_item() helper (emboss=False + alignment='LEFT' for a flat menu-row look) and re-emits the exact operator props the old inline icon buttons set; a separator(type='LINE') divides Reset from the rest. popover()/menu() can't pass per-row args, hence one panel per target field. New dev/tests/test_row_action_menu.py drives each Panel.draw through a fake layout asserting operator sequence, props, INSTANCED, flat, left-aligned, and the LINE divider; full suite green headless. Follow-up: Browse Folder was pulled back out of the Directory popover to an inline button left of the ▾ (draw_output_panel_prepend) — TKS_OT_BrowseDirectory.invoke does Shift+Click → open_path_in_explorer, and inline operator() buttons pass modifier state where popover menu items don't; the Directory popover is now Build / Sync / Make-Abs-or-Rel / Reset, and the sequence test was updated accordingly. Later: Sync Brackets was removed from both popovers (TKS_PT_DirPatternActions / TKS_PT_FilePatternActions now hold only Build / [path-mode] / Reset) and re-surfaced as a conditional red button beside each field — a new _sync_alert_button(parent, value, target, **props) helper draws an alert=True FILE_REFRESH operator only when SmartSyntaxEngine.needs_bracket_sync(value) is true, placed innermost (right after the field, before the always-on Browse/▾) so those icons never shift as it toggles. Applied to all pattern fields (scene Directory/File Name + node directory/file_name/slots); the node panel's always-on FILE_REFRESH sync buttons were replaced by the same conditional helper.

    23. 🟢 Smart Output bracket-style switcher relocated to Add-on Preferences; syntax-sheet button removed — no behavior change to resolution. smart_output_bracket_style prop moved from the Output panel header (draw_output_panel_prepend + the Node-editor TKS_PT_SmartOutput) into preferences/draw_workflow.py's "Render Output" accordion (below smart_output_apply_to_f12, PREFS_TITLE_GAP between them). The standalone tks.syntax_cheat_sheet_popover TEXT-icon button was dropped from both panel headers (still reached via each field's Build Pattern popover and the docked TKS_PT_SyntaxCheatSheet). The setting only affects Smart Output token brackets (used solely inside features/batch_render), not the naming system (naming_separator) — hence the Render Output home; the unused prefs fetch was removed from draw_output_panel_prepend.

    24. 🟢 Standard/Link/Compositor mode buttons moved beside the Smart Output toggle and gray out when off — no behavior change. The mode_row was merged onto the toggle's row (row.separator(factor=0.5) gap) with mode_row.enabled = scene.tks_smart_output_enabled, so it grays out rather than being hidden behind the early return (drawn before the return in both draw_output_panel_prepend and TKS_PT_SmartOutput). Design note: the toggles stay per-scene (Scene.tks_output_standard/_compositor/_linked) and were deliberately NOT moved to prefs — they're per-scene operational state, so a global pref would collapse independent per-scene modes to one shared value.

    25. 🟢 Separator tokens single-sourced; shared {token} resolver; glyph display. FIXED_SEPARATORS + new separator_display() moved to core/naming_utils (re-exported by features/batch_render/engine); _build_token_values now spreads **FIXED_SEPARATORS. _cleanup_separators() extracted from _generate_name_uncached and shared with new resolve_pattern(). ops_smart_output.TKS_OT_CopySyntax.description delegates to token_builder.token_example; preferences/draw_naming uses separator_display. (UI-facing effect: invisible separators render as ␣/∅.)

    26. 🟢 Build Pattern popover previews each token's value on hover and dims tokens that don't resolve in the current context. New shared resolver token_builder.token_example(raw, context) — single source for the hover tooltips (TKS_OT_BuilderAppend.description now returns only the Preview: <value> line, falling back to the token description; ops_smart_output.TKS_OT_CopySyntax.description delegates to it) and for grid dimming (panel._draw_builder_columns sets trow.active = False when it returns ''; separators are never dimmed). Resolution order: separators → separator_display; then the Smart engine (SmartSyntaxEngine.resolve_token, render-path semantics) preferring a real File Output node (active node, else scanned via handlers._get_compositor_trees(scene)) — node-data tokens (_NODE_TOKENS = {node,label,input,socket}) return '' with no real node instead of being faked by a stub _DummyNode; then core.naming_utils._build_token_values as fallback for naming-only tokens.

    27. Absence sentinels. A resolved value in ABSENCE_SENTINELS (new frozenset in engine_token_resolvers.py: None, Unsaved, NoAction, NoSlot, NoCamera, NoMarker, NoWorkspace, NoPreset, NoVariant, NoTag, NoCollection, NoPart, 0mm, f0) or a still-bracketed unresolved token ([token]) counts as empty → dimmed. The resolvers are untouched (those sentinels are still produced for real path/name output); only the preview/dimming layer treats them as "nothing".
    28. Latent Blender 5.1 fix. The node scan previously used scene.node_tree, which raises AttributeError on 5.1 (compositor moved to compositing_node_group) and was silently swallowed — the original CopySyntax example had the same bug, so node tokens never previewed. Now routed through _get_compositor_trees (5.0 node_tree ↔ 5.1 compositing_node_group).
